title: Unbelievable! Chi-Fi delivering overtime with these
text:
Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome

title: Audiophile quality at a budget price!
text:
I have two issues, and it is not with the IEM's themselves, but the company that sold them. First, the ones I purchased were originally returned. How do I know? Because whoever had them before me had worn them, and left ear wax on the silicone ear pieces. Luckily, they were not the size I wear so I made sure to wash all of the ones that came with the IEM's (included the dirty ones). And second, they went on sale two days after I bought them so I had to send an email to the seller to see if I can get the $10.00 off. UPDATE: 6/8/22 - Got the $10.00 discount!!

Other than those two things, they are excellent IEM's! If you look at the frequency response of these, and realized that they are tuned, they're great for someone in the mid 50's. As you get older, you notice that your hearing loses higher frequencies. Pretty much every frequency above 12kHz are gone. These are tuned perfectly for someone who has lost those frequencies, and these start dropping off after 10kHz. So if you are younger, adjust the treble if you need to.

How good are they? If you have ever heard Bruce Hornsby & The Range's song "Every Little Kiss," you can hear Bruce shift his weight on the bench while playing his Steinway at the beginning of the song.

So, if you love listening to music, and don't feel like forking hundreds of dollars for earbuds, these are the ones to buy. Oh, and the bass is excellent!!

title: Very good for the money.
text:
I grabbed these for quick field recordings with some zoom equipment. I wanted something smaller that wouldn't take up half my case when I was basically just checking to see that things weren't clipping anyway.

These DO NOT HAVE ACTIVE NOICE CANCELLING. I am so sick of that term getting confused with items that are noise isolating just by virtue of having a good fit. These do a great job of blocking sound, but if you are expecting noise cancellation you will be disappointed.

The manual is ridiculous. It looks like it was translated in google translator. Things don't make sense at all if you don't already know what the paragraph is probably talking about. Fortunately these are basically plug and play. You insert the wires (there are pictures showing how, so it doesn't matter how poorly translated it is) and off you go.

title: Great budget IEM
text:
So I'll ride the hype train on this one. These sound very good. They have excellent clarity. Imaging and separation is good, soundstage is... well fairly small. But for $50 these may be the best I've experienced.

In terms of audiophile quality, these do beat the Tinhifi T2's (also same price range); from the perspective of fidelity of sound. The Tinhifi T2 is a very enjoyable headphone - it is just 'rounded off' and more Harman tuned.

Pros:
Clarity and detail are great for this price range.
Imaging and separation are good for the price range.

Neutral:
Despite me saying these are more true to sound than the T2, these are V shaped. The low end is pronounced/punchy, and the upper end is pronounced. This can be good or bad depending on your taste.

Cons:
I am new to the audiophile hobby, so I couldn't point to an exact frequency range, but the treble definitely spikes at one or more frequency. This is largely eliminated by using foam tips. But these treble spikes can make this IEM fatiguing, especially with certain tracks, and especially when you stick with the stock silicone tips.

Overall:
Great IEM for the price, I do not regret buying them. Their quality is excellent. And I even joy the build quality on these. The cable that came with it is... okay... It's one of those clear plasticy rubbery jobs that feels like it should be on a pink set of a 5 year old girl's headphones. But they do the job.

title: Works great for electronic drums, but you'll NEED foam tips.

Not booming, thumping low end, but enough low end to not need to spend any more money on "better" IEM's. I used the foam tips for a while and that improved the sound and fit, but found the ZS10 Pro still didn't have as good of isolation as the AS10's. So, I got some Radians Custom Molded Earplugs and made custom fitted molds for the ZS10 Pros. Now the isolation is incredible, even good enough to use with acoustic drums. I also got the upgraded cable and could not be happier. No tangling at all. After 1 year, these still work perfectly and have never had any issues. None. If you want super-sub bass freq's, then these probably aren't for you. But if you want killer sound for under $50, these are it.

text:

As expected, this product is less comfortable and clearly uses cheaper materials and construction, but I can't really complain given the price. The sound quality is fine as far as I can tell. The battery life is decent but noticeably shorter than my previous headphones. Also, the low battery warning is a very annoying loud series of beeps that repeats periodically until you charge it. So if you just want to listen for 5 more minutes or get through the last couple of minutes of that video and then charge it, well too bad, because the beeps are going to annoy the **** out of you until you charge it. Also, the pictures in the instructions were not clear to me at all, and it took me a while to find the charging port (you have to tilt one of the earphones to reveal the port which is otherwise hidden behind the headband).

Also, unlike my previous headphones, this one does not work well with my tablet's media volume sync (when the headphones are turned on they always revert to a default volume, they don't remember the last volume used), so I had to turn sync off to avoid constantly having to recalibrate the volume of the headset relative to the tablet.

title: New Headline New Review...See the photos. Brittle plastic broke within a few weeks.
text:
Where do I go with this? I'm a fan of JBL/Harmon Kardon products as you'll see in my review. And I was a fan of these - especially at $30 - except they broke after only a few weeks. Luckily - even being outside the Amazon return window - Amazon is willing to refund. Now the question is do I try another pair of these???

I ran across these marked down to $30! I've been looking for a pair of reasonably decent bluetooth headphones. I own a pair of Harmon Kardon Sound Sticks on my Macpro workstation and have amazing sound taken care of. I just needed a decent pair of bluetooth headphones for occasional use.

At $30 these fit the bill! JBL quality at an amazing price. The sound? Well, definitely heavy on bass as indicated. I used my iTunes equalizer to drop a bit of bass and make mids and highs cleaner.

These are great entry-level bluetooth headphones. I can see at some point adding a more expensive and better sounding pair. And I'll probably stick with the Harmon/JBL brand.

EVEN NEWER INFO: I should have asked for a replacement because the price on these has increased. I decided to spend more money and purchase Audio-Technica ATH-AR3BTBK SonicFuel headphones ($89).

title: It doesn't turn. on
text: The JBL Tune 500BT turned on once. Only once, out of the box. After pairing it and using it with a one-year-old 4K Samsung 55" TV for about one hour, we turned it off and charged it. But the red light continuously stays on, indicating that it is continuously charging. (The light is supposed to turn off when fully charged.) We have tried charging it using a 2.4W plug-in to an outlet, for a full 24 hours, and also directly into my iMac for several hours, but the light stays red. After disconnecting it, the light turns off, but the headphones do NOT turn on. We have tried multiple suggested factory resets from You Tube, but none of them, work, because they don't turn on. HELP!!!

title: Better Than I Thought
text: I bought this hat thinking it was going to sound awful-to-tolerable & I'm happy to report I was 100% wrong!! I LOVE this hat!! It works great as a warm hat, but it's also awesome as a Bluetooth device. It was very easy to link with my iPhone, so I don't know who's struggling with the pairing—the unit says out loud when it's turned off & on, if it loses connection/is too far away from the paired device, & even this colorblind woman can see it blinks when it's on, pairing, charging, or off. I believe it does run a little small, but since my bean is smaller, it works fine for me & neither slides off my head nor squeezes it too tightly. My son (with a larger noggin) doesn't like the speakers/headphones pressing on his ears—they sit comfortably on mine. The buttons are easy to operate with a light glove or glove liner; I have not tried with a heavy glove. I do find that I keep pressing the "back" button instead of the "forward" button, but that may be simple training/mental programming on my part. I love that I can listen to wireless music outside while doing "chores" & not miss a phone call or TM. The mic is mildly affected by the wind, but then again, so is every other BT or wired mic. It was a little tricky to properly find & then seat the USB charging hookup the first time, but each time it's easier. I highly recommend this BT hat & will be buying other colors/styles. Now, if there were a baseball-style or workout version made from performance fabric I'd get that style for the summer <thumbs up!>

title: Good deal
text:
The sound quality was better than I expected for a product under $50. It may be because they fit so well but the background noise doesn’t seem to be heard through much at all. They were easy to pair with just the push of a button. They charge with a micro usb (included) which I like because it’s something I use for my Kindle so I’m not carrying separate chargers. It has a 2 button design so you click once for volume up or double click for skip. The other button you click for volume down or double click for rewind. I much prefer this method to other 2 button designs. I have other 2 button designs that are reversed and it constantly skips when I am trying to volume up. This is a much better design.

They are a nice size to easily fit in your pocket and are sweat proof. For under $30 this is quite a deal.

title: So Glad I Have These Headphones
text: Prior to this past year, I could count on one hand how many video calls I had ever made in my lifetime. Then work from home started and I've been on more video calls than I can remember. I generally didn't like using headphones because I found them so uncomfortable after a while, and especially had trouble with the ear bud types that plug into my ears. But being able to hear well was essential for my video calls, so I decided to try these PowerLocus Wireless Bluetooth Headphones. I'm so glad i did because they have been indispensable. They adjust well to my head and I can wear them comfortably over my ears for hours. The set up to get started took virtually no time at all. The controls on the headphones do take a little practice to get right, but after one or two days of use, I was good to go. I plug these headphones directly into my mic and they work great together. The sound quality is also very good, although my husband tried them and said he doesn't get as full of a bass sound when listening to music as he does with his set of studio headphones (which cost about 4x more than these). All the same, while wearing them, I can hear the other speakers clearly and still hear if my phone rings or if someone in the room is speaking to me. But having them on blocks out a great deal of extraneous, distracting, ambient noises. Overall, these PowerLocus Headphones work well, are comfortable, keep me focused, and are reasonably priced on Amazon. I'm so glad I have them.

title: Solid build quality but with a few quirks.
text:
I ordered the ‘adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - New’ for review as I am a sucker for wireless headphones. My initial thoughts right out of the box were that these are solidly built, lightweight and beautifully designed headphones. They look and feel "high end". I’ve now had these for nearly a month and feel that I am ready to share more.

First I would like to comment on the fact that these are touted as “Sport” headphones and my idea of “Sport” headphones are more of the "in-ear" earbuds, which fit much more securely and do better in the “head-shake” tests. I honestly don’t see these working for anything more extreme than jogging. Don’t get me wrong, they do fit well and are lightweight but just don’t quite pass the “head-shake” test haha. These are IPX4 Water Resistant which is a bonus, and the padded ear cups are removable and washable which is nice (though I have not been able to figure out how).

Pairing was super easy and they sound really good for “On-Ear” headphones which leads me to comfort of “On-Ear” headphones and wearing glasses. I wear glasses and I have issues with “On-Ear” comfort in general. These are no different. Though they are very light and comfortable at first, within only a few minutes of wear they get quite uncomfortable for me. With that said, my Son who does not wear glasses has zero issues with comfort and says that they are really comfortable to him. Also speaking of comfort, personally (after about 30min of wearing) my ears tend to feel like I am wearing Winter Earmuffs as my ears get quite warm. This isn’t a huge deal but I thought it worth mentioning.

Now on to my absolute favorite thing about these headphones. The single Toggle Button on the right earphone. This is so simple to use and can control pretty much everything. Long Press to turn the headphones On or Off. Toggle forward or back to go forward or back a track. Toggle up or down for Volume Up or Down. Short press to Answer and End calls. This innovation is absolutely incredible and makes this the easiest pair of wireless headphones I have ever used. The button on the Left Earphone has the ability to assign three different functions. For example a single click could activate your phones default assistant or double click to play your favorite Spotify playlist and three clicks could play a different Spotify playlist. So basically the left Earphone button can only be used to use your default assistant or play Spotify. My guess is that Adidas could eventually add other apps to this button (with a firmware update) but for now, you only have the two to work with. In my experience so far, this button is a little tricky. First off, the button does not protrude much and can be harder to get it to click, especially if you have large fingers. Once you figure out how to get it to click, the next issue is that you really need to click fast to get the triple click to work. I've gotten to where I can get the triple click to work nearly 80% of the time. It's not a big deal because there's really only two apps it can control. I did notice that if you use this button to start playing Spotify, the Spotify app does not actually open on your phone which kind of freaked me out. This means that the headphones will be all that you need to use to quickly start playing Spotify. If you need to access it for anything else (on Spotify) you'll need to actually launch it from your phone.

USB C charging! More companies need to get on board with USB C and I appreciate the fact that Adidas have included USB C charging which makes for super fast charging of the Adidas RPT-01 Headphones. I have not fully tested the advertised 40 hour runtime but I can say that I have used these a couple hours here and there over my time with them, and I have only had to fully charge them once.

The Adidas app is pretty basic but it does offer some nice eq presets with the option to customize your own. Personally I like to start with the Adidas preset which is "flat" by default. Then if you prefer, you can customize it. The sound is amazing but not quite comparable to some of the other higher end noise cancelling headphones which I won't name.

Overall, I do love the Adidas RPT-01 headphones and they definitely have a place in my collection. Really the only two complaints that I have is, the comfort issue while wearing glasses, and I feel that at this price point they should have come with a nice protective case.

title: adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones
text:
I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.

title: Nice headphones, expensive, small
text:
These are nice looking and sounding headphones but they are small and, in my opinion, overpriced. More about the headphones.

- Sound quality. The have some nice mid-low and low end oomph. There is some crispness there that masks some of the high end lack of articulation. They aren’t terrible on the high end, respectable actually, but for the price I would have expected more.
- Price. List for these are higher by a third than what I feel is reasonable. At a $150 I feel these aren’t quite worth it at $100 these would be a much easier recommendation.
- Design. These look and feel pretty good. The charcoal heather design is very sporting and really fits what Adidas was going for here. I also like the small reflective details in the 3 stripe logo.
- Set-up. Pairing was a cinch with my iPhone. (Though at this point in Bluetooth tech that is expected.)
- Sports features. Water resistant and washable ear pads.
- Size. Small. These almost feel like they were designed for kids. On my 7 1/4 inch head these were almost fully extended. Adults with large heads will find the on-ear pads small and possibly the headband not big enough to fit.

Summary.
Nice headphones but a tad overpriced and possibly small. For kids/teens looking for sporty headphones these though would be a great pickup if the price was right.

title: Overall are a great product with some shortcomings
text:
First off I have the conference speaker and love it, that's what motivated me to buy the headphones.

The headphones should be amazing however they have some shortcomings. First off I ordered the Pro because I wanted the lightning and usb-c, I don't understand why each connector has an adaptor, I assumed it would be a lightning connector on the end and have a usb-c to lightning adaptor included. Instead both are separate adaptors and go to some non standard adaptor on the headphones. So if you loose the adaptor your out of luck. On the pro it came with "comfort tip" memory foam earbuds and silicon tips and silicon tips with wings to hold them in your ear. The comfort tips are not glued onto the headphones. The documentation included is not very robust but the tips do come off. I recommend going to comfort tips website to learn more about them. The silicon tips with wings go onto the end of the earbud. I've included a picture to show you how they go. Make sure the hole in the silicon is lined up with the microphone. When I first received these I didn't have the wing tips on all the way; and it's not clear in the instructions...anyways see attached pictures.

Anker does make a usb-c to lighting cable adaptor and Anker states it is compatible with this headphone, so I returned this one, received a Pioneer Rayz Plus and basically with the adaptor it has the same functionality but better since I do not have an adaptor with some weird connector.

As for the app and updating the headphones that worked perfectly, same as with my conference speaker.

I really love that these are noise cancelling and pick up power from the lightning port, I was so excited when I found these since it's something I don't have to worry about keeping charged and the fact they have a usb-c adaptor so I can use them directly on my computer is amazing. However I recommend the Rayz or Rayz Plus and purchasing the Anker adaptor that is mentioned.

If you don't need/want/or play to charge while using the headphones you probably want the Rayz and not the Rayz Plus since they are cheaper and less bulky, since the lack the charging port.

Only issue I will bring up is I'm not sure about the location of the inline remote/mic. It's kinda large and up high. It doesn't affect wearing the headphones but I'm used to apple design, size, weight and this is more noticeable. It's not bad but will take an adjustment. I like the fact I can program the smart buttons through the app and change the functions, audio prompts, autopause, smart mute, voice isolation, etc...

Pioneer customer support has been amazing, they contacted me with issues on the product and worked through everything and I'm 100% satisfied with the resolution.

title: Not Sure What The Standards Are that These Compare To
text:
I don't think I've used these for a month, and they are disappointing in so many ways.

1. No removable in-ear piece ... Prepare to mess around with your own earwax more than you ever wanted to.

2. Not loud enough, I had my phone cranked all the way up, well past the "hearing damage" warning, these were almost audible enough to drown out ambient noise then... almost... because...

3. These are not only NOT noise cancelling, they seem to be noise AMPLIFYING. I tested this watching TV without the headphones even plugged in, the TV speakers across the room seemed considerably louder while wearing these earbuds. I think the hollow plastic cone works like one of those ear-horns you see Old-timers use in classic Warner Brother's cartoons.

4. The screens... Who thought this was a good design?... These tiny little 2-layer screens that fall out easier than anything... Yeah, that's something I want falling out and rattling around in my ear-canal, a metal screen. Once I tried cleaning these things, and realized how LOOSE those screens were, I took them out and threw them away. On the plus side, they got a tiny bit louder without the screens. But ultimately, the screens served the purpose of keeping these hollow plastic cones from becoming earwax shovels that you can't clean out, because of the 1st problem I stated.

Bonus gripe: The mic was garbage too, it's too low on the cord to pick up your voice clearly.

I suppose the only real positive thing I can say is that after my month or so with these "worst designed earbuds I've ever used", they still worked when I chucked them in the trash. Well, I mean they worked as well as they ever did...

These are horribly designed earbuds, and the mitigation for the horrible design makes them even more horrible, and possibly dangerous. Cheap earbuds I had in the early 90's that came with my knock-off Walkman sounded better and had smarter design. There are better options for similar pricing, get some that have removable ear-pieces, and not tiny little screens built to clog up and possibly dislodge into your ear canal.

title: Great WIRED headset!
text:
It's so good to find more wired TRRS headsets hitting the market. For a while it seemed like only wireless ones were selling and the wired models were all low-end earbud styles or the kind that have the mic embedded by your ears instead of your mouth.
This is a good over-the-ear style set, with decent bass response and sound quality, as well as a mic on the wire. I really like the placement of a microphone on the wire, it is second only to the telescoping mic style you see receptionists and gamers using. It keeps the mic relatively close to your mouth (rather than headsets that put the mic by your ears) so you pick up your voice more than ambient noise in the room. Just keep in mind, it is a TRRS set which means it has the extra pin on the plug for a mic. It may not work properly in standard TRS headphone plugs (stereo only, designed for use with headsets without a mic), although some can work with both.
Most modern laptops support TRRS, as well as tablets and phones (if you're lucky enough to still have a 3.5mm headset jack!).

title: Hack for Ear Pinch and Glasses - Bandage Tape
text:
I’m a longtime fan of ear-hook, wraparound wireless headphones. I wear them daily while working at home, to listen to podcasts, audiobooks, or the spoken audio notes I make for my writing project while my hands are busy. My eight-year-old headphones finally stopped working and I decided to try these.

Advantages:
• Lightweight and not cumbersome
• Good sound quality for headphones of this type (and I’ve owned lots of them)
• Long battery life
• Good wireless range
• Fits securely without slipping around or falling off
• Decent microphone for phone calls - I tried the mic first on my iPhone audio recording app and the results were clear
• Allows enough background sound - I would feel safe riding my bike while wearing them
• Sturdy case included for travel or storage

The only drawback, so far, was that the earphones pinched and hurt my ears after wearing them for a while. Ear pinch is a common problem with these type of earphones. Add in a larger than average head, like mine, and glasses - things got pretty uncomfortable.

I had some self-adhering rubberized bandage tape and decided to wrap some around the earpieces. The tape is just thick enough to cushion the earpieces without causing the headphones to slip off, and it accommodates my glasses. End of pinching problem! If the tape wears down or gets icky from sweat, it will be easy to replace. I’m going to buy some black tape for aesthetic reasons.

I hope these headphones will last a while. I’ll revise this review in a few weeks.

title: Light weight and suitable for vigorous physical exercise
text:
I needed a light weight headphone for music enjoyment during my daily workout. A headphone that completely cups the ears causes overheating and excessive perspiration. Moreover, such a headphone has excessive mass, causing an inertial problem if exercise entails rapid head motion. My workout sessions have a durations of 75 to 120 minutes, which is too long for comfort with most headphones and earbuds.

Overall, I'm very pleased with it. Good sound quality, very light in weight, stays put on on my head, not uncomfortable, and easy to slip on/off my head. Before purchasing it I was skeptical that it would stay in place while I exercised, but it has proven to function quite nicely in that regard. Some of the noteworthy exercises that I subjected it to: situp crunches, jumping jacks, push-ups, and quick torso-twisting. And then afterwards I gave it the ultimate test of staying power, i.e. rapid cyclical shaking of my head like a "yes", and also like a "no".

And I've worn them up to 2 hours continuously without much discomfort to complain of. Keep in mind that I don't wear eyeglasses, so I'm NOT accustomed to having anything resting on my ears. For reference, my head's semi-circumference ( measured around the rear half; just above my ears ) is exactly 11", and my ears are naturally close to my head. Doubtless, my features are ideal for the size of this particular item. It's not difficult to imagine that a different person having a smaller head, or with ears that pop outwards will likely not get as firm a fit as me.

Its integral one-piece design has a couple overwhelming advantages over other lightweight personal audio devices that are designed as separate two-piece. Only one set of switches, with both earpieces controlled simultaneously. Quick and easy to place on your ears. And the same for temporarily getting them off your ears, because you simply slip them down to cling around your neck. The convenience of stowing them around your neck cannot be overstated; keeps your hands free while preventing you from temporarily misplacing them. Thus, it stays and goes with me all day; either around my head or around my neck. If I'm wearing a shirt or jacket with a collar, the Itayak is concealed very neatly when stowed low on my neck. Nobody notices that I'm still wearing the Itayak when it's not in use.

While listening to music there's a noticable lack of deep base, i.e. unless you maintain pressure on both earmuffs with your fingers, which of course is impractical. I had thought the explanation was that it's ELECTRONICS were really designed for an earbud system, and that Itayak had instead implemented them incorrectly. But this theory was later disproven, because of a similar observation with a Lakukom earbud system that I obtained afterward. In fact, the Lakukom earbuds require slightly MORE finger pressure than the Itayak earmuffs in order to reproduce an equal level of bass. IOW, the Lakukom's bass reproduction is inferior to Itayak's. And here's the kicker : as of this writing Lakukom continues to advertise that product as "deep bass" :-(

Most days of the week I use the Itayak while exercising about 5' in front of a noisy 18" dia circulating fan. It's also in use while driving my Ford Focus or Jeep Patriot along a county highway. I've never observed any significant degree of active background noise cancellation. This isn't a complaint, as I had no such expectation for it, and that wasn't one of my requirements.

It's Iithium battery was already charged as received.

Only 3 negatives:

1. When the battery charge drops to 20% or below, the recorded voice annunciator "Battery charge low" interrupts whatever you're listening to about every 30 secs. This warning is far, far too early, because with 20% charge, there's still at least 90 mins of functional battery service remaining. So it's quite annoying to have that last 20% of charge practically wasted by an intolerably frequent warning that's not even necessary yet. I'd prefer a warning when battery charge is at or below 5%. Hopefully that improvement will appear in the next future version of this model.

2. Disconnects from Bluetooth when charging. Thus, it's unusable while charging.

3. The click-switches on the right earpiece are frustratingly difficult to use while the headset is on your head. In order to operate the click-switches, you really cannot be wearing this particular headset at the same time, because with this Itayak unit you must be able to see where you're fingers are. It's a minor nuisance, as you shouldn't be using any headset if frequent on/off switching is required. Also keep in mind that music play can always be paused via its app, or muted via the hardware button on the tablet/phone.

text:
I've had a pair of these for just shy of a year, and at first I loved them! They rested in my ears nicely, and barring being very active always stayed in. The sound was really great, not top of the line, but really good without spending much more. Battery last forever.

However, as time has gone on, these earbuds are showing their true colors as cheap headphones, priced much higher than they should be. It's no wonder they are always on sale. As many others have said, my number one complaint is the silicon cover on the tip (part in the ear) no longer sticks. It's completely peeled up and will completely fall off in a matter of days. With out it, the earbuds will be unbearable to use and fall out constantly. This started happening after 5 months. After continuing to deteriorate, around the 8 month mark I decided to contact JBL since these have a 1 year limited warranty, and was promptly told it doesn't cover most physical damage, even though it's from a design flaw.

I wouldn't waste your time on these. At their sale prices, you can get other products that better, and at regular price you might as well spend the extra for airpods or something else.

I have a bunch of JBL products, which is why I was draw to these initially, but I would not recommend to anyone.

title: Great headset
text:
These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned. The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome. I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out. If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it. But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.

The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack. I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.

The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMeeting, Skype for Business and Google Voice.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.

title: Excellent quality for the price
text:
I felt the need to review because there were wildly varing reviews out there and I almost didn't purchase these. I own 3 varieties of BOSE headphones, and I needed to get a new headset with a USB connection since my work laptop is broken in that I can hear web calls but not speak. I'll address some conflicting reviews that I found to be bunk:
Comfort - I'm usually not a fan of on-ear headsets but these are padded and comfy. They aren't too light as to slip off, nor are they heavy or bulky. One reviewer said the cord and control circle (volume and mute) was so heavy as to drag the headphones off his head ... totally untrue. The cord is very long - you can slide over to your file cabinet or printer - yay. And the cord is NOT heavy as to feel its weight on that side of the headset.
Sound - The sound is excellent and as I mentioned, I'm a BOSE girl. There are so many USB headsets in the $39 - $79 range and I'm glad I spent the extra dollars for this price point. Working from home in the COVID age means a lot more WebEx and Zoom meetings, and sound - and noise cancellation - has to be excellent. One reviewer said she could hear herself breathing. That only happens when the mouthpiece is aimed at your nostril - duh. Move it.

I can't comment on longevity as these are new, but hopefully these will have a nice long usage life.

title: My machine moves on a daily basis so this is great! These headphones do the job just fine
text:
I recently got a new laptop and, given the mobile nature of this machine, I wanted to set it up so I plug/unplug as few things as possible every time I take it somewhere. Eventually I decided I was getting sick of plugging and unplugging from the headphone jack. Okay, it's a first-world problem, but what often happened is I forgot to re-plug in the headphones and would end up making unexpected noise.

So I wanted a pair of USB headphones, the reason being I could just plug them in to the same USB hub that the mouse and keyboard is plugged into. So now I just have the one plug to attach when I dock my machine. My machine moves on a daily basis so this is great!

These headphones do the job just fine. They do NOT require any sort of driver install (tested on Windows 7 and OSX). Audio quality is better than expected, I suspect because USB provides power. The little hand-remote is nice, admittedly I rarely use it, though, since I have the volume controls on my keyboard. They're also nice and compact.

If I had one criticism it's that I cannot find any sort of marking which describes which headphone is left or right. It's not a big deal, after-all this set has a microphone on one side so it's really just a matter of figuring it out once.

All in all, I dig it, and I'm glad to finally be off that headphone jack!

text:

My experience was, the sound would work well for 20-30 seconds then switch to very low quality with no low-end, and flip back and forth between bad and good quality, sometimes never switching back to good. I called Jabra support and they were very helpful, but we didn't come to a root cause.

I sent these back and received a new pair, they did the same thing.

I noticed in the system tray while testing sound, there was a microphone icon that said 'Cisco Webex Meetings is using your microphone'. Long story short, when Cisco Webex Meetings is using your microphone, it seems to affect the quality of the headphones.

I don't know if this is an issue with the headset or not, but I feel like it's a windows issue caused by Webex.

This is a good headset for using with voice call software. That is the main advertised feature of the headset. I like how clear the microphone is for voice calls. The headphones are good, but they are very low volume. I have to turn the volume up way higher than I normally do for my headphones when I am wearing this headset. The mic is not flexible, so the mic goes right up to your face and I often worry that people will hear me breathing when I wear this. The mic arm swivels either way so you can put the mic on either side of your head.

The headband does not expand very far, so if you have a big head this may be a challenge to fit. The cable for this headphone comes in two parts; there is a 3.5mm part that connects to the controls, and then the USB cable comes out from the controls and can be plugged into any USB port. So you can use this with either a USB or 3.5mm connection. The headphones also comes with a carrying case and you can download some drivers from the Jabra website to add modest functionality.

I think these headphones are good, but the price is very inflated for what you get. I can get much better headphones for a similar price. I would wait until the price goes down to get these

title: Stereo Bluetooth headsets are way better than they used to be ...
text:
I've only had the August EP650 for a couple days now, and there are a number of quality, comprehensive reviews -- so I thought I would write something specifically from the perspective of someone who hasn't owned a stereo Bluetooth headset since they first came out.

The tech has come a long way, and I'm really quite pleased by how good these are for the price. If you're like me and have a bad recollection of the early days -- with the flaky connectivity and the terrible, tinny sound -- you'll be pleasantly surprised.

Build quality feels pretty decent for the price; comfortable; buttons are easy to find with the headset on, and I've been putting them on while taking public transit, without playing anything, just so I can concentrate on reading, and not the prattle.

So, thumbs up. If you've not been happy with Bluetooth cans in the past and don't want to spend too much to check them out again, the August EP650 is a very good option.

title: Sweet Spot Found.
text:
I have IEM dementia. Spent hundreds if not thousands looking for iphone headsets that work for me. I've had Monsters, Shures, Etymōtics, Audio-Technicas, Sonys, JVCs, multiples of some of these brands and many others.

For exercise you need something that is cheap, lays down a good beat, has low cord noise and stays put in your ears. Because you are going to beat on them. I like Nixon Micro Blaster phones. I can find them on eBay for around $16 shipped. Their over-ear cords keep the noise down and stay put. Sound is great for something so cheap.

For airline travel, train commuting, or lawn mowing/snow blowing, you need seriously damped sound isolation. I like Etymōtic's HF3 for these times. They feature a truly fine sounding single balanced armature design and hands down the best microphone in the Apple headphone industry. And their true deep insertion design allows real near total physical sound isolation. Not for use when you need awareness of stuff going on around you.

For compromise use in just about any situation, I have preferred Sony's XBA1i single balanced Armature model, which is now discontinued but can still be found NOS for under $30. A very fine inexpensive headset with refined sound and light compact design. Lacking in deep bass like the Etymōtic but sounds just beautiful anyway.

I have left the Sonys home for these new Senns. The Momentum in-ears have surprisingly balanced frequency response for a dynamic design. Fast and engaging midrange and acceptable highs. Best sounding dynamic IEM I have, better than my much-loved metal bodied JVC Micro HD Carbon Nanotube Japan imports.

And very solid bass without overplaying it like those ridiculously tuned Beats. I have some very expensive 4-driver Sony balanced armature phones and these sound as good in most aspects for a third of the price. Sony's hybrid BA/dynamic designs deliver more engaging sound but boy do you pay for it and they're HUGE. Ditto JVC's multi-driver dynamics.

What Sennheiser has done in this $100 package is deliver a headset that sounds wonderful and is an acceptable compromise of the virtues discussed above such that if you only want to own one pair of headphones this Momentum IEM is a strong contender. Excellent small size, comfortable shape,decent shallow-insertion isolation, beautiful sound with great bass, good cable, mic and remote, durable construction.

All for the market sweet spot price of a hundred bucks and worth every penny.

Some aftermarket Comply-type foam tips can improve isolation still further if you wish, and there are triple flange insertion tips out there that will turn these guys into true isolation stars. I don't like either of those options and find the included silicone tips to work great.

In short, these are great, bone stock right out of the box. If you are so interested that you are reading customer reviews, consider this a full-throated endorsement from a true IEM junkie.

My new all-around favorite. The Sony single BA is relegated to listening in bed. I still recommend it, but these have real bass, stay put better, are far better built and more comfortable.

Total win. Best IEM I've ever tried from Sennheiser.

That's not necessarily true of other brands in their price range. Read carefully when you start to shop, because a name doesn't mean that much anymore.

title: Headphones
text: I really like the look and color of these headphones. There is a large letter "L" and "R" on the inside of the headphones. They adjust about an inch on each side. The top and the ear piece are padded and very comfortable. The ear pieces rotate about 90 degrees, and they can be folded in. There is an audio jack, a mini usb port, a volume increase and decrease button, pause button, noise cancelling activation button, and power button. The volume button controls the volume on the device you have it connected to. When you press the volume button, for some reason the media stops for a second then adjusts. When you turn it on, it makes a noise and tells you the status of the battery. The headphones are pretty loud; I was able to hear what was playing clearly while holding the headphones in my hand. The sound is good too, all the bass from my sons came through and sound the same as if I was in a car. The noise cancellation comes on automatically when you turn them on. I feel like when the music is all the way up, it is noise cancelling and I cant even hear myself yelling what (not at the top of my lungs). As I turned the music down, I could begin to hear myself a little more, but I couldn't hear things outside of that (this is with the volume at about 80%). The true test was turning on my tv with my sound bar on (and it's a really good one) and I kept turning it up and didn't hear a thing. I took these headphones off and my tv was blaring, so much so that my sub woofer was vibrating the bed, but I didn't hear a thing. So, these are DEFINITELY noice cancelling.

title: Great sound quality and amazing battery life
text:
I was not ready to invest in a set of Apple, Bose, or Sony headphones, yet I was afraid to buy the cheapest headphones available. i wanted something that wouldn't ruin my music, or break the bank, and based upon other reviews, I believe I found a happy medium with these Anker headphones The bass doesn't sound over amplified, or pushed and it has a nice balance in the mid and high ranges.

At first I used it with my phone, and was terribly disappointed, but on my computer and other bluetooth sound systems, they sounded fantastic. I later learned I would have to re download my entire Apple Music library to enjoy higher bit rate music, so I primarily use these with other devices.

The battery life it amazing. I have not had to charge them in almost a month after daily use of an hour or so. When the battery does get low it takes only a few minutes to get hours of use thanks to its quick charge technology.

They are lightweight, comfortable, and the sound quality is surprising decent for an inexpensive set of headphones. About my only complaint would be that the controls are not as intuitive as I would like, but overall I am very pleased with this purchase, and would highly recommend them.

text:
Context: I've used this product mainly with SE846 for almost half a year now.

Pros:

- Decent sound

Cons:
- Not so ergonomic
- Very hard to detach IEMs from the MMCX connection. It requires a lot more force to detach than with any other cables or wireless adapters I've used. It eventually BROKE one of the MMCX pins on my SE846.

Conclusion:

title: Physically solid, technologically average
text:
Been using this thing for a day now. Here's my pros and cons.....

Pros
1. Solid construction. Wide metal interior headband feels strong and fits my melon head snugly but not uncomfortably.
2. Quick charging via USB-C.
3. Ear cup is supposed to be "over the ear" but it sits more "on the ear". But, it does pretty much fully cover my ear so it does a good job of blocking external sound. It's still comfortable and doesn't make my ear sweat which many previous headsets have.
4. The plastic casing of the earcup and headband and good too. I like the solidity of it and the texture. Not flimsy or sticky at all.

Cons
1. Lower than average volume on ear piece and mic. On both I need to set the volume/output to about 85% to be average sound levels in Discord and other apps. But, when set to this level, the remote party hears me fine and I hear them fine and clear.
2. Yeah, it's got a dongle and it's bluetooth but the behavior of the headset is confusing. When you power it up, it goes into pairing mode or bluetooth connect mode immediately so this appears to be the preferred connection method even IF the dongle is installed and waiting for a connection. A short press on the mute button seems to stop the bluetooth pairing process and it immediately then says "paired" as it finds the dongle. There is no switching process to actively flip back and forth between dongle and bluetooth. That has to be set on headset power up. In my opinion the dongle should be the primary connection method not bluetooth.
3. The dongle connection seems a little hinky. If I'm listening to music on the headset and using the dongle as my connection, when I add the headset mic to ManyCam as the input source, the quality of the audio drops significantly and begins to drop in volume as well. Maybe the noise cancelling logic is crushing the audio stream? Dunno. But, if I remove the headset as the input source from ManyCam, the audio stream immediately goes back to better quality. This does NOT happen when I'm connected via bluetooth.

I'm going to keep the headset unless something else pops up I'm not fond of. It was cheaper than Logitech and better build than that brand but Logitech certainly seems to have better functionality.

text:
Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome

title: Finally - a convincing KZ IEM!
text:
I own many Chi-Fi IEMs, among them a few by KZ (ZSN and ZS 10). The ZSN were fun V-shaped IEMs with a somewhat peculiar timbre and very bright highs, while the original ZS 10 was possibly the worst experiment in the IEM-making industry - muddy, lifeless, dark, and unnatural. Honestly, my expectations for the ZS 10 Pro were not high, even though the initial reviews were excellent. I finally decided to try them and was very pleasantly surprised - they have nothing in common with the original ZS 10!

I replaced the stock cable with a NiceHCK 16-core silver-plated upgrade cable and the silicone tips with a pair of Comply Isolation 500 memory foam tips. I tested the ZS 10 Pro on a R3 Pro Saber DAP, streaming hi-res files from Tidal, Qobuz, and also trying a few FLACs from my own collection. And I must admit that the ZS 10 Pro impressed me!

The sound is very clear and natural, the brightness is more controlled than on other KZ models I've tried, and the bass is very well expressed without overemphasis even through memory foam tips. Vocals sound natural and do not feel more recessed. Not all genres sound equally immersive, though - the ZS 10 Pro shines with pop/electronic, but has less brilliance with metal/hard rock. The curve seems to be halfway between V-shaped and neutral, which is a plus for me because I don't like completely neutral signatures (and steer clear of brands like Shure, even though I own a pair of their earphones and very rarely use them).

The comfort is average, better than on the KZ 10 and about the same as the ZSN. The stock cable is not good at all and since the IEMs sound so good out of the box, you should consider replacing the cable with an upgrade 8- or 16-core audio cable.

There are a number of other very competitive offerings with a similar signature and a similar price tag that you can buy on Amazon - RevoNext QT2, TRN V80, Blon BL-03, etc. The KZ ZS 10 Pro has a more controlled treble that all those and a slightly more clear nod toward balancing the sound (the others are firmly V-shaped, fun-sounding IEMs). It compares favorably also to slightly more expensive and more balanced IEMs like the Tin HiFi T3. It adds better bass presence and controls more the treble in comparison to the T3, and has a similar clarity of sound.

In conclusion - finally, there is a great-sounding offering from KZ!

title: Comfortable step up from the KBear KS2
text:
Pictured: KZ ZS10 Pro with aftermarket cable, sitting next to a FiiO BTR5.

Like the KBear KS2, this is an IEM with a V-shaped sound signature. Nice grunt in the low end, non-fatiguing treble. I think most people would enjoy this sound signature, as I do. The aforementioned KS2 has a similar sound, just a bit lower quality in both sound and build (as you would expect for half the price of these). It would be hard to go wrong with either pair.

As for fit, these are the best out of all my IEMs to use. They fit into my ear and stay there, no fiddling for a perfect seal. Stock tips (pre-installed) worked just fine for me. Your mileage may vary of course, but this combined with the fact that they sound quite nice has made them a daily driver for me; I take them to work nearly every day. I have IEMs that cost 4x as much that I pass over simply because they do not fit as securely and easily.

If you care about looks, these look decent. I got the black version, the faceplate has a pleasing matte black finish with some nice contrast from brass screws. They certainly look better IRL than in the picture. The rest of the housing is plastic; not really a downside at this price point, but good to consider. No complaints here.

Last, the stock cable. As you would expect for this price, the stock cable kinda sucks. I don't mean sonically, as I am no golden-eared listener (yet); I just mean it's thin and cheap looking. I would buy a nicer aftermarket cable, of which there are plenty around. I confess I did not listen to it, simply took the cable I bought for my KS2 and used that right off the bat. That's a plus for removable cables at least.

I bought these headphones as a cheaper alternative to a more robust pair of wireless headphones, like the pixel buds or airpods. Really, I bought them in late 2019 as a hold out for the pixel buds 2 and the USB C cable on my pixel 3 keeps giving out and I just didn't want to deal with the hassle of wired headphones any longer.

The sound quality is good. As someone who is used to listening on a respectable set of AKG 702s or Sony MDR-7056s they obviously don't stack up, but it's better than I would have thought to achieve for the price point, especially in the width of the soundstage.

My main gripe is the in-ear feel. They encompass your whole ear canal with sweaty, grippy plastic. The bad kind. Like the kind that makes it really hard to talk while wearing them, or when you move you hear a muffled rumpling with every step. I personally can't stand that and would prefer a more open ear feel, but that's just me. Just be aware of what you are buying, I find it hard to take calls wearing these as my voice seems to reverberate all throughout my head.

I keep them in my bedroom, where, if I want to doze off to some tunes they provide a decent option. Also, they are good for airplanes as the mild noise cancelling and isolation will drone out even the heftiest of plane sounds. As everyday headphones or workout headphones they are a no-go for me though.

text:
The headphones themselves are nice. They pair easily, and can easily use one or the other, or both. They pair automatically with the last device upon pulling them out of the case. I find that as I move frequently, they often feel like they are going to fall out and I have to continuously reposition them in my ears.

The biggest issue though is that I find these to be incredibly uncomfortable in my ears after an hour or more. I've tried all the different ear pieces on both, and they just get annoying after a period of time. I'm not sure if this is a personal issue due to my ears, or by the nature of true wireless buds themselves. However, I use wired earbuds and have zero issues wearing them almost the entire working day, sometimes for three+ hours without any pain in my ears. I believe the discomfort comes from the weight of the battery, bluetooth, etc, tech, all crammed into a tiny earbud and the weight of that resting solely on your ear canal. Wired buds don't have nearly as much weight to them. If you can overlook that or know that isn't a bother to you, I would definitely recommend them.

Battery life is close to 9 hours when listening at just under half volume, call quality is okay. The person on the other end can hear me fine but my voice isn't the clearest.

title: Get some foam earbuds
text: These are fantastic at this price point and offer good sound and value.  If you're reading this, you're not moron or a sucker in buying $250 Airpods or even $100 earbuds from mainline manufacturers.  I upgraded from wireless earbuds with the wire connecting in back, but wanted true wireless since I'm at the gym or running 5-6 days a week.  The wire in back got annoying.  The build quality is solid with a really nice case and I like how they connect via magnet to charge.  Battery performance is always overrated with bluetooth stuff so only time will tell how long they truly last - that's why it's useless to pay top dollar for something with a non-replaceable battery.  The real key to all earbuds is to get some foam tips though IMO.  So much more comfortable, better sounding, and you get some noise cancellation as well - it really upgrades the sound.  Foam tips don't last as long with sweat so get a pack with the size you need, not a multi pack, so you'll use all of them.  Overall, these are a great buy, there are tons of these budget true wireless buds on AZ.  Sport loops and foam tips are the key for runners and highly active people.  The sound quality will obviously not match Airpods or other high end buds, but remember those morons are still listening to crappy mp3s anyway while spending $230 more.

title: A good value
text: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: CozyPhones are, in fact, pretty cozy.
text:
This sleep headphone band fits quite comfortably. Before I bought this I was introduced to the product at my mom's house and I wear a considerably bigger hat size than her, but the stretchy band fit both of us perfectly. Despite my big bobblehead of a noggin, I don't find this too tight even when worn for hours, and yet it hasn't become stretched out either. A smaller headed person could still wear mine. Also in regard to fit, the light weight, low profile speakers can easily be moved inside the headband to exactly where they are most comfortable and best heard for each wearer (I did have to move the speakers back when I tried my mom's). Once in place the speakers stay put really well simply due to the friction between the textures of the fuzzy fabric pad over each speaker and the headband's fabric. I occasionally have to tweak where a speaker is sitting as I put them on, but once in place the speaker has never needed to be repositioned during wear. I also love that the speakers can be slipped out through the back so the headband can be laundered.

I would say that the sound quality is that of average headphones. I don't notice a discernable difference between these and any other headphones I own, but I may not have as attuned an ear as some people seem to have, so my feelings won't be hurt if you get a second opinion on this part.

I don't really have any cons to mention for these, but wait, I almost forgot to mention that when buying these I saw multiple other reviewers warn that the dye bled from the colored edge of their headbands. I should say that I specifically bought the one with the white edge to avoid that happening. I've had no dye transfer at all from mine, so I can suggest getting the white edged band if that's a concern.

Hope this helps.

title: They Could Build in a Tiny Modicum of Durability
text:
Are you tired of lousy reviewers who write up glowing 5-star reviews after one week, so you have no idea if the thing lasts a year? Are you tired of paid reviewers who say "As advertised"? Or worse, "Arrived on time"? Be still, my wild heart! Here, take my money!
Like, why aren't they reviewing the Post Office for that?

Well, your help has arrived.

When these started failing, I searched my order history to see how long they lasted.
Slightly over a year!
I would pay more for more durability.
However, I did pay more once - a lot more. Before these, I bought a set of Sleepphones. Directly from the company, maybe before they were offered here.
I paid SEVERAL TIMES as much for those!
Warning: It does not buy you durability.

So I like these slightly better, because they are not so unconscionably exorbitant.

However: "Better Than Sleepphones" isn't saying much. It is a very, very low bar to clear.

So if I see ANYthing like these, that give you a few more durability units for a few more dollars, I'm on it.
Sadly, I expect to see the few more dollars charged, with nothing in return.

I still don't know whether to buy these again. The other depressing option is to buy the speaker "refill".
You know, the same junk that was installed in this headband?
There is a business opportunity for someone to make a durable, affordable set of thin speakers. Surprisingly, some excellent, affordable products are "Made in USA".

Do it!

title: Great headphones for a three year old, and above...
text:
While preparing for our upcoming trip we felt that it would be good to work on getting our almost three year old more comfortable with wearing his volume limited headphones; however, once they were on we realized they were definitely too small for his head, fully extended. We noticed some of the CozyPhones child headphones and thought it'd be a great idea for him to have the headband style. While looking at the specifications for them we decided it would be in our better interest to ensure that the measurements would fit his head, as 3T are a little small for him, already, and wanted something that wouldn't be outgrown before he's even had a chance to really use them. Sure enough, the child size headphones were already too small, so I started looking for adult headphones in the CozyPhones brand, while also comparing other similar brands as well.

The dimensions of these headphones were half an inch smaller than his head circumference, based on the Q & A section for the CozyPhones sleep headphones, making it so they wouldn't just fall off. Using the tape method, mentioned in the included business card, it was easy enough to position the speakers in the headband to the correct placement for his ears. Using the [[ASIN:B01JHI73IC Limit Volume]] app on his [[ASIN:B01GEW27DA Fire 7 Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 8 GB, Black - with Special Offers]] we are able to ensure that the volume doesn't get too loud for him.

Our little guy enjoys wearing these, even though he'll occasionally pull them away from his ears, only to quickly put them back on his ears. When asked if they're comfortable, he replied with "yes".

These are a great form of headphones for a three year old that's in the 95% size range for their age, or anyone else looking for some cozy headphones.

title: Very good sound quality, great comfort
text:
These earbuds were up against some tough competition. I regularly use my Airpods with my apple products (which "just work," but are not super comfortable) and my Jabra's (which are outstanding in every way, but were triple the price of the Soul S-Nano's, so it's not really fair...)

So keeping in mind the affordability of the Soul S-Nano buds, I was really impressed.

Sound quality:

My test album for audio stuff is deadmou5 - "here's the drop!"
- Bass 3/5 - You definitely hear the lows, but you won't feel them in your teeth
- 3D sound 5/5 - Really good. I ended up closing my eyes for a couple tracks and "watching" the music in that way you can when you can hear it coming from different "parts of the room" on a good 3D track.
- Clarity 4.5/5 - For buds? This small? Pretty darn good. Instrumentals were clear, treble sounds great and beats are crisp.
- Volume - subjective. I'll say these can get painfully loud. Be careful!
- hear-through feature - I don't use it. I don't use it on my Jabra's either. It's just sounded weird to me on whatever buds I've used it on and I've never liked it. It does work. It actually sounds better on the Soul buds that it does on my Jabra's, but it's a personal preference thing.

Comfort:

- 5/5. I have princess ears. I find earpod/airpods pretty uncomfortable I usually prefer over-the-ear cans for comfort. These buds are VERY comfortable. They come with three sets of tips, so you can pick the ones that fit best for you. They stay in my ears without being "suction-y" and I can wear them for hours.

Controls/connection:

- Touch controls 4/5 - These take some getting used to. Read the quick-start guide to learn the gestures (there are more than I thought and some are not intuitive). Generally, they're pretty reliable, but sometimes the pause doesn't stay paused and volume control goes up instead of down because it doesn't pick up both taps. It's also very easy to accidentally set off a control just doing normal stuff. I'm afraid I'm going to accidentally call someone taking out an earbud or something.
- Bluetooth stability 4/5 - Once connected, the buds usually remember the connection. Sometimes they don't automatically reconnect; sometimes they do. Overall, this has been pretty good and even when it doesn't work, it's very easy to fix manually by reconnecting to your phone using the phone settings menu.
- Initial connection 5/5 - Very easy. No problems at all connecting!

Battery/case:

Battery life 5/5 - I've been using these for a couple days and am listening to them right now. I've been working and jamming out for two hours and I'm only down to 80% battery. And then I can put them in the case and top up.
Case 3/5 - This was the only real disappointment for me. The case does not seem super durable to me. The plastic is thin enough that you can see the LEDs on the buds through the case. Seeing as you need the case to charge the buds, if the case breaks, you're out of luck. I've cut up a vinyl sticker to put on the case for just a little extra protection, but I'm still a little wary of just throwing it into my bag or leaving it hanging on my purse strap where it can get bumped into and cracked. Compared to the Jabra and Airpod cases, it is very flimsy.
Charging 5/5 - the case charges fast and has a USB-C connection. Not a micro-usb port in sight. The included cable is VERY short, though, so if that doesn't work for you, grab another one that you have at home. It will work fine.

So overall... 4.5 out of 5. For the price, these buds are quite good!

text: These in-ear headphones are very impressive.  They are durable, have lots of different sizes of ear plugs so I'm sure one of them will fit your ears perfectly.  The cord is made of a type of nylon material that won't allow you to hear the cord dragging across your shirt.  They sound very, very good, but for my taste they're a bit bass-heavy.  If some ear-thumping bass is what you like then you won't be disappointed in these.  But if you're looking for some separation between the lows, mids and highs and not wanting your bass to override everything else, then maybe you should look at a different set of headphones.  Depending on what type of music you're listening to, for instance, Lady Gaga....  then these phones will make you happy, but not so great if you're into Simon and Garfunkle.  And to really get the fantastic sound from these headphones you need to set your volume around 8 or 9 out of 10.  Anything lower and the sound gets really flat.  For half the price of these earphones, you can get a set of Skullcandy Ink'd in-ear phones that will give you across-the-board sound with enough bass to make you happy but not so much that it washes out the other ranges of music...  and you don't have to crank the Ink'd as high in volume, maybe 6-7 to get the same amount of pleasure from your music.  These SoundMagic's are very good headphones, but you can get something as good or better for a much lower price.

title: Honest Review
text:
Update - 3/26/22: Right side just went out on me at the worst time. What good is all the high quality material when the driver goes out on you after a few months? I'll give it a couple stars for the experience it gave me, but not a fan of now unexpectedly having to get earbuds again for no good reason.

Original Review: Honestly I don't know what the raving over these is about. Yes they seem very high quality with their braided cord and their heavy drivers, and they are just a TAD bit better sound quality and noise cancelling than the (very) cheap JVC earbuds they replaced. For the price these are a big cut above anything else and I'd recommend them for that alone.

They sent a nice felt pouch to keep them in (who uses these?) and a nice note saying thanks. I appreciated that.

I can't find where the manufacturer is (threw the packaging away before I wrote this, too) but I did read an German address on the packaging, so it's possible it could be a German designed and manufactured product (a big, big plus for quality if so).

Here's the critical part. Maybe I don't have a good enough sound card on my computer (laptop) or phone (S7) to experience the "driving bass" as advertised, but it's nothing special from what I've experienced so far. And with that I don't see why the drivers are that much heavier than normal earbuds. Again, don't get me wrong, the sound quality is pretty good.

What I really bought these for is to replace the cheap earbuds that went out on me all of a sudden, and the mic which I don't have at all. And while they did their job in replacing the earbuds, the mic isn't that good. It works well enough to do the job if you're in a pinch, but it could have been much, much better than it is given the rest of the effort that went into this product.

So all that being said if you're looking for pretty good sound and quality for a cheap price these are it. If you are looking for a cheap set to use the mic with, I'd look elsewhere.

Edit: After getting used to these I had to upgrade the rating to 5 stars, despite how I still feel about the mic. These heavy, corded earbuds are constantly reminding me I got more than I paid for, and after listening to them a while bass does jump out at me in subtle ways. They could probably handle a lot more than what my computer is giving me.

Something that has been a great relief to me as well is they don't get tangled and twisted. Half the time the buds are stuck together when I pick them up to put them on because their magnets are so strong. That probably helps in staying untangled.

title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
text:
I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation.

The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did.

After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great.

Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.
