title: I really want to like these...
text:
This is my first purchase of earbuds in the over $200 category. I got the Jabra Elite 65t as soon as they came out and have since bought a couple of other pairs of earbuds in the under $100 category that had better features like IPX7 or 8hr battery life. Therefore I was excited to upgrade to the XM4 for their bettery life and the noise canceling.

Unfortunately, I've had several issues with these. I don't have particularly small ears. Usually the medium tips fit without issue. On the XM4, I started with the medium tips and tested their air tightness using the app. The small tips don't have any kind of seal on my ears without really shoving them super far down my ear canal, so I decided to stick with the medium size. Unfortunately, I have experienced significant ear fatigue enough so that I can't wear the earbuds for more than a couple of hours. I have since switched to the small tips for the sake of comfort, but that means sacrificing any passive noise canceling - and unless I have a defective unit, without the passive noise canceling in addition to the active noise canceling, there is absolutely no difference between having the noise canceling on and off. To me, this completely defeats the purpose of buying noise canceling earbuds.

I also have had issues with connectivity such as the bluetooth connection on my phone suddenly dropping and having to go into the app to manually pair them again.

In terms of battery life, depending on the control settings of each earbud, there can be a difference in the drain of battery between the left and right side. On a bad day, I had a 30% difference with the right draining significantly faster. My earbuds are using the factory settings with the playback controls on the right and the noise canceling on the left for reference.

Both the connectivity problems and the bettery difference between the earbuds has seemed to have gotten better since performing a factory reset, but be aware that there is still a little difference in the rate of battery drain between the L and R earbuds (It's not super significant now and maybe reaches under 7-8% difference at the end of the day).

I bought some Comply foam tips, which I hope will fix the discomfort issue and make the noise canceling work at the optimal rate without the ear fatigue. However, I shouldn't have to modify almost $300 earbuds to make them work like they should. It would help if Sony would offer more sizes of ear tips to help make them more usable for a wider population. Then again, if I have gripes like these, then maybe the XM4s aren't for me. Makes me super sad considering I think that they're probably fantastic for most people.

title: Above average offering, but don't care for the design of them or the gesture controls
text:
This product feels different to me than other Sony stuff I've gotten. It's like they've gone out of their way to make everything feel like cardboard. The packaging was like egg carton, and the earbuds and their charging station are a rough lightweight material in a drab color. The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.

USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on.

I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds. Lots of companies putting out new designs.

title: Didn't do it for me
text:
I purchased the Klim earbuds as a substitute for wearing gaming headphones, and I was overall disappointed with the product. After about a week of use, I noticed that the left earbud was significantly quieter than the right, making for an unbalanced and awkward experience. Due to this, I will be returning mine.

Assuming not all Klim earbuds have this problem and mine was just defective, I had some other problems with these headphones as well. The product comes with several styles of replacement buds, ranging from different material to different shapes, and even one in a different (red) color. Unfortunately, they all seem to be molded to fit about the same size ear. I have pretty average sized ears, maybe a little small. When plugging my earbuds into my PC (below my desk), I noticed the earbuds were sagging significantly in my ears. The metal material they used on the outside of the earbuds is a little bit heavy, and since the earbuds don't fit me well to begin with, they are difficult to keep in place where I want them.

Also, as these buds are marketed toward PC users, at 1.7 meters (slightly longer than your average iPhone or Google Pixel bud cord length), I wish the cord was even a little longer. There isn't much wiggle room by the time you plug them into a PC that's sitting on the ground and run them up to your ears. I'm not a tall person, and these buds were just *barely* passable length-wise for this purpose. You won't experience this problem if using on a mobile/handheld device, but small cords are a big issue for PC gamers.

Sound quality was okay; I found the bass to be passable. Treble was a little harsh, but fine for $20. The product is packaged well and if you get a working product and generally don't have problems with earbuds, these will probably still be okay with you. In the near future, I will be replacing these with earbuds that resemble the shape of the iPhone buds, and hopefully will find something with a cord 2+ meters in length.

title: I hope you like BASS!
text:
First, the good. These earbuds appear to be made with good materials, and provide multiple sizes and materials in the ear-canal inserts. The wire gauge is good for the purpose and the volume is higher than most. They might last for a long time for normal use. The in-line controls seem to work just fine and the designers placed them in a good place along the wire. Good design principles seem evident.

But I might not use them because of the negatives.

These earbuds put so much bass on the music, voices, and even my white-noise generators that I cannot listen for long and revert to other options like my bulky over-the-ear headphones that I certainly cannot carry out of the house on my normal routine. I used the eq on my phone and dropped the bass out and raised the treble up as high as possible, and still there's too much bass.

I changed the ear canal inserts to their secondary option, a kind of rubber insert that doesn't fit the ear and doesn't eliminate any outside noise. Another fail for me. It might be the right thing for others, but not for me. And as for the shape of the sound with the new inserts, I didn't notice. They're too uncomfortable.

And something that I consider a "manufacturing flaw" annoys me even more. The left earbud constantly clicks and snaps, like there's noise in the line, but it's a completely mechanical noise and I can duplicate it when the set is unplugged from my phone. I think it's a loose diaphragm that's moving with the shape of my ear and clicking when it moves.

Sometimes I use my earbuds for sound isolation alone; no music, no sound in them. I just use them to isolate me from the world. I cannot even do that with these earbuds because the random clicks and snaps jar me from my meditative silence, with just a swallow or a sigh. Sigh.

I'm still uncertain if I will use these earbuds so I'm still debating with myself about even getting a fix or replacement. If I'm not going to ever use them because the bass overwhelms every other frequency, why do I care if they make clicking noises while they're in the box?

I'm even uncertain if I will return them. They're expensive enough to make it worth my while, almost. I agree that I didn't pay what I would pay for a good set of over-the-ear cans, so I'm not complaining all that much. I have a lot to say, but my complaints must be taken within context that these earbuds sell just above the "bargain" brands. It may be emotionally easier to toss these in the back of the drawer and eventually throw them away when I move my office.

Caveat Emptor.

So why would I give three stars to a product about which I have so much negative to say? They are solid for the price. I keep that in mind. Many deaf millennials may want the bass. That's purely personal preference. But it's not mine. So I take one star for not meeting my expectations.

I take another for the click/snap.

They're nicely packaged. They have options. They are well-designed, if not ideally produced. Production on your day may have been better.

It's worth a shot if you're willing to send them back if they fail your experiment. If I were to give them a score, it would be a 60. I would have hoped for an 80, at least.

title: Pass on these.
text:
This is my third pair of Raycons via their website. I'm writing the review here to preserve the review.

My first pair was their E50s, which I really liked but the left randomly stopped charging. After contacting customer service and confirming all troubleshooting, they gave me a discount on another pair as I was out of warranty. I then got my first pair of Blue Fitness buds early September.

After they arrived, I felt the sound quality was great, loved the way they fit, awareness mode is a game changer, wonderful battery life, and they still worked independently which is a major need for me. Right away, I noticed some charging issues, occasionally they wouldn't charge in the case and I'd have to tap it gently a few times until the lights came on to indicate charging. No big deal since they charge quickly and it only occasionally happened, figured it was from carrying them in my pocket around the house. Then my earbuds would randomly disconnect, even when I was right next to my phone. Even had them power off without reason. Not to mention, the left earbud is meant to lower the volume and it only increased the volume. Then one day the left earbud randomly wouldn't sync to my phone, despite trying to factory reset multiple times. They'd turn on and off, but wouldn't attempt to pair to anything. I wrote in to customer service and they directed me to the link for replacement or exchange. I figured to give it one more chance before moving into another product.

This process was fairly simple. I was given a shipping label and the option to schedule as USPS too.

After receiving my new pair, I immediately put them on charge until it appeared fully charged. Paired them to my phone. They were only charged to 10%. Had to do the same gentle tap to get them to charge. This did get them to 100%, but only with careful monitoring when left on a flat surface. Same great qualities as the previous pair, but this charging issue happens every time I put them in the case. Today is my second or third day with the new pair, and I'm over it. I left them charging all day while I was out running errands to come home to them being 10% when I did the tap method to make sure they were charging before I left. For earbuds at $119, although I received them at 30% off, this is ridiculous. The great qualities mean NOTHING if they aren't functional.

title: Excellent Sound from Great Fitting Smaller Size TWS BT5 Earbuds w/ Charging Case, Rose Gold Color
text:
I love listening to music and really enjoy a great pair of ear phones to use when I walk, work around the house or read. Picture 1 shows the full set which I received with 6 extra pair of silicone eartips (deep and 1/2 height) and a USB A to C cable to charge the case. I loved the smaller size and additional eartips of this set of TWS Bluetooth 5 earbuds that are also IPX-7 Waterproof. That's better than most! These look great too.

I found using the Bluetooth 5.0 pairing connection easy to make with either my phone or iPod device. Range was as good as any without dropping out over a room away. I experienced no trouble and if the connection dropped due to distance, reconnection was automatic. These use touch controls on each earbud with a Bass Boost Mode on the Right bud (3 presses gives 2 Beeps for ON,One for OFF), a No Lag Movie Mode (4 Presses on either) and the usual volume & pause controls as well as "Voice Assistant". They were very responsive to my touch. I loved the control choices that are clearly explained on the box.

These sound crisp and clean with great mids, vocals and high end sound and excellent boosted bass. Way better sound than some buds over twice this price! Vocal tones sounded great too. I loved how they sounded and when being used with my phone and callers found my voice quality very good from the built in microphones. The sound drivers are very well tuned and give good low end sound without boost; these are not skull thumping boomers but do quite well. Even turned down very low they were good. I really liked how these sounded which is ultimately what a great pair of ear buds is all about. The comfortable fit helps also.

The instructions warn not to use more than a 5V 1A USB charging source for the case. Quote" Do not use a charger that exceeds 5V 1A. A higher powered charger may damage the battery." I did not like that as I have quite a few higher powered chargers and it is easy to use one that may damage this case. That would drop a half star but since there are no halves, I'll default to 5. They do indicate that the case won't overcharge if left plugged in, so that's good...so long as it's not a high powered charger!

I Highly Recommend these Tempo 30 Rose Gold Wireless Earbuds for Small Ears Women, Cute Pink Bluetooth Bass Boost Earphones Small Ear Canals, IPX7 Sweatproof, 32-Hour Long Battery. I think these are superb for the price and these sound excellent to me!

I hope you’ve found the information and my review helpful.

title: I'm a Cyclist
text:
Hey there, I am a road cyclist, also known as a "Roadie". These bone conducting earphones are the cats meow. I've had these for a long time now, giving them a good evaluation. I loved them the first day, first ride. Believe me, I did not think these were going to work! I was more than skeptical and prepared to return them if they didn't work to my satisfaction. I was so surprised, amazed, these are awesome!

#1. I don't even know I have them on my head. Super comfortable, they disappear. They sit super flat against your bone in front of your ear. I route my helmet strap over the top of them. They do not transmit any wind noise because they don't "catch" the wind. In other words, I put these on first, then my helmet, then my glasses. There is no interference of OpenRunPros/Helmet/Sunglasses combination. It's all good, perfect.

#2. On the downhill at 48 mph, I can hear the music clearly, no wind noise! The music is super clear, and inspiring to ride faster!

#3. They lasted my entire ride today, 6 hours.

#4. Easy to operate. On the left side, tap to pause. Double tap to skip a song. Pausing is great if you come upon another rider ahead. Tap to pause, announce Behind You, On Your Left...hello how are you, where you headed, yada, yada, yada....ok, I'm plugged into my music, I'm gonna go now....tap to unpause and on you go.

#5. Easy to operate, again! On the right side, press for volume up, or press for volume down.

#6 Charging them is the best in the world, NO dumb micro anything to wrestle with, and 9 times out of 10 have that stupid thing backwards. No, this has a Magnetic attachment. It's the first time I have ever seen this type of charging attachment. You just put the end of the charging cord near the contacts, and "whoop click!" It attaches automatically and the headphones are charging!

I wear comfortable foam earplugs, in both ears. I turn down the volume on these bone conducting OpenRunPros. I also suffer from tinnitus, a ringing in the ears. So these are perfect! Ear plugs to stop the wind and road howling. And music down low, with the balance adjusted to only one ear. I can hear traffic, cars behind me, but do not experience wind howl that caused my ears to ring. And I can still listen to all my favorite music tracks.

title: good product, terrible software.
text:
In terms of function, they're great. I can hear my surroundings while listening to music. However, it's severely lacking in quality of life improvements in the software.

Pros
+ Hear surroundings and music
+ Dual pairing works relatively well
+ Incredibly comfortable
+ Battery is more than enough

Cons
- Volume only increases in increments of 10, with no volume levels in between. This is highly irritating, as I'm often unable to correctly match my volume level with my surroundings.
- People around me can hear my music at 70+ volume.
- Sound quality is pretty bad, but it takes well to a treble boosting EQ.
- Dual pairing is only available while using the app.
- Doesn't seem to automatically turn off as long as it's connected to something.
- Does not use a common charger type.

I still think this is a good option if you want your ears open while listening to music. Hopefully some of my complaints may be fixed in upcoming updates.

title: Great hardware ruined by horrible software and horrible "features"...
text:
Overall these are great and work well and have good audio quality for what they are and how they work. Unfortunately they are ruined by horrible software and "features".

I got these and the OpenRun Mini's. The pro's fit me better. I have a big head and fairly thick neck. The mini's still fit but were pulling on the top of my ears a bit and became uncomfortable over time.

Pros:
1. You can hear everything around you while listening to music or having calls.
2. They are comfortable and stay put.
3. Audio quality is not as good as earbuds or over the ear headphones but impressive for what it is.
4. They are water resistant.
5. They have multipoint and supports multiple devices being connected at the same time.
6. They have a mute feature where you can mute the mic on the headphones themselves instead of the phone or computer, however the feature is ruined by constant beeping while muted.

Cons:
1. Auto mutes the headphones after a video call starts. You have you unmute by pressing the vol+ and vol- buttons at the same time. Sometimes it auto mutes again. There is no way to turn this feature off.
2. When muted on the headphones, they beep the whole time you are muted. Why? Who thought this was necessary and a good idea? There is no way to disable this.
3. When multipoint is enabled and 2 devices are connected, if one device disconnects the headphones beep continuously for the next 5 minutes. Why? Who thought this was necessary and a good idea? There is no way to disable this.
4. Multipoint is not enabled by default. There is no reason for it not to be enabled by default.
5. No way to update firmware on any model except the pros so you are stuck with horrible "features" and firmware you can't change.

title: Just purchased today at RunDisney Orlando Expo
text:
[[VIDEOID:6eac4eb71a3579ffda057eed0275546d]] I just purchased these today for the same price they are being sold for on amazon.com. Apparently they were just released today. I gave all three models along test lesson at the run Disney expo prior to my four days of racing. I’m doing the dopey challenge which is 48 miles of running in the next four days. This will give these new headphones a very good test. So far I believe that the new pro model sounds better than the other two models I try it out. Longer battery life, better bass and sound. A very noticeable difference in my opinion. If you are a audio file as I am I would think that spending the extra $50 is well worth it. I thought the first two models sounded quite similar and then these went Bam! Much more bass and better fidelity. The rating says that they are water resistant and sweat resistant. I will certainly be putting these through the test in the next several days. if I find any problems I will certainly get back to this review and let you know. Bluetooth pairing them to my iPhone was a breeze. There might be a small bug with the app, but it certainly didn’t seem to affect the usability so far. JS

So after running four different races with these headphones I’m still quite pleased with them. The worst thing I can say about them is that I believe the sound quality still could get better. I also feel as though there could be some adjustability on the back strap behind the head with maybe some pads or something to prop them up so that the sound speakers get positioned a little bit closer to your ear canals. If I hold it up behind my neck a little bit it sounds better. I do realize that there are many different shapes and sizes of heads and that’s why this is the case. But there’s no real adjustability with these and it seems like there could be.

One great complement as I do believe the battery does last close to 10 hours as advertised. One day I used these for at least six hours and they were turned up more than 3/4 of the way if not all the way for some time. The battery lasts quite well and they also charge very very fast. And that’s with a fairly normal USB power supply.

Don’t feel as though anybody can hear these even when they’re turned up fairly loud. I would have them turned up and regularly still startle people slightly when I run past them during races. Another very impressive thing.

When they are not on your head, they store quite easily around your neck and hold on securely. Another nice feature.

text:
I couldn't use wired earbuds anymore at work so I needed a better option. It takes a bit of practice to get used to the sensitive touch button as I'm prone to touching like a push button, if it meant extending the life of the battery a bit more by having a push-button...may it be.

As far as the battery life, it is strictly 4.5 hours! I mean almost on the dot with a full charge. I can't use both while I'm working so I can hear people around me talk, so I start the day with the left bud, then finish the day with the right bud. Since I work a 10-hour shift I'm just short of being able to use them to their full extent. I'm 45 minutes away from the end of the shift and I look at the clock and sure enough, I hear the "low battery" in the wonderful British woman accent. (Good choice on voice by the way)

The only thing I would change is to give you full control of the volume on a single bud if they both aren't active, single tap for lowering and double tap for raising. Hold for pausing and hold longer for unpausing. Maybe 3 taps for song skip? I would buy a second pair if they were like this, it's slightly frustrating when I want to raise or lower the volume (since they are independent in volume control vs the phone) to retrieve the other bud to change the level. I know they are made for both to be worn, but the tech is there :)

Very much worth the purchase, give them a try!

title: Good sound and battery life; not the most comfortable

title: Best in Class
text:
Not sure I've ever been happier with any purchase.
First you should know these are semi-in-ear buds, which is to say they don't have a any kind of tip which is inserted into your ear canal. Nor do they site entirely outside and on top of or around your ear. Instead they have a bulbous end shaped to fit the chamber of your ear lobes with a sound opening pointed at your ear canal.
Because of this, and the absence of a tight seal created by the silicon or foam tips on in-ear buds, this type of ear bud normally has poor isolation with mediocre sound including weak bass.
But this Soundpeats Trueair 2 pair, whether thru deft engineering, or blood sacrifices to strange audio gods, defies this formula. The audio quality is AMAZINGLY good. And the bass, while by no means thumping, is clear and present. These won't replace my best pair of isolating ear buds for serious music listening, but they are far better than I expected, even knowing that had the latest name brand chipset and enabled premium audio codecs like aptX.
Other major pluses include the ridiculously light weight, which aids comfort and security of these in your ear, while still having very good battery life. I presume the improved power management of the Qualcomm chipset and latest Bluetooth 5.2 iteration helps here by allowing less battery weight.
I honestly can't think of ANY minuses. Not at this already low price point. The features are already insanely great for a sub $50 set of buds.
If you're looking for a pair of semi-in-ear stem based buds, and you don't require features like ap control and custom equalization normally only available in the $150 or $200 price range, just go ahead and buy these. You won't find better without doubling your budget, if even then.

title: SoundPeats Does it Again!
text:
To start I have owned several pairs of earbuds. Out of all of them, my favorites seem to be the SoundPeats earbuds. When I am working on my laptop and doing Zoom meetings, my go to pair is always a semi-ear type. The reason is I like to be able to hear a bit of my surroundings and I have noticed when I try to have Zoom calls with earbuds that have some noise cancellation, I sound muffled and find myself talking louder than I should. I own the SoundPeats TrueAir first version (SPTA1) and have used that so much that the battery life has started to degrade. At the time, I was going to get another pair but thought I would give the Taotronics Sound Liberty 88 (SL88). The SL88 sound good but they have issues. Then SoundPeats came out with the SoundPeats TrueAir 2 (SPTA2). I immediately purchased a pair, as the SL88s were a bit frustrating. In this review, I will compare all three.

Core Specs:
SPTA1: 14.5mm drivers, BT 5.0 Chip QCC3020, IPX4, Codecs: SBC, aptX, 600mAH (case), Dual Mics, Touch Control, USB-C

SL88: 10mm drivers, BT 5.0, IPX8, Codecs: SBC, AAC, Ear detection, Smart Noise Reduction, Dual Mics, Touch Control, USB-C

SPTA2: 14.2mm drivers, BT5.2 Chip QCC3040, IPX4, Codecs: aptX, AAC, SBC, CVC Noise Cancellation, Dual Mics, Touch Control, USB-C

Build quality
SPTA1 has the best construction of a case and feels premium.
The SL88 feels like a level down from the SPTA1 and is the biggest of the three.
The SPTA2 also feels like a level down but it is also the smallest of the three, which makes it more pocketable.

Earbuds
All three earbuds are comfortable to wear. I have used all three through a full charge and never have I felt any discomfort in my ears. Another reason I like semi-in-ear buds. The SPTA2 is the smallest that makes it even more likable.

Battery Life
SPTA1: 5 hours of playtime and 30 hours with case.
SL88: 5 hours and up to 25 hours with case.
SPTA2: 5 hours and up to 25 hours with case.
All of them delivered on their estimates of 5 hours however, I do have a very frustrating problem with the SL88. For some reason it does not always charge the right earbud. I have inspected the contacts on the bud and the case and cannot understand why it does not charge when needed. Maybe I got a faulty pair.

Connectivity
I did not have any trouble pairing any of the three. The only note is that the SL88 pairs the fastest as it will pair before you can get them in your ears but both SP buds pair very quickly. On the other hand, the SPTA2 seemed to keep a connection at a longer distance with the other two about 8’ shorter. The other thing I noticed with the SL88 is that when watching videos sometimes the sound was delayed which is annoying. I did not experience the lag with either SP buds.

Controls
Both SP earbuds were decent while the SL88 I had some issues with accidental touches. I think the SL88 is a bit more sensitive.

Sound
While they all sound very good, I think both of the SP models are better especially when listening at higher levels. This is probably due to the larger drivers. The SPTA2 to me is a cut above the other two models. It had a more smooth sound without strong jumps and had very clear voice and you can identify individual sounds.

When on calls, the SPTA2 is the best of the bunch. While wearing I can hear everyone on a Zoom call very clearly. I have also had my wife wear them and see how she sounded on the other end and was impressed. That is one of the advantages I think the stem based earbuds have is that the mics are closer to your mouth.

In conclusion
Why I was impressed with the SPTA1 you can tell the SPTA2 builds on this success. If you are looking for a great pair of earbuds at an affordable price while at work listening to music and taking Zoom calls, I highly recommend these especially over the Apple AirPods as they offer better sound at a fraction of the cost.

title: Cowin Flex
text:
So this Pro version in White came with a power (USB) cord that says Cowin and when you pair it says Cowin E7, instead E7 like the old E7's (normal and pro). It also has an audio cord for a 3.5mm if you want that, but it's "so-so" quality, great if you have nothing else or an old Walkman/iPod. The body of the cans feel good, but the plastic connectors to the head band is still cheap. Also, NO CASE. My COWIN E7 Pro came with a case and this Silensys E7 Pro did not. I also paid $81.00 after tax, which is a lot for these and here is why.

Sound: This is a huge step down from the COWIN E7 base and Pro. I have the E7 Pro and my SO has the E7 base. The base model broke a while ago, which I fixed and now I wanted to get another Pro. Since COWIN isn't a name on Amazon anymore this was the replacement name. I did a side-by-side test and the old E7 is clear with a good range and bass. When the NC on the Old is turned on it works good to cancel vacuum's and/or airliner sound. The new E7 doesn't work well at all for the NC. You can hear a hiss when it's on and the sound gets very tinny when playing music. Say goodbye to bass and midrange. When not on it sounds like you are listening to music through a wall, like no low or high, just mid. It's very muffled. The old E7 didn't do that. The quality isn't in the headset anymore. You pay a premium with no usb-c upgrade and no case. Overall I am very dissatisfied. I feel conned and I am returning them immediately.

It's sad to see this happen to a great product line.

Lastly, when you turn it on the battery is stated as "Battery Full," even when at 60%. When switching between modes the sound stops from your device and a broken English voice tells you the mode you're going into, ~3-4 seconds and it doesn't pause your media device. The Old just did it and you knew from the sound cancellation quality without a loss of audio quality, not some annoyingly useless voice to tell you what you already know.

title: Volume level solved
text:
Paired with samsung TV.

These headphones have a button that disables adjusting the volume. It is located between the plus and minus buttons. It's basically like a lock button to prevent you accidentally pressing the volume and adjusting it by accident

If you press it, the volume will go off for 2 seconds and then come back. That will indicate the volume plus and minus buttons are locked and even if you press it, it won't change the volume.

If you press it again, the volume will not turn off but it will allow you to adjust the volume again by using the plus and minus buttons.

title: The incomparable Bose does it again!
text:
Bose has been and remains the best headphone maker. I’ve tried at least a dozen different products on amazon, with perhaps a dozen more in my life, and in all those experiences, the Bose name always stood far ahead of the crowd.

First, their noise cancelling technology remains the best. Eerily effective, especially on airplanes and in cars, trains, or buses, you put them on, and the world becomes quieter, making you realize how terrible the ambient noise was! These have the added benefit of adjustable noise cancellation, unlike previous models.

In comfort, these are built for long-term use, remaining wearable for hours. Most other headphones I’ve tried tend to make your ears sore, but not these! They feel soft and lovely everywhere they land on your head.

With or without Bluetooth, these offer exceptional clarity of sound, powerful bass, and clear crisp treble, none of which turn to distorted noise, even at high volumes. Yes, these are very powerful! And they offer the option for wireless battery-operated use or plug-in use. They sound equally good in either setting. As for battery life, these won’t let you down. They last hours and hours without needing a charge.

My partner has the QuietComfort 30, I believe, and I always loved borrowing those, so it’s great having a pair of my own (in an even better version, no less!)

Fantastic! No product compares to Bose.

title: What kind of idiot would pay $300 dollars for headphones? Me.
text:
Back when I used to spend my days fumbling with earbud wires, I wondered "What kind of idiot would pay $300 dollars for headphones, when you can hear your sounds perfectly fine for less than $10?". Even as these products rose more and more to popularity, I scoffed and resisted.

Those days are long gone. After I borrowed them from my friend for a day and tried them myself, I knew why. After getting them, these quickly became a non-negotiable part of my life. I use them to:

- take and receive meetings
- freely go pee, refill coffee, and wash my dishes while listening to a meeting
- go on runs while listening to music
- ignore noisy people around me
- get myself into a state of focus
- calm my anxiety on airplanes
- show people I am not interested to talk to them
- as a fashion statement

Seriously, I wear these so much I think I am developing a bald spot. Maybe that's why all the engineers are bald. The sound quality is superb, and so is the bluetooth range and connectivity. I have since tried the Sony's, Dolby dimensions, the newer model of these, but these are the best one. I have bought a pair for my whole family, and replaced my old pair when it got old without a second thought. One time, I tried my friend's airpods and almost threw up at the sound quality. Not to mention, with this size, they are much harder to lose.

These are my favorite product of the last several years (this, and the divacup) and I would wholeheartedly recommend!

title: Upgraded T10 Earbuds
text: I have the previous version of the Tranya T10 earbuds and still use them for, mainly, at the gym. I decided to buy/try the upgraded T10s before giving them as a gift. The upgraded T10s, much like the previous version, come through with easy device pairing, great sound, and plenty of battery life both in the earbuds as well as the case. The IPX7 rating ensures that any sweat or other moisture (within reason) will not degrade the earbuds. The main differences between the two versions is that the newer version does not support wireless charging and does not have a 'bass mode/boost' (replaced by 'game mode'). Charging the T10s is relatively quick with the USB-C cable and I have power to last several gym trips along with any airplane travel. The sound is balanced in my opinion....plenty of bass despite the lack of 'bass boost' in the previous version. I did find myself using the T10s for several phone calls and they performed exceptionally well. Overall, these earbuds remain a great value for the price and definitely recommend.

title: Bass is controlled.  Tight even.  Treble's even better
text: I'm not used to IEMs.. I've always either used over-ear headphones (aiwas from 20 years ago, at least)  or other decent 10 dollar earbuds like JVC marshmallows or those panasonic ones which people like.  I'd always kind of thought that it was just a given with earbuds that they will either be drowned in bass/low mid frequencies or there will be none and instead strong midrangy grindy/uncomfortable frequencies -  I've played with a LOT of really bad earbuds.  I sort of just thought because everybody's ear canal shape is slightly different, you would just have to put up with varying degrees of uncontrolled bass.  Some cheap buds are better than others in this regard.  I found those two sets I mentioned earlier were pretty consistently okay in the bass, but it wasn't really until I tried these that I realized what I was missing in terms of clear, airy highs.. It really sets up the soundstage.  It's funny, because as a turntable user, you'd think that I would demand excellence in my portable music experience (I use a pretty high bitrate lossy compression), but I just always kinda wrote it off.  I'm really impressed with this pair.  They seem well built, sound really three dimensional.  They'd be good gaming headphones.  Though I bought them for digital media, I find myself grabbing them instead of my cans when i listen to lps in bed... The high transients sound really nice as long as the volume isn't too aggressive.  One caveat.. I don't listen to a ton of modern music.  The music I generally listen to for my own amusement requires a pretty flat eq envelope.  But I did throw some Gojira through them at some point and I still think they sounded less muddy than my other headphones.

title: Unbeatable at this price point and more than worth it, but may not last years for you
text:
How I use them:
Worship leader--I use them as in-ear monitors for rehearsals and on stage during live events.

Frequency of use:
Generally twice per week, occasionally more if we have multiple events, occasionally less if I get a week off.

My take:
I was honestly blown away by the sound quality at this price point. All the other five star reviews noting this are accurate. These are so impressive that they are the goto in-ears for any new member that comes on and needs a good pair fast. Some move on from them to more expensive brands, but more and more the members of our teams get these to start and then stick with them. I think mine is the first pair to suffer any kind of failure (but I was also the first to get them, so that makes sense).

The only real con is that after about 9 or so months of twice-weekly-ish use, the wire in the cable on the right ear (for shaping around the ear) popped through. My best guess is it's a quality control issue, as opposed to me just being hard on them, only because I keep them in a hard case when not in use, and almost never use the right ear, keeping it out so I can better hear the room sound. Only once in a blue moon do I use the right ear and then only for a minute or so to get through a difficult part where I need to block room sound and be hyper focused to get something right. After it pierced through the cable sheathing, I gently removed it to keep it from snagging or poking or just tearing up the cable from the inside since it wasn't seated in place anymore. A few weeks later, the right ear didn't work at all anymore. Left side is unaffected. So at some point, I'll get another pair and see if it's just the cable that needs replacing or if the right monitor just went bad and it's unrelated to the cable, but for now I'm going to try out another model of KZs because they all have fantastic reviews and I want to see if I can find something even better for me.

I do have relatively small ears, so these are a tad bulky, but all of them are for me. I'd need to get into the super pricey custom stuff to fix that, so these aren't faulted for that in my book. They're really great in-ears.

All in all, still 5 stars because for twenty bucks I got more than 6 months worth of two hundred dollar quality. But do be aware that they probably won't last forever.

text: First time trying out IEMs, so I tried to find something that both looked aesthetically pleasing to me, and was also not expensive, as I was super unsure how how they would fit my ears. I am smol, my ears are also smol. I really love the color on these, and I was surprised by how perfect the fit was. I've been using Skullcandy earbuds for a long while now, and while they of course may not have the sound quality of something much more expensive I find that it is pretty decent, I was expecting IEMs to have better sound quality than my usual earbuds, since they generally have a more complicated build. But the sound with these IEMs when I tried them out with several of the same songs that I listen to pretty much every day I found the sound quality was just not that great compared to my Skullcandy earbuds. With my usual earbuds I can easily distinguish between different instruments being played in a song, but for some reason with these it was like the sound of the drums, guitar, and bass all just melded together, and the sound of the vocals kind of blended into the music, making the vocals and guitar sounds come out in a tin-y sort of sound, and it just...wasn't that great imo. I still love the way these look and feel in my ears though, and I will try them later for gaming and see how they sound with that and with a different device. So far have only tried them with my laptop and with music.

text: Got the TOZO A1 primarily to use with my Nintendo Switch.  Works great with the Switch…pairs with easily and stays connected, no problem.  Didn’t intend to use for music, but turns out these value-priced buds work fantastic listening to music on my iPhone.  Sure, they’re not as good as Sony WF1000XM4 or Apple AirPods Pro, but for less-than-$20 these easily outperform original Airpods.  Other positives:  USB C charging, a small/pocketable case, and decent battery life.  These are pretty small, but not teensy-tiny…about the same size as Beats Studio Buds (sound a lot like them, too; but doesn’t have nearly as much bass presence as the Beats).  The only negative I have is the “non-standard” size of the included eartip.  It’s about half the size of other buds.  And there’s only one size included (I’d estimate the size to be medium), no smaller or larger sizes are included with the package.  In summary, the A1 is a great value, good sounding option for anyone looking for decent set of backup or low-cost primary earbuds.

title: Basically perfect, fantastic wind ANC, perfect case
text:
I needed a replacement for my Galaxy buds pro's that have the fatal ANC "roar in one ear" that Samsung won't fix, and they don't stay in the ear. Bring an absolutely ENORMOUS fan of the 1more comfobuds z (the single best sleep focused earbuds at any price) I liked that these are also small, the case shape is wonderful (flip top, tiny, wireless charger) and they're relatively inexpensive.

The sound quality uses 1more's app to do a "sounds" hearing preference test. I would prefer a proper EQ option but it works well enough. I prefer real audiophile iem's and headphones, but enjoyed the Galaxy buds on bass boost, they almost hit like planar magnetics. These are about 80% there. They're totally serviceable, with the only standout being a pretty good technical performance, with genuinely solid imaging and separation. They absolutely do need the soundID set up though, I hate the stock tuning. For tiny little things they are, I am perfectly happy with the sound quality when I want music on my bike or public transit.

The ANC is stellar. They have a specific mode for wind reduction that downright curbstomps Samsung and apple. If you ride a bike, you need 1more ANC buds. The transparency mode is great too, very natural sounding. It doesn't have that "talk and it switches to transparency" gimmick, but I found it obnoxious on Samsung.

Touch controls are easily customized and no "single touch" feature means you don't accidentally press anything readjusting or putting them in. Auto pauses when you take one out, your can use just one or the other no problem

The app features depend on the product but these are meant to be usable for sleeping, do they come preloaded with a library of sleep/ambient sounds. I just use my own but it's a nice feature. I can easily fall asleep with them in and I'm a very picky side sleeper, but I do prefer the absolutely microscopic comfobuds z's.

The stock eartips did bother me a bit, they have a little ridge from the mold that irritated my ears after a few hours of use. They have a very odd mounting system that I was only able to find one option for, spinfit 1025 tips are shallow enough to fit and still let the case close (the wells for the eartips is a bit to shallow, id like it if they addressed this on a revision) so if you don't like the tips, spinfit 1025's.

The case magnets that hold the buds in are hilariously strong. Your have to SMACK it to dislodge them. Very nice detail. The case size is tiny and perfectly shaped to slide into pockets, with a flip top that you can open one handed

For being so small they also stay put well. Not perfect, but I can work out or mow the lawn, an impossible task of the Galaxy buds pro.

Overall though, these things rock. They're exactly what I need as a paramedic who also rides a bicycle. 1more is a serious brand with some seriously well thought out products at extremely competitive prices. I can sleep on my side with a podcast and still be able to wake up for a call, they crush wind nose when I'm riding my bike, they sound perfectly adequately tuned with impressive imaging (once you run the sound id feature once) and the case is (slightly too shallow recessions for the eartips aside) very nice in the hand and perfectly shaped.

Highly recommend.

title: Mini, but Mighty
text:
Look, we know you aren't here for premium sound quality if you're looking at the tiniest earbuds and in this price range. That being said, these do still sound quite nice! There's a lot of oomph for such a small package. Unless you're used to professional grade sound equipment, these will cover most anyone's sound needs.

SMALL EAR HAVERS! I have been on a quest to find comfy earbuds. So far, these have come the closest. I can wear them for like 2 hours with minimal discomfort. This is a huge upgrade from "most cause physical pain near immediately". When placed correctly, they're pretty solid. I couldn't shake them out. They did come loose a handful of times and needed to be readjusted, but in comparison to the others needing that every 5 minutes? I'll take it.

They say they have ANC, but honestly, I'm not so sure. In my personal experience, turning ANC on didn't actually cancel any noise. It just brought the bass out. Unless I just can't get the right fit, the ANC mode is effectively just a "make the music sound better" button.

The drawback here is that you can only use ANC if both buds are in. Not usually a problem, unless you want to pop one in to listen to music and leave the other ear open for communication. The make the music sound better button won't do anything with just one bud.

title: Not What I Expected From JBL
text:
I was able to verify that these worked by connecting them to my iPhone very easily. Once I knew they worked, I was very disappointed with the sound quality. The JBL system I had in my Prius some years ago was hands down the best and clearest sounding car stereo I’ve ever had. That was what I wanted and why I selected JBL. Unfortunately, I was disappointed.

The sound is very thin and reedy. There’s hardly any bass. I adjusted the EQ in my iPhone to Increase Bass, and also tried several other settings in hopes that would remedy the problem, but it didn’t. My AirPods sound far better.

Once I verified that they worked, I instructed my phone to forget them and reset them to factory settings. I had to await arrival of a Bluetooth transmitter - my tv is a smart tv, but apparently only works with Wi-Fi and not Bluetooth. I purchased a Trond V5.0 transmitter. No matter what I did, I could not get the ear buds to pair with the Trond. But then came the final nail in the coffin.

I read on a different website (I purchased these on Amazon and lines at the description closely). On the Best Buy website, someone asked about connection to a tv because they also had connectivity issues. There, JBL told the customer that these earbuds are not recommended for tv - and that was why I purchased them in the first place. If they aren’t suitable for tv, why not mention that, like, ANYWHERE in the description?

Bottom line is, if these earbuds are only useful for listening to music, I think you could get a less expensive pair that would sound better. They do seem like they are good quality, but I would much rather just stick with AirPods for music. And I’ll have to get something different for tv, because apparently, these are not low latency enough, even though the description does say they use AptX Low Latency.

title: Best single-ear set out there
text:
Been through a LOT of bluetooth earpieces in the last couple years. I finally spent the $ for the updated version of my old favorite Voyager...and was it ever worth it.

Battery life is pretty good - not as long as some out there, but with the charging case, it's not a problem. The case is a little oddly shaped, but I do like the dual indicators (for the earpiece and the case battery). The opening at the top with the second set of contacts was puzzling at first, but I suppose you could leave the case plugged in, sitting on you desk and then just set the earpiece into it. I prefer to just close it up inside each time.

Sound quality is great and even standing in the wind, friends could hear me just fine. Most were not even sure I was on a bluetooth earpiece.

I don't listen to music on this much, mostly podcasts on the way to work in the morning, so a single ear is just fine for me. I also like the fact that I can still hear traffic around me.

The flat-ish ear pieces are a little odd and don't feel very secure, but they haven't slipped at all and after a few weeks you don't notice anymore.

One piece of advice - use the original ear tips. I spent $15 on some rounder silicone ones, but they are larger than the largest Plantetonics tips and don't fit in the charging case. If you don't enclose the headset, but just set it in the top charger, then that's probably not an issue though.

I'm not going back to any other earpiece again!

title: In this case, you DO get what you pay for
text:
I give up. How do you find a decent-sounding pair of earbuds that will last at least two years? I've bought DOZENS. If they're expensive and sound great, one earbud inevitably fails. Fast. If they're inexpensive, the sound quality is so poor you don't want to use the earbuds. I thought I'd try these out to see if I could replace my expensive bluetooth earbuds whose battery just died. These have such a tinny sounding treble that I can't understand what speakers are saying (movies, music). The bass is decent and the volume gets higher than my bluetooth sets' volumes, but the sound quality is so muddy that I know I'd use these only in emergencies.

The sound also doesn't have a natural stage. The left earbud gets far more of the sound. If you increase the volume to hear out of the right earbud, the left earpiece distorts.

What a shame. I thought at this price, I'd have a backup pair of earbuds while I research a day-to-day version. But I would rather listen to nothing than struggle through trying to understand what's being said through these. Another knock against these inexpensive buds is poor fit. They keep falling out of my ears. You get only one pair of ear inserts with these, so if they don't fit your ears, you're out of luck. On the bright side, the ear inserts these buds come with pop off easily so you can try putting on other inserts--which is what I did with my now dead BT headset's comfort inserts.

Overall, I don't recommend these earbuds. The most important feature of headphones is sound quality. If the sound is so poor as to make you uncomfortable or make words unintelligible, nothing else matters about the headphones.

title: Good sound quality, sleek fit.
text:
My favorite thing about these headphones is the sleek fit. They don't stick out too far, or hang down. Sure they aren't perfectly flush with your ears but I like the design better than the Belkin Rise headphones. More about these headphones.

- Sound quality. About what you'd expect for a pair of $60 headphones. Reasonable dynamics high and low with what feels like an emphasis on the mids. They won't blow you away but for the price and the fact you're likely at the gym or a crowded space, they get the job done.
- Fit. I like the sleek nature of the design but I can see someone with smaller ears/lobes having a harder time with these.
- Call quality. About what you'd expect. Decent but people will know you aren't talking into your phone microphone.
- Runtime. 38hrs of runtime with case - 8 hours headphones only. Enough to get you through any commute or plane trip.
- Has an app and some level presets. Does anyone use that stuff?
- Case is solid with a magnetic latch.

In summary, at around $60 these will definitely get the job done. The sound quality is good and I prefer the sleeker fit as compared to other Belkin headphones. Plus lots of runtime on a charge.

title: Great earbuds
text:
These ear buds are great. They connected to my phone and computers easily and reconnecting is essentially automatic. The sound quality is extremely good. The three preset EQ settings were easy to cycle through. There was a strong bass when needed and since the ear buds do not have active noise cancelling, there is no underlying hiss. They fit well, with 3 sizes of silicone tips provided and they were completely secure. As a result, the passive noise blocking is competent and far better than a pair of the original Apple iPods I used.

In an experiment, the battery in the earbuds alone lasted for several days, using them a few hours each day. The charging case can provide about 4 recharges to the ear buds, meaning that in my regular use, I would need to recharge the case less than once a week. The USB-C to USB-A charging cord is provided, but not the adapter from a power outlet to USB-A.

The touch controls were a little difficult to use and seemed to perform inconsistently. Pausing sound was easy, but resume was not always reliable. It was easier to do it from the connected device. At times this was because I did not wait long enough, and the second touch was interpreted as another pause, but at times touches were ignored. Answering phone calls was easy and I had no trouble hearing or being heard.

One quibble is the size of the case, which is larger than I would like. This makes it extremely easy to insert the buds, but it is slightly larger than is comfortable in a pocket, where I carry it.

Overall, these are a fine set of Bluetooth ear buds that connect easily and provide high quality sound.

title: Best wireless earbuds I've owned
text:
I'm an audiophile and when I can't sit at home with my DAC and amp rigged up, these are the next best thing. The sound profile is clean and neutral, the bass is surprisingly powerful.

I bought these when my 3 year old Sennheiser Momentum TW 1.0s finally bit the dust, and this was a big upgrade. I live near downtown Minneapolis and the earbuds are surprisingly good at blocking the sound of a 8-lane highway I walk directly over on a pedestrian bridge. The earbuds are better than that older model at fewer (but still a couple) 1-2 second dropouts.

The worst thing about the Sennheiser TW 1.0 was the trapezoid, round shape that naturally would slip out between your fingers when you touch the buds or hold them. The TW 3.0's have a shape with parallel sides and there are these rubber fins used for ear-sizing and fit. Combined, these two design choices mean I've never dropped the buds onto the ground. 3 pairs of Senn TW 1.0's slipped out of my fingers and were killed on impact. This isn't an issue with these new buds.

These buds fit in my ear much better than my Pixel buds A-series, which slip out of my ear even with the largest rubber flange.

The battery life is vastly improved over the Senn TW 1.0's as well, and are better by a bit than the Pixel A-series.

I would rate these buds even better than my Entymotic ER-4P XRs that alone cost the same as the Senn TW 3.0's, but still needs a good DAC-amp to get the most out of them, an additional $100-200 cost.

The max volume on the Senn TW 3.0s are much higher than any of the other wireless earbuds I've tried. You can always crank the volume to uncomfortable levels.

title: Premium audio with a couple of downsides
text:
This is my first set of premium ear buds by Sennheiser. I prefer their over ear headphones, but I needed something more suitable and subtle for video meetings that are required for my WFH setting.

The pros that come to mind:

-Noise cancelation. I currently have a personal server running 24/7 in my office, and it sounds like a small plane engine. These ear buds completely eliminate the shrill whirring. The clicks of a mouse and keyboard keys are still faintly audible from time to time, though.

Sound quality - The sound stage on these is fantastic. There is a little sacrifice to the quality of sound with it being an in-ear device (think sounding a little compressed and less spatial in a way), but the mids are warm and the highs are crispy (sometimes in a way that feels like your skull is getting a nice scratch, so if that's too much you can adjust in their app). The bass is fairly restrained by default, but you can adjust that in the app as well. If you like music that is bass-heavy, these might not be the best fit for you.

Controls - the controls are simple, and I love that they can be customized to my preference in the app. The auto-pause to music when taking out the right ear bud is a huge plus for me!

Cons:
The ear bud tips - the M3s come with various sized ear buds, but unfortunately (for me anyways) they get pretty uncomfortable after about 4 to 5 hours of wear. I wound up switching to aftermarket bud tips as I found myself fiddling with the buds in my ears a lot to the point where the inside of my ears started to chafe. The other issue is that the ear pieces will slowly come loose or fall out if you are talking or eating with them in. I primarily use the M3s for stationary/desk work, so this isn't the biggest dealbreaker, but I don't feel that they would be ideal for use with working out or any activity where you're moving around (or talking) a lot.

Bugs - The M3s were a little bit of a pain to initially get connected to the app, but once they were set up I have had no issues there. The app immediately prompted firmware updates once connected. The only problem I seem to have is that if I take a phone call and hang up my left ear bud will stop working, or the noise cancelation will stop doing its thing temporarily. I have to return both of them to their case and reconnect them to my Bluetooth for both the left ear bud and noise cancelation to work again. Hopefully this is fixed in a future update.

Overall, I've been very happy with the M3s, and they get pretty heavy use from me. I've been consistently wowed by the quality of sound these bad boys put out! Perhaps one day Sennheiser will come out with some comfort ear tips, but in the meantime I continue to be pleased with my purchase.

title: Not A Good Fit For Me
text:
I’ve been using the 1MORE Stylish True Wireless Earbuds for almost 4 months now (July 2019). Based on the video reviews I watched, I really thought I’d like them. Unfortunately my experience has not been the same as most of the reviewers. The volume is not an issue for me. I do not need to blast my music or podcasts. The battery life has been good enough for what I use them for (cutting the lawn, listen to podcasts while the wife watches her programs on TV). The charging case is great when traveling. The big problem I have is w/the fit. I cannot get the earbuds to fit properly & seal correctly in my ears. I have tried all possible combinations of the ear pieces in the box. Because of this, there is no noise cancellation. Besides the mower being heard loudly, I can hear the television when my wife watches it. If I put in my wired Sony earbuds or my Phaiser BHS-730 BT earbuds, I cannot hear the television over what I’m listening to. The 1MORE earbuds also fall out when I’m moving around. When mowing the lawn, they’ll fall out multiple times.
From my experience, I cannot fully recommend the 1MORE Stylish True Wireless Earbuds. I’d suggest you try to find a pair & see if they fit your ears first. If not, be sure you can return them if they do not fit correctly.

title: The clear best buy for audiophile sound quality & battery life
text: If something approaching audiophile quality sound  is critical (or you primary reason for purchase), the 1More Stylish True Wireless earbuds are a best buy.  You have to spend 3 times the price (for the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless) to get earbuds that sound as good or better than the 1More Stylish.  Period.  Nothing else on the market even comes close.  Treble is crisp and bright.  Mid range sounds are smooth and rendered with nuance.  Bass is true and tight.  And the 1More Stylish battery life is impressive (and far better than that of the Sennheiser Momentum).  Audio talk quality is also quite good - no noise cancellation - but not quite as good as recognized top performers such as the Apple and Sony.  People on the other end of the conversation have told me my voice comes through clear and undistorted. There are a few things that could stand some improvement, however.  First and foremost is fit.  These tend to fall out of my ear; changing to the largest eartips helped, but I still need to be a bit more careful than I think I should need to be.  Secondly, some level of water-resistance would be nice; currently there is no IPX rating at all so these may not be the best choice for wear while exercising.  Third, I would like the controls to be easier to engage.  Lastly, the manual needs a complete overhaul; the print is so small and the ink color/saturation so light that it is unreadable.  All in all, however, these earbuds can't be beat at their price point (approximately $100).

text:
INTRO:
Been looking for TWS earbuds for a bit now, since I've been tired of having to untangle and fumble with my current IEMs' cable multiple times everyday. They sound good enough for my use of mostly podcasts when I'm on the go and music for when I'm studying, but most importantly they're comfortable and isolate around 7-8/10. I've gotten a $50 budget pair, these, and a $130 pair so far (will have reviews for all of them). Looking for the aforementioned comfort, good isolation, and sound that doesn't noticeably offend.

SOUND:
Probably the best out of the bunch, fun punchy bass was all I really noticed on first listen. Didn't care to really sit down and analyze these like I would headphones or IEMs that I use at home. Most wireless earbuds I've tried so far have a background hissing that I really really dislike, but these didn't. To be expected of a company that actually does well for itself as a low to midrange budget company.

FIT/SEAL:
I used my own single/triple flange eartips. Obviously triple flanges isolate the best, but they were a bit uncomfortable in ear (these are comfortable on my daily drivers) and you won't be able to charge the buds without taking them off. Most of my single flanges fitted on about the same, but also didn't isolate that well. Like a 7/10 at some frequencies, and a 4-5/10 with almost all other noise. The "wings" worked sometimes but would pop out every so often. They didn't make the earbuds unstable in my ears, but simply didn't add to the experience.

LOOKS:
I don't like when the body of an earbud sticks out unnaturally, but these look very natural, reminiscent of the old bluetooth earpieces that I would see businessmen walking around with. However I think this is where the lack of isolation comes from, because only the eartips are working on isolating outside noise.

CHARGING/BATTERY-LIFE:
I used these for a few days and they were at low battery (<30 minutes) because I presumed that they were at least ~50% charged (my mistake here). Case is plastic but still looks nice, and the buds just click in magnetically. Charge time is listed as 85 minutes, but I didn't keep track of it because I don't think I'd ever use these for 6 hours straight, and I always have classes that are ~80 minutes or more where I can just leave these charging if I wasn't managing the battery life well. After a full day of listening I got a "medium battery life" left. (The earbuds will tell you how much battery life is left, but I was also able to see a small bar next to the bluetooth symbol on my phone that gave me a relative sense of where my battery was at) So that was roughly 3-4 hours of listening.

CALLS:
I don't get calls too often, but it is nice to have the option to quickly take a call by pressing once on the button on top of the bud. Sound quality according to my friend was decent enough, but picks up background noise (obviously shouldn't expect too much from something that has to sit on your ears and pick up your voice).

BUTTON:
The button is nice for play/pause, but sadly doesn't have an assistant feature (the $40 buds did). I found myself accidentally pushing it during the first day when I was trying to adjust the fit and insertion of the tips. The button is nice and tactile, without requiring too much force. Location is good because you can use it with 2 fingers to get a solid push without moving the buds much at all (a problem I had with the $130 option).

VERDICT: Won't be keeping, but had a lot of promising high quality pieces that would make this great for someone that wants to hear the environment around them. Comfort was okay, but I wasn't able to get the "wings" to work for my ears. Sound quality is great for wireless bluetooth, and is to be expected from a company that's already made a few good IEMs.

title: Finally! Great sounding earbuds that stay put!
text:
I've reviewed more than a few sets of earbuds for Amazon through their Vine program. Some were quite inexpensive, some, not so much. My chief complaint with virtually all of them boils down to FIT. The darn things just don't stay lodged in my ear canals. I've even tried using those pricey memory foam ear tips. Those tips help, but then most buds don't fit in the charging case with them in place.

I just purchased these 1More Stylish earbuds and am really pleased with them. I was attracted to them for their claim that they would fit and stay fit... and they're close to perfect for me. I've not even changed the tips that came with them out of the box and have used them for several hours. Only occasionally do they feel like they will come out and a gentle push re-secures them. Only once did one fall out unexpectedly while I was on a long walk. For me, this is remarkable, almost a world record.

How do they sound? Great - the highs are high, the lows are low without being forced. Podcasts sound natural and music is a joy. I listen to an eclectic mix of jazz, classical and 60s & 70s rock and it all sounds great. I read several reviews about these and only one complained that they distorted the bass frequencies. Not in my ears - if anything, they put the bass track back where they belong - in the background, well balanced and appropriate, but not predominant. There is no noise cancellation working here other than the tight fit that blocks out exterior sounds.

My best earbuds for sound prior to these 1Mores were the Jabra 65T.... they were natural and well-balanced, but wouldn't stay in my ears for more than a couple of minutes. You should have seen me crawling under my seat in coach on a trip to London, trying to retrieve the earbud that rolled under me - in the dark. Nice sound, but who cares if you can't wear them? These 1Mores are at least as great-sounding as those Jabras at a much better price.

Complaints? Sure - they're not perfect - I know of no earbuds that have zero weaknesses. Here's my short list:

- Case: it's a bit large, considering the size of the buds themselves. You're not going to slide these into your jeans unless you wear those jeans really loose.

-Charging: there is no indicator telling you the charge level of the case, itself. When you take the buds out of the case, you get this cool "1More" music jingle, then a message telling you the charge level ("Battery High".) Fine - the buds get charged every time you use them and put them back into the case. But there's no way to tell you that the case is getting close to empty until you take the buds out and get a message other than "Battery High." Now, these are $100 earbuds, so I don't expect frills and lace, but some sub-$30 earbuds have charge level indicators on their case.

- Manual: skimpy at best, there's no troubleshooting information and their website needs a major upgrade to be supportive. The manual is awful - light grey letters of the tiniest font printed on glossy paper. Bring your own magnifying glass, 'cuz you're gonna need it

- Support: not terribly responsive. I read that there was a firmware update and downloaded the app from the Google Play Store. I ran it and lost all the sound in one channel - whichever one connected to blue tooth last. I reached out to 1More support a couple of times. I called them and got the ever-popular "COVAD19 excuse" for not being available. It took them a couple of days to get back to me, but their email solved my issue.

Wrap-up
I really like these. The sound is really good for me - on a par with the really expensive Jabras I had but sold on Ebay. (Damn things just wouldn't stay in my ears!) They're not overly large and don't make me look like a freak when I wear them.

title: 300 Dollars Though?
text:
While I am impressed with these headphones, I cannot find anything to justify the price point.

They feel good on my ears. I usually don't wear over the ear headphones but haven't had any comfort issues. I like that there is an application where you can customize the equalizer (among other things). I'm more of a bass kinda gal so I appreciate being able to turn it up. I also like that I can control the volume and skip songs straight on the headphone so I don't have to fool with my phone.

I like the way they look but they aren't very "trendy" they are literally the same color throughout the product. I'm wondering if they are trying to appeal to an older customer base. The single color does look clean.

A big plus for me that it uses the same charger as the Samsung S10 so I know I will be able to charge them wherever I charge my phone such as my car or work desk.

Overall, a nice headphone but you can get something very similar at a fraction of the price.

title: Jabra 85h head-to-head with Bose 35
text:
If you’re looking for unmatched sound reproduction in a very quiet music room, neither the Bose 35 nor the Jabra 85h is competing in that studio monitor class.

These are yeoman everyday transit use with great sound quality. It’s the noise cancelling depth that shuts out the chaos that makes the two exceptional. Ambient sustained engine/crowd noise will wear you out. That’s what makes noise cancelling central for me.

Noise cancelling – Jabra is the first headphone experience every bit the equal with the Bose 35. Other noise reduction players competing in the price bracket don’t come close. The Jabra and Bose cancellation are different. Audible net cancellation is so close to the same that I can’t discriminate. Bose noise cancelling has a sort of over-pressure feeling that I don’t notice in the Jabra. It’s not a discriminator or fatigue element either way for me. If you know what I mean, you will notice it.

Bass – Jabra by a hair

Treble – Jabra wins

Clarity – Bose by a hair

Comfort – High personal importance for air travel. Bose passes the 8-hour flight test. I believe the Jabra will too.

The Jabra 85h is incredibly impressive. It’s a competitive break-through from my perspective. The same price range as Bose 35. Overall the same with very subtle differences that make a winner impossible to my ear. I’d need an acoustics lab to compare the 2 in detail and that degree of detail would be irrelevant for me or the typical user in the price bracket.
Nobody’s going to go wrong with the Jabra 85h. Bose has the first genuine competitor in the price range. That’s good for everybody.

title: My New Daily Use Headphones
text:

title: Nicely done
text:
I'm not an audiophile, so sadly I'd recommend looking at another review for details on the audio quality of these headphones. I personally think it's great, but I have aged ears and just want to be up front about that.

I think what has really made me warm up to these headphones is that I can tell a lot of effort went into some of the more subtle features of the headset. For example, you turn them off by twisting the headphones so you can lay them down flat. Turn them back to the 'over-the-ear' position and the headphones come on. Not only that, but when you put them on a voice tells you how much battery you have left. To put it another way, unlike my other wireless headphones, I don't have to find the nearly-invisible button to activate them. I think the noise-cancelling is good, too.

If I had one criticism it's that when you use the smart-phone App to configure the headphones they throw a term or two at you about how to configure them that is a little odd, to me anyway. They describe the configuration of your headphones as 'moments'. As I understand it, a moment is just a snapshot of an area you're in so the app/headphones can determine optimal settings. The settings would be different in your home vs. in a bus vs. walking in the park. Why 'places' or 'environments' wasn't chosen... search me. But that's just a teeny tiny criticism about their choice of words, not a flaw or anything like that. Overall it works fine.

Nicely done!

title: Not entirely thrilled
text:
While these are generally good, I found three things I don't like.

They aren't comfy. My Corwin cheapies are more comfortable for long-term wearing.

They don't block sounds as well as I wanted. I am listening to legal proceedings for transcript editing, and I need to be able to hear without background noise . Even at the highest level of sound blocking, environmental sounds still break through. I'm not saying they don't help. Maybe my expectation of "sound blocking" is too high. I just wonder if for the price there isn't another that is a little bit better.

Finally, you can only connect them via Bluetooth to your phone, not your laptop. As a result I am tied to my computer by a cord connection. That is really a problem. I cannot even check the battery level without disconnecting from the computer cable and connecting to the phone. I don't know if that is the same in other products in the same price point, but I'd definitely check. It never dawned on me that that might be a problem. Guess that's my failure to research.

If I had to spend what is for me a lot of money on another pair of headphones, I would not purchase these again.

I only had one complaint with my new QuietComfort Earbuds, sometimes one would fall out of my ear, and mine (being both small and black), we’re sometimes hard to locate.

I ordered the “1+“ size and the “0” size earbuds. I found the “0” size earbuds to fit me perfectly. They create a much better,(and more comfortable), seal between the earbud and the ear. In addition to the more comfortable fit, the “0”, Sized Earbuds do a better job at sealing out unwanted noises, and increases the quality of sound heard through the earbud. The size “0” both Fit and Sound Better than the smallest, (size “1”), earbuds, originally included with the QuietComfort Earbuds New!!!

It is too bad Bose didn’t include this size earbud in the box along with the physical earbud which these earbuds “wrap around”, to create the different sizes. However, I am happy that an earbud in my size is available, at an affordable price, provides the benefits described above, plus, my earbuds now never fall out anymore!!!
