title: Game changer for all day work!
text:
I was reluctant to try but after hearing a friend's rave reviews about a certain name brand version of a bone conduction headset I was compelled to give it a shot. I wasn't willing to go whole hog given the price, but after a lot of research I narrowed it down and purchased these.

I'm just going to lay it out... these are PURPOSE BUILT.

One must have reasonable expectations of the technology. One must match their specific purpose with this solution for it to work.

PROS:
1) They are comfy, It takes some getting used to, but after a day or so, you hardly notice they're there. It can get a little sweaty but not any more than say wearing a pair of sunglasses. Still they're lightweight and you'll hardly notice you're wearing them.
2) I wore these for 9 straight hours on and connected to my laptop. By the time I turned them off they were showing nearly full battery power left. Granted it was a slow day and I didn't have much in the way of meetings but it beats having to charge them midday. I imagine on a busy meeting day I'll be cutting it much closer or will need to top it off at lunch. But hasn't been that way yet.
3) The audio is not bassy or broad, but I get clear meeting audio and do not want for more. It is not hifi and won't do justice to music or movies or the like, but figure if you needed to make a phone call, or listen to an audio book or podcast, or if you have zoom meetings all day, this fits the bill. It's like listening to an in ear headset but with nothing on your ear pressing down on it. It also does not obstruct any external noise. I can still hear the sizzle while I'm cooking.
4) The range is impressive and connection is stable. I'm able to go anywhere in the house even on different floors and I stay connected and the audio doesn't clip or stutter.
5) Controls are easy to find and use. Pairing was also easy.

CONS:
1) Like I mentioned before the audio isn't great so it won't replace all your headsets/headphones/earbuds, just the ones you use for whatever you need it to do.
2) At high volume the transducers vibrate on your temples and tickle some. It's like having a broken woofer cone on a speaker except its pressed to the side of your head. Just gotta remember to turn the volume down or perhaps turn down the bass balance on your audio device.
3) Proprietary charging cord. As much as I like the magnetic cable (how easy it is and that there's no jack to wear out), the fact that I must have THIS cable to do the charging is a worry, but since I keep everything work related with my work stuff its not a problem for me.
4) I do wish they were "louder". You can cheat a little and place the transducers right over your ear canal but they're still not as loud as speaker based headphones. In my home office, they're fine. Hanging out outside in a busy neighborhood, no big deal. In a noisy restaurant, its a challenge, for me at least.
5) Lastly, they don't do a great job of noise cancellation. Your audience will be able to hear everything. And my office which does have a little echo... well that echo comes through in these.

CONCLUSION:

I'm pleased with these as they're comfortable and make work communications and audio easy. I will be using these as my primary headset as they're the only ones I can wear all day and not notice. I've got my old Jabra earbuds as a standby in case I'm going to be in a noisy environment but in most cases that can be helped.

I did have a pairing issue but the seller's CS got back to me immediately and solved my problem faster than I could have asked for.

For the price I could not have asked for more and have no regrets!

text:

My wife got a fancy bone conducting headset and I resisted since I already have too many of these devices but the calling was simply too much. I decided not to spend a fortune as I wasn't sure I would like them. I got these and like them, but don't love them. Things I like:
1) Allows you to hear things around you while wearing them
2) Good for driving - people say the sound quality on their end is good (not always the case)
3) Light weight
4) Sound quality is okay. These are not meant for high quality sound for that, look elsewhere. Even the cheapest ear buds have better sound. But that's a product of the design, not a flaw.

Things I am not in love with:
1) The charger is non-standard. I get it -these are water proof but I really wish companies would all go with something standard (USB-C?) OR that they would include a 2nd charger cable
2) There was no charging block. I really hate the assumption that everyone has extra charging blocks. This isn't the first item I have gotten that lacks a block
3) The fit seems a little tight - maybe I have an exceptionally big head?
4) The sound quality - see above. These are good for the car, for walking around and maybe running or other exercise, but not for tuning out the rest of the world or for getting good quality sound.

If these are what you want, this is a good set which won't set you back major bucks.

title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
text:
The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life. Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.

I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house. When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.

So far, I have not found a good one. The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction. It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear. There is no bone shaking going on. With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.

In addition, there is a half-second delay on these headphones meaning they are no good for watching videos. I have not experienced bluetooth delay in quite a few years so I wasn't expecting it. Further, there is no charging light, meaning there is no way to tell if they are charged or not.

Then there's the price they are charging for this thing. Everything is just NO.

title: Excellent choice for water sports and for safety purposes
text:
PROS

1. These headphones are really different in appearance from regular earbud-type headphones, but they are oddly attractive in their design.

2. They are great for swimming in a pool or in any outdoor body of water, because they are extensively waterproof. They can be submerged to a depth of 20 meters (65 feet). This means they can be used for snorkeling and scuba diving.

3. They do not fit in the ear. Instead, sound is conducted through the cheekbone. I don’t understand the science behind this, but it does work.

4. They have the ability to play audio files from a built-in 32GB memory card.

5. When not submerged in water, they have Bluetooth capability. When underwater, you have to use the built-in memory card.

6. This type of headphones are outstanding for safety purposes. People who walk, jog or run on public sidewalks or, especially, on deserted park paths/trails, are taking a big risk if they have their ears plugged with regular Bluetooth earbuds such that are not aware of sounds around them that could signal danger (e.g., a bike speeding down the park trail, careless skaters or skateboarders sharing the sidewalk and, worst of all, muggers).

6. A built-in microphone allows you to use the Bluetooth function to place and received calls on your cell phone.

7. These headphones are lightweight, durable, and flexible.

CONS

1. Other than for water sports and for safety purposes, these headphones are not as good as regular earbuds, because their sound quality is comparatively quite inferior.

2. Compared to regular Bluetooth earbuds, their price is very high.

title: Generic earbuds in a strange case
text:
I've reviewed many low cost, generic earbuds, and what sets these out from the rest is the somewhat strange case.

While most earbuds come in a more familiar case - a box with a lid. You open the lid, and the earbuds are inside, charging (if the case is charged).

This case is different - it's a cylinder. You turn the cylinder to expose the earbuds, one at a time. When each earbud is exposed, you can take it out (or return it to the case when you're done using them). I've discovered that it isn't particularly hard to accidentally move the case to expose the earbud. So far, none have escaped from the case, but carrying it in a purse or pocket could possibly expose an earbud if the case turns to expose the earbud.

Sound was good - not great.

title: Decent components, poor execution
text:
Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.

text:
My Bluetooth earbuds kept falling out when I tried to listen to music in bed. And, I certainly didn’t dare fall asleep while using them. I finally decided to get something more secure. Control is easy:
+ Press the middle button to power on or pause.
+ Press the left button to raise and the right button to lower the volume.
+ Hold down the right button for the next track and hold down the left button for the previous track.

Overall, this is a good headband style headphone for this price and I have really enjoyed and recommend them.

title: The Moondrop Chu is dead. Long live the new king.
text:
Well the Moondrop Chu's reign didn't last long. These WILDLY outclass everything under $50. They wildly outclass a lot of stuff under $200.

For starters, detachable cable. I hate the fixed cable on the moondrop chu's with a passion - it's all silicone rubbery and tangles, doesn't stay in place, doesn't stay tied up in your pocket or backpack. The chu's come with a microphone, which is the only thing it has going for it, but if you REALLY need a cable, these are still a far better deal with another $10 spent on the cable. This cable is nice, comfortable, wraps up easily around 3-4 fingers and stays coiled properly.

Then, eartips. The Chu's "springtips" don't really fit quite a few people, myself included. They were so bad that the chu's sounded downright broken until I got some better tips on them. The Zero's come with about five different size of tips that were no problem to find a comfortable seal/fit.

Comfort and build wise, they're awesome. My ears can be quite picky, and they basically disappear in your head. They're light and smooth plastic, with a nice stainless steel plate on the outside. No complaints, they just work perfectly as IEM's and feel plenty durable to just live in your backpack.

Sound wise, these things really up the game. The Chu's have excellent technical performance (detail is great) but they're downright claustrophobic. It feels like every instrument in the band is licking the inside of your ear. And it's unpleasant. They're tuned quite neutral, but with no sense of space, instrument separation or imaging (that sense of more than left/right, but front/back and in between) they're just not a pleasant sound. The Zero's have IMPRESSIVE separation and imaging. Not impressive at $20. Impressive for IEM's, period. There's $300-500 stuff that doesn't do imaging and soundstage this well.

The bass could be cleaner and it doesn't quite hit the detail of the chu's (which are also punching well into the $500 range in that one specific area) but I'm nitpicking HARD. For $20, these have no right sounding so spacious, detailed (you can enjoy the detail a lot more when the instruments don't feel all laid on top of each other) and pleasant. They're not overly bassy, but they are thumpier than the chu's. No overly sparkly either. Just a very "grown up" tuning meant to make music sound nice, paired with truly outstanding soundstage.

If you play video games, there's nothing anywhere near these in the price range. You'll hear sounds ahead, behind, and how far away they are.

Songs with real detail and separation will dance around you (Bobby McFerrin, Polyphia) and show you things you didn't even know were in your music.

The only next step up I can think of from these is the $50 Truthear zero's (same model name, different brand) but they're only marginally better (with a slightly worse fit) and the $100 7hz diokos are a very noticeable step up in every way. But jeez. These things are $20. I don't understand how they're so good for that little money.

Anyone else entering the $20-$50 space better bring their A+ game. These are a tough act to follow. If you really need a microphone, these are still unbeatable with another $10-15 for a cable with one.

Some reviews talked about the headband having to be charged after 8 hours. I only charge mine a couple/few times a week. I do make sure it is off in the morning. Syncing it to my iPhone was super simple. The enclosed directions made it easier than pairing with my car. Once paired, I have not had to redo. The sound quality is fine. I like that I can still hear what is happening around me, but it is does not disturb my bed partner.

title: Don’t even bother. OK for podcasts in dead quiet environments. Comfortable with glasses.
text:
Bought these because they were highly rated for people who wear glasses. They’re comfy enough, but the sound quality is trash and volume is nonexistent unless you turn it all the way up and press them against your head. I decided to return them because while trying them out in public, I got out of my car in a Walmart parking lot and immediately couldn't hear them, even at full volume, just due to the ambient noise (slight breeze, traffic, semi idling across the way, etc.) They just completely got drowned out.

I bought them so I could listen to podcasts at work without disturbing others and without having to have one AirPod in, which gives me a feeling of unbalance that I was hoping not having either ear obstructed would solve. These are fine for that in a DEAD QUIET environment. At about 3/4 volume on the iPhone, I can hear clear enough and they’re not going to disturb anyone. I could have it at about 50% and other people would never know I was listening to anything. Any louder and others can hear a little buzzing. But again; as soon as you consider the air conditioning or whatever, you won't be able to hear them.

For $50, I’m not sure you can do much better. I’m interested in seeing how the more expensive brands compare. These are TERRIBLE for music. Don't even bother.

Another reviewer said these go on your cartilage (your tragus) - they do not. They go on your temple right in front of your tragus.

I wish they were just a LITTLE tighter. Maybe if I lose some weight there’ll be less fat to buffer the sound and they’ll sound better… I feel like if they were just a little tighter, the volume would increase significantly as well as the sound quality. I'm not sure how comfortable they'd be if you left them on/in for several hours, though, if they were tighter.

Overall, whether it's the technology or this exact implementation of the tech, they just don't work well.

title: Hearing impaired specifics reviewed
text:

title: AWESOME
text: I have the ZSN, ZSX, and ES6. I also have headphones, T50 and T40RP MK3, HE 400i, and WS1100si. I have a Jotunheim connected to a Topping D70. These sound better through this than my phone, Note 9. After listening to these for three days I have done this review. You must understand that earphones are more sensitive than headphones. You must have good recordings, I use FLAC 44.1 BY 16 and 24 BY 96. My Jotunheim and D70 might seem over kill but, they do sound better through them. These little drivers pick up EVERYTHING. Even the noise floor of my Emotiva A-100. What you put into them, you get out of them. It is that simple. Cables with different impedance can effect them. Seriously, try them with different amps and DACs. You will be surprised. I listen to metal and classical music. Sure the equipment I have is over kill for these but, try something different besides a phone. I read all the time how headphones and earphones sound like crap. Well, my T40RP MK3 sounds like crap through a phone. Needs more power. I speaker needs to POWERED. Your amp is the ENGINE that powers it. Better engine, better sound. Does not have to expensive however. I'm 58 and retired. I have heard ALL KINDS of systems. I have very little money, so I don't buy without doing research. These are not expensive so I gave them a try. I'm glad I did. Movies sound good too. Yes, I have took care of my hearing and I have good hearing. I can still hear I watch tick. I have a self winding one. You can't go wrong for the price. Take them to a friend's house and plug them into a good DAC and amp. You will be surprised I'm sure.

text:
I wanted so badly to like this, but I just can't. First off, if you have a sleeping partner, this things has a blinking light the entire time it's in operation. FIne for you because you can't see it, but your partner won't appreciate it very much. Strike one. So I tried it on and after figuring out I could slide the earbuds along the cloth channel, tried to lay down. The earbuds are not low-profile enough and dug into the side of my head, but it wasn't too bad so I thought "meh, I can live with that."

It turns out, I couldn't live with that. This is because there is no earthly way to adjust the mask to where it's covering my eyes and the earbuds are covering my ears at the same time. It may be my head shape or it may be a design flaw, but I could NOT comfortably position the earbuds to cover my ears without having to push the eyemask either up off my eyes or down below. As my ears are pretty much normally aligned with my eyes (I took drawing classes--I know the proper alignment and ratio, LOL), I would say it's some sort of design flaw. And the earbuds are still uncomfortable to lie on. Strike two.

But the coupe de grâce, or the straw that broke the camel's back was the fact that, as others have mentioned, a voice comes on unexpectedly to yell "Connected!!!!" at highly inopportune times--multiple times. A very bad feature for something purported to help you sleep.

I'm just lying there, about to drift off, and "CONNECTED!" Whaaaa??? I *was* connected, thankyouverymuch. Now I'm awake and angry. Strike three, you're going back.

They seem to say in my ears when I am stationary, but if I walk they seem to work themselves loose which is annoying - they never get to the point where they have fallen out, but they require readjusting every few minutes. They are not uncomfortable though, they just work loose. I have the ear hooks installed but they don't help much. For the money, they are decent.

Update - Thanks to the suggestion from the seller, I changed out the tips for the smallest ones (which I did not think would fit as well as the medium) and they now stay in better. The drawback is that I cannot fit the ear hooks with the smallest tips. I think a molded design incorporating the ear hooks would be better in my opinion, though fit is going to be unique to every person. With the small tips, I can still only use them for walking, I would not run with them since they will work loose too often and when the tubes bump something they make noise. I might buy these again since they do what they claim and sound decent for audiobooks (since I don't expect greatness from $20 headphones).

title: Nearly Great
text:
There's a lot to like here, but ultimately it was uncomfortable enough for me to send it back. I'm comparing this with the SteelSeries Arctis 9X. The sound quality and direction are great in both headsets.

Some differences which were important to me:

The Good:
The Stealth uses USB-C. The Arctis uses micro USB.
The Stealth uses a rigid mic boom and swings up out of the way to mute. The Arctis uses a flexible wire boom and has a button (and a red LED indicator when muted) to mute.
There is an iOS app which lets you manipulate settings and such.
Updating the firmware on my Mac was easy.
I experienced only slight connection issues during gameplay compared with the Arctis.

The Bad:
The band across the top is quite firm and after a ~2 hour session was uncomfortable.
The ear cups press in on my head to a level which caused sharp pain towards the end of a ~2 hour sesson.
The Arctis has no iOS app, and the Mac app does not support the latest OS.

Ultimately I kept the Arctis, because the Stealth's were actually painful to use. If they had been more comfortable they beat out the Arctis, IMHO, in every other way.

title: Finally found a wireless earclip style headset to can replace my Phillips earclips!
text:
So for over 15 years I exclusively bought Phillips Earclip(over ear) headphone. Before they discontinued them I bought two pair for safe keeping. About 3 years ago I had to open my last box. I NEVER bought a inner ear head set because I already knew they wouldn't fit and be uncomfortable! So I've been randomly and hoping for a wireless version of my Phillips ear clips and had no luck. Until recently a few months back I took a chance on Koss which I already knew would not be worth the price. But got them anyway and although sound was ok, the ear clip was way too flimsy and the speaker piece was uncomfortable you can feel the plastic through the sponge cover.
Now these F2'S they are to closest I've found to the Phillips! They fit very comfortably around the ear including the speaker over the ear. Now as far as battery life I haven't used them long enough to see how long they last. But they've been in the case for about 4 days now and the case itself is still going.
My only issue so far is the sound quality could be improved. My Phillips has a well balanced sound and I still use the one pair I still have for mixing music on my laptop!
Soon I want to make a comparison video of the 3 ear clip headphones I mentioned! Now if these continue to work I've the next few months I'll update me review. And although the sound is a lil so so for my taste, at the moment is But these again and actually plan to buy a set for my mother when a few extra dollars! If this company upgrades F2's I'd love to rep them because I truly love this style of headphones and right now their so hard to find!

title: A blessing for dealing with migraines
text: While I do use this, with or without sound, as a regular sleep mask, I primarily got it for migraines. Depending on how I feel, I can use it to listen to a book, to white noise or gentle music to help soften the racket from barking dogs, or just as a mask. It's cool on the face, and a bit warm on the ears (which I like, since mine are always cold), and has very soft padding around the eyes so it doesn't cause pressure points. It does sometimes press on my nose in a way that makes me feel slightly stopped up, but I can usually adjust it well enough to minimize that. The little speakers are flat enough that, properly aligned, they don't hurt my very tender ears. I can't speak to the sound quality for music since I mostly either use them for audio books or white noise, but they're fine for that. Once of the best migraine-mitigation products I've ever found!

title: Nice Secondary Sleep Mask for Features
text:
I was as skeptical with the sound quality as the rest of you. I recently purchase Airpods 2 so my standards were stupidly skewed. But actually... it's ok. It's better than you would expect, not great but not too bad. The earpieces are tucked within the ear mask so you can position it so it rests over your ears as loosely or tightly as you'd like it. You can set up some white noise and it'll work just fine. The blackout quality of the mask is very good, blocking out any light when I have it on comfortably on my face. My primary cheap face mask has a ton of light leak, but this one I would use for sensory depravation or sleeping in the daytime.

One of the features to rate is noise cancelling - it is noise cancelling insomuch as holding a loud pair of speakers next to your ears, drowning out anything softer than it. There isn't any.

Now why it's my secondary and not my primary. The design resembles that of a headband that goes over your eyes and ears - and my ears get warm quickly. As someone who prefers earbuds over headphones, having my ears covered just changed my comfort level too much to fall asleep. If you can't fall asleep with headphones or earmuffs on, this won't work for you. If you live in a cold climate with no money for heating, it'll help your glasses-holders warm and cozy.

The other goofy design is that the power, forward and back buttons are around the bottom of your forehead when you have it on. The buttons are clicky too, so pick your playlists wisely. Otherwise you'll be the day-napping person who occasionally jabs at a button against your forehead. The tube-top like design also means it will slip off your melon head during normal toss and turn. I suppose if you secured the mask securely enough, it won't budge and I won't judge.

title: Blocks light well, easy to pair and use, very soft
text:
I enjoy going to sleep listening to music, and recently I've started using a sleep mask, so I thought this would be the perfect solution.

The mask is very soft.

it is not a 3D mask where your eye lashes don't touch when you open your eyes. Hard to know that for sure from the listing.

There are thin speakers in the part of the mask that covers your ears. At first I didn't think this was a big deal, but I woke up in the middle of the night and my ears were a little sore from laying on my side with the speaker pushing on my ear. Since I didn't need music anymore, I switched to my other mask and went right back to sleep.

I don't mind a 2 mask approach if I can enjoy a little music as I drift off.

I have the volume turned really far down. The sound quality is pretty good for a $30 sleep mask headphone.

So let's talk tech. The Bluetooth was easy to pair with my phone. Volume controls while wearing it are easy to use. Track repeat and skip are also easy to trigger.

I'm not sure why this has a phone capability, last thing I need is for a phone call to wake me up in the night on my head. I removed phone from the Bluetooth setting so that won't happen.

Ok, here's what I don't like about it.

First, the micro USB charging plug gets covered by the fabric, I can deal with that, it's a tight fit, so be aware you'll need to push while you plug. Since it's micro USB you have that 50% chance of getting the right side in.

Second, after your music stops using a sleep timer on the music app, the Bluetooth stays connected and never auto shuts off. I didn't know this the morning after the first day of use my phone wasn't ringing. Turns out it was ringing in the mask. I missed a few phone calls. You'll need to actually power it down when you're done using it. Seems to me, if there's no music for an hour it should auto shut down.

It comes with a little storage bag which is nice, and a charging cable, but no brick, since we all have plenty of ways to plug in USB cables to charge.

I like this mask, I continue to wear it.

title: Super soft and comfortable
text: I like that this mask is very soft and comfortable to wear.  It's a little big on me which means light come in from the bottom, but it makes up for that in general comfort.  The strap in the back can be tightened if necessary.  I was able to adjust it so that it doesn't fall off of my face.  The sound quality is about what you'd expect at this price point.  It's a little tinny, but it's fine.  I don't think I will use the sound function much though.  It would be good if you live in a noisy environment to put on some white noise.  Overall, this is a nice eye mask.

title: Love it
text: Great to sleep with or if you have a headache.

title: Sooo Soft!!
text: Its really soft and comfy. love the lil side pocket that holds usb charging wire, it does bother me at all surprisingly.  Sound good.

title: Pretty decent mask but couple of issues.
text:

Pro's -
Keeps all the light out! very effective
soft and comfortable to wear.
strap on back is adjustable and easy to adjust while on head.

Con's -
if your wearing it to sleep and the voice yells "powering off" it will wake you up.

Overall, the mask is pretty good. Will keep and continue using.

title: Works very well
text: I've tried everything for my ptsd nightmares with no success.  These are great for blocking light and I've been listening to "pink noise" and it's helped.  The left side isn't very comfortable because of the wires. Otherwise, I'd give 5 stars

title: Super comfortable
text: I don’t normally wear a mask to sleep in. I just wanted it for the headphones. But I’m so glad I got it. There’s a short little cord that attaches to the charger, but it can be tucked in the areas where the speak is and you can’t feel it. And you can move the speakers around to for your head. This is fantastic.

title: Comfortable but not perfect
text: This is my third attempt at finding a comfortable mask that has speakers so I can listen to my sleep meditations. This one is comfortable as a mask but for some reason it’s way too big for my face. The speakers are set far behind my ears and I can only hear one of them at a time. When I laid on my side the light came in so I tried pulling them lower and then I heard zero audio. The designers of these devices need to actually try them. These will join the others in my nightstand unfortunately as I continue to keep looking.

title: These are SO COMFORTABLE
text: This is the second bluetooth sleep mask I have tried.  I LOVE the contoured eye portion.  It is so so so comfortable.  The sound quality is good, and it is very easy to move around the headphone pieces to get them in place.  But the sound cancelling quality isn't great.  I can definitely still hear my husband snore.

title: Does the job
text: It's very comfortable and does exactly as intended. Audio quality is there but not the same as ear buds. I'm satisfied with it.

title: No auto power off.
text:
This unit does not have any form of auto power off when whatever you're listening to finishes. This is an essential battery saving feature as running the battery dry on a daily (nightly in this case) basis will quickly kill it.

The electronic components are also not secured in anyway on the inside and will freely move out of place causing the buttons to not do anything (since they're no longer on the circuit board).

Maybe it's just my face but the nose section also bleeds in light.

I do not recommend this unit on the battery draining/killing issue alone.

title: Soft, Good Sound, not tight enough
text: I must have a small head, because it is very loose on me, and if i tighten it up enough to be comfortable the velcro pulls my hair. Over all, good quality.

title: Not for smaller heads
text:
I bought this so I could listen to relaxing music for when I sleep. The idea is great and you can adjust it to fit, however, because my head is smaller in circumference (I guess, never really thought much of that before), the speakers end up behind my ears making it harder to hear without blasting the volume which nullifies why I wanted it. So I would try and adjust the mask and lose the snug feeling on my head just to get a speaker in a decent area. Also, if you're a side sleeper, while the mask itself is comfortable, the speakers hurt to lay on and you have to figure out how to adjust them for minimal pain. I'd cut the speakers out just to have the snugness of the mask itself, but I kind of hate the idea of doing that since I'd still have the main part on the front.
Overall, I guess it's great if you have a larger head than I or don't want a snug fit and are a back sleeper.

title: Works well, for what it is
text: I use this EVERYNIGHT. It blocks light amazingly, the sound quality is pretty good, but most importantly, it's comfortable. You will need to play around with the placement of the speakers since when they are in the wrong spot it can cause this repetition. I only listen to audiobooks with them, but the sound quality for voice is pretty good.

title: Love It But NOT Durable
text: Great for falling asleep to music, white noise, recorded books etc. However, after less than six months wiring has frayed and is quickly nearing the end of it's service life. Given that I've been VERY careful not to abuse it, I'm not certain I'm willing to keep buying a new set twice a year. 🤔

title: husband loves them
text: my husband asked for these for xmas, he loves them, he says they work great for noise reduction and sound quality, just like they say they do.

title: Best Headphones I have Ever Owned
text:
I love these headphones, they are easily my favorite. I always worry about these wireless headphones because I tend to be terrible at keeping them in one place, and these are quite pricey so losing one would really be unfortunate. They come with a really nice carrying case, it's a super durable case, thankfully, and I really like that it's easy to put the headphones in it (just drop it in and like a magnet kind of pulls them down). It's super easy to charge, and I really like that when I start using them a little voice comes on and tells me how much battery life is left. The battery life is also pretty impressive, I used them for hours upon hours without the battery running out, so I was pretty impressed by that.
The sound quality on these is amazing. I love how noise cancelling they are, I had my doubts with these being earbuds, that they wouldn't be that good at cancelling out noise, but these are great. I love how loud I can make it without affecting the sound quality.
I would highly recommend these to anyone, as I said these are hands down my favorite earbuds of all time.

title: Won't Hold A Charge
text: A few weeks in, I can leave an informed review. These earbuds are pretty good when they work. The sound is nothing compared to my Bose over the ear headphones (I'm on my third pair and they are on the list of things I'd grab in an emergency) but it's decent enough. But most of the time they don't work at all. I keep them in my purse for when I need them, and honestly hardly ever do, but I can probably only get about 45 mins of use out of them before the battery drains. I'm surprised that Bose put their name on such a flimsy product. And the mandatory app is useless and annoying, like a lot of apps.

title: Great 👌 Product
text:
I would be commiting a sin if I don't give this a review!!!!

Noice Cancellation: 10/10
Comfort: 10/10
Audio Quality: 10/10

title: Great noise cancellation
text: The noise cancellation is amazing, main reason I got these earbuds. I have the bose qc 2, and this makes a great companion for summer headphones. Thanks to this, I dont have to increase the volume to max to drown out background noise or chatter. There will be some external sounds that makes it through, but it isn't a deal breaker, since these are just earbuds.

title: Greatest Ear Buds
text: I love the way they fit snug in my ittle ears.

title: Noise cancelation best feature
text:
The sound quality is great, but in my opinion not what justifies the price. The feature that does justify the price is the level of sound cancellation they provide. I've used premium over the ear sound cancelling headphones (including Bose) but none of them come close to the reduction in sound these provide.

If you are looking for quiet, these are what you want. You can also use provided modes, or custom design them through the app. The app allows you to create a mode that has minimal or no noise reduction. You can even create a mode that senses the noise level around you and when it becomes too loud the noise cancelling kicks in.

I was hesitant to spend this much money on ear buds, but am now happy I took the chance.

title: Simply the best
text:
My family has tested out numerous noise canceling earbuds in the last six months, looking for the best ones to fit each member of our household. This set of earbuds was the universal favorite among every member of our family.

For one, the noise cancellation feature is absolutely the most effective noise cancellation we have found on earbuds. Even having it on silent, I was unable to discern individual words from my mom reading loudly to my two noisy children in the other room. With an audiobook playing, I really didn't notice anybody else being in the house, though I could hear them if I thought about it. With music, it was like they weren't there, someone can stand right next to me and talk to me and I can be blissfully unaware.

If you get overloaded from auditory stimulation easily and just need the world to stop making so much noise every so often, these are the earbuds to get.

The sound quality is extraordinarily good on audiobooks, rap music, metal music, and more peaceful and soothing ballads and classical. The base was not overwhelming, nor did the treble get screechy.

It fit my very small ears well, and fit my husband's ears well also, he has a much bigger ear canal size.

The one thing that we have both noticed is that these are also heavier than most of our other earbuds, however even with my ears feeling rather sensitive, it really didn't bother me because they are weighted nicely and fit so well.

Overall, while these could be improved by being slightly smaller and less heavy, these still beat out five other well-known brands in our household for both the noise cancellation and in audio quality.

title: The best noise canceling ear buds
text: These are the best ear listening devices I have ever owned. I'm super happy with my purchase

title: Amazing!
text: My daughter is in college and becomes distracted by surrounding noises while she is studying. My other adult daughter recommended these to her and they are outstanding! You can adjust what level of noise cancelation you want. So when she needs to be attentive to noises around her, she changes that setting. They both love these and recommend them to all their friends!

title: Bose sound quality

title: Fantastic Earbuds
text:
At first I was skeptical, so bought a pair of EarPods instead. I was disappointed with the fit, sound, and noise cancellation so returned them. I then ordered these and was blown away by how comfortable they are, the effectiveness of the noise cancellation, and best of all the sound. To my ears these are the best earbuds I have ever owned. The sound is deep, rich, and present, and is great for all kinds of music. They only connect to one device at a time, but that's not a big deal to me. They sound great on the phone too. I have already used them for over 20 hours and am very pleased.

The only criticism I had was that there was no volume control, which is a real issue if you plan to use these with devices like Apple TV where there is no Bluetooth volume control on the device. I got a very pleasant surprise when Bose released an upgrade that added volume control by sliding your finger up and down on the right earbud. Perfect!

Though pricy, I would highly recommend these.

title: Best sound quality and comfortable

title: An excellent sounding earbud but could be better at connecting different devices
text: These sound great. They lock into the ear with a twist. The silicone tips are easy to interchange. The noise cancellation is nearly as good as with Bose QC headphones. Bose recently added the ability to change volume on the earbuds. I purchased the "white" model and I must say they are very attractive and not so boring as "black". The appearance is opalescent, like pearl, and looks good. Of course, that's just my opinion. I have two complaints; the case and connecting. The case is beautifully made and is imposing in size. It is substantial, to be sure. But why is it so difficult to open? You have to really mash the button and if your fingers are anwhere near the hinge at the back of the case it will not open. You have to fiddle with it or you have to learn to grip it lower down so the mechanism works freely. This is complicated by the fact that the case is smooth, like a bar of soap, and it will pop right out of your grip if you are not careful. I guess if you are wearing gloves you are just going to have to smash it  with a rock to open it. (Just kidding, sort of.) My second complaint is that these are not so convenient for connecting between different devices. If you frequently switch between devices, there is some delay and annoyance involved. This is the main reason I am downgrading from 5 to 4 stars. In sum, these earbuds are the best I've ever used as they tick the most boxes of things that are important to me. That being: world class ANC, secure fit, comfort and great sound.

title: Impressive sound, and attractive earbuds
text:
These earbuds sound amazing. I’m comparing them to my PowerBeats3 by Dre for sound quality. These sound much better, and are more comfortable for me. Then I turned off ATMOS and turned on HD and it was like going from black and white TV to 4K color. These earbuds get loud enough that I don’t anticipate any difficulty using them when traveling on a plane. They are easy to pair. Open the case, press the button on the back of the case, look for the Bluetooth device named Edifier and Bob’s your uncle.

-Easy to pair

Cons:

I haven’t used these long enough without recharging to speak to the battery life, but the packaging claims 7+14h (whatever that means -see pic). I will download and try the Edifier App and update this review when I get a chance. I hope you find this review and pictures helpful. Thanks!

title: Great sound quality!
text: They sound quality and noise cancelation is very good!  They pair up very quickly with my computer.  I have a good set of headphones, but the sound quality of the earbuds exceeds the headphones. It's nice that I can walk around the kitchen and living room and enjoy listening to my favorite music while getting work done.

title: Very good
text:
These are currently my favorite earbuds. And I have many pairs. They are my dedicated pair for my bedroom computer.

They are a breeze to connect through bluetooth 5.3. Sound quality is great, very clear, although I will say they don't seem quite as loud as most of my other pairs. For the most part this isn't a problem, however, except that I tend to use them one at a time to save on power, and that can affect volume perception.

That's not to say the buds don't have a long battery life. They do. And I only have to charge the case every three days or so. They also use a type c charger. Pretty much a requirement these days.

Noise cancellation is good, but I have small ear canals, and even with the smallest tips--and there are several enclosed--I struggle to get a tight fit that stops sound leakage. This is, of course, when I'm wearing both buds. All bets are off when I'm wearing only one.

Earbuds are water resistant, which is an excellent quality, especially if you've ever drop one in a sink with the water running.

As I said, my new favorites. Pricing for the quality is excellent. Definitely recommeded.

title: Sounds really enjoyable
text: For the prise these ear buds are a no brainer.  I've bought the neo buds pro, they sound good but there's a little bit of sibilance. Definitely the w240nt take care of that. Everything just sounds clear and good and the bass is even better. Simply just enjoyable. It's tuned more on the warmer brighter side but the vocals still sound really clear and decently forward. Now I've listened to the Airpods Pro 2 and honestly the Edifier W240TN sound way better! It definitely has more sparkle and for the price point just makes it sweeter. The call quality on theses headphones are outstanding. My wife can't believe how quite the background is and how my voice comes in clear and I've been in some pretty noisy environments. My only complaint is that sometimes it cuts out. Not a whole lot but it definitely has a couple times. I'm hoping a future firmware update will take care of that but otherwise these are still my go to earbuds. I believe Edifier is headed towards the right direction.

title: Great headset, even better deal!
text:
*This is a first thoughts review. There will be an update posted if there is any damage similar to the black headset also shown in the images*

I received them yesterday. They were on sale with -$50 to the $149.99 MSRP. These headphones are awesome! However, you can only gain access to ldac through a firmware update that is done through the app. I had to do 2 updates total.

Q30's vs. Q45's:

Sound quality: points to Q45
Q45 has ldac while q30 does not. They have a similar sound signature, but both can be customized. My favorite sound signature comes from the q30's set to "acoustic" on the Soundcore app. This audio signature is achieved on the Q45's by the screenshots included. #1 is strictly the Soundcore app. #2 is for devices with a 10 band or higher EQ. With my testing, the Q45 is closer to neutral with the stock EQ, but it can be improved greatly with that 10 band EQ. If your phone does not have Dolby Atmos or if that EQ is still not present, "Flat Equalizer - Bass Booster" on the play store has a 10 band EQ. You can also use a 10 band EQ on windows if your PC or laptop has the latest realtek audio console software.

Comfort: toss up
The Q45's have better ear muffs, being larger in diameter and thicker, and more comfortable. The q30's have a better padding for your head, however, it is not that big of a deal if you have your headset adjusted correctly.

Build quality: points to Q45
The Q45's had a sturdier build than the q30's which cracked and broke above the adjustment sliders.

ANC: Points to Q45
The Q45 has better noise cVancelling in general. Not only does it stop more noise, but the app lets you customize your ANC further. With the Q30'S, you get to switch between 3 different presets which vary in effectiveness, but the Q45's allows you to adjust the level of noise it cancels or gives you the option to let Soundcore decide what noise cancelling levels to apply and when. The Q30's microphones are placed at the back of the headset, while the microphones on the Q45's are lower to the bottom of the headset, making for better placement and improving the next topic:

Transparency: toss up
The Q45's have a louder transparency volume, but lack soundstage. It more or less sounds like you cut 2 circular holes in your headset, one in the middle of each ear cup. The Q30's are less loud, but have better sound stage. It does not sound like you have holes cut into your headphones, but rather the headphones sound like they are open back to a certain degree. Despite having better soundstage, the Q30's microphone placement means that wearing the headset correctly makes you hear everything behind you, or everything in front of you if you flip it the other Q4.

Loudness: toss up
They can get just as loud as each other

title: First flight... Loving them
text:
I had been casually using them around the house just to test them. In this aspect, they're very useful and functional if you are wanting to drown out the background noise. I find the noise canceling to be pretty amazing. The cans are comfortable to wear for extended periods. I thought I wouldn't like them because I would get sweaty and hit with them on but I was wrong.

I took them on my first flight since purchasing them. I had other headphones and buds as backup but I didn't need them. I pretty much had them on from boarding until I took them off for landing. They were so comfortable I forgot about any of my concerns. Yes I got a little warm but I didn't sweat nearly as much as I thought I might and the sound was good. The most impressive thing for me was the noise canceling. It drowned our all noise to the point where I barely even noticed it anymore. I did have to turn up the volume a bit but with other headphones, I've had to max out the volume to get the output needed so I could hear the movie. This pair didn't need that.

It was quite the difference when I switched modes with a single button press and transparency mode basically let me hear things as they were. A little muffled but what a difference between that and noise cancelling.

These are coming with me everywhere I travel now. No question.

title: Rare Headphones Currently On The Market That Can Support ANC In Wired Mode WITHOUT Bluetooth!
text: Soundcore by Anker Space Q45 headphones rival the top-rated Sony WH-1000XM4 and Bose QuietComfort 45 at 1/3 of the price. I actually own both the Q45 and Q20. I used the Q45 at night to get a good night sleep because my wife snored too much. I've bought the highly rated and expensive QuietOn 3.1 noise cancelling earphones but after trying them, I've found that they did reduce the volume of my wife's snoring by about 2/3 but I could still heard a quieter but disruptive snoring! The Q45's noise cancellation was actually very good thanks to the hybrid and active noise cancelling functions. However, due to EMF concern because having a Bluetooth transmitter next to my head for a long time may not be good even though the radiation level is low, I only used the direct 3.5mm cable connection to turn off the Bluetooth transmission and only used the ANC. This can only be done with the Q45, not Q20. I used the latter one with Bluetooth on for workout because the Bluetooth duration is only for a short period of time so I think it's OK. I found the Q45 was the best choice because of 3 things: 1) Noise Isolation 2) ANC 3) The ability to play pink noise from an external device. The QuietOn 3.1 lacks the last function! I played a falling rain to drowned out the weaker snoring sound that the ANC could completely remove and that put me through a good night sleep through a pleasant falling rain :-)

title: Wow - Great Sound!  Comfortable Headband & very nice looking - Super Bargin!
text:
First I want to say how super impressed I am with the sound quality of these headphones... Wow how did all of that sound get in there? The thing is, I currently work as an Audio Recording technician/engineer for streaming videos of musicians and public speakers. So I have a pretty good idea of how things should sound and these far exceeded my expectations especially at this price. I really enjoy listening to music such as The Moody Blues on these (good definition and the drums sound fantastic). Of course you wouldn't use these for professional audio work, but for casual listening they are wonderful.

The headband is great too. When covid happened I stopped going to the barber. I've never let my hair grow this long before but decided that I like it this way. However I have also discovered that long hair can be difficult to manage. I figured that a headband could help with that and looked for some. I was disappointed by what I was finding, didn't really like the look or the fit of what I was finding elsewhere. But I love this, I got the Starry version and really like how it looks - of course style is a very personal choice the Stars work great for me but they have many other styles to choose from. It is also very comfortable. So even if it did not have bluetooth I would still consider getting it just for the headband.

They do work as a Sleep Mask.... which is to say that you can pull it down over your eyes to block out light. I sometimes find myself sleeping on couches and stray light can be a problem. These do a pretty good job of blocking that light. So that works pretty well and then I can put on some soothing tunes for while I sleep.

Also I should point out that I have a big head (in terms of hat size, not ego <grin>) and the stretchy fabric works fine. I am guessing that this will fit just about any adult sized head.

Sound Leakage is pretty much non-existent, which given their open design is surprising. When I am listening to music other people in the same room tell me that they can't hear it. so that is great! I won't disturb others with my music choices (even in the library).

Be aware that these do not provide sound isolation, in a noisy environment they are difficult or impossible to hear. On the other hand it means that you can have a conversation with someone without taking these off. Also these do not get super loud -- which is a good thing -- but many people demand that their music be super loud which damages their hearing which then forces them to increase the volume in a vicious cycle. if you are one of those people you will not be happy with these, they won't be loud enough for you. but for people with normal hearing these are plenty loud enough.

Another aspect of this design is that because the speakers are open and not sealed you ears stay a lot more comfortable. I have worn this all day in 90F heat and been comfortable, something that is quite unlikely to be possible with sound isolating (sealed) headphones. So the design is a trade-off between noise isolation and comfort. For most purposes this design is a good choice.

Battery Life is adequate... everything is a trade-off especially when it comes to batteries, which are heavy and bulky. I do wish this battery was about double it's capacity but that would have made these heavier and their current weight is good, would not really want to add to that. So this is probably as good as it can get. I timed it and I get about 12 to 14 hours on a full charge. I have not timed how long it takes to charge them but it's in the ball park of a couple of hours, perhaps less.

Bluetooth follies.....
I have not attempted to use these with a cell phone so can't comment on that... apparently there is a builtin microphone?

I actually bought these on a lark... I was having a conversation with someone at work about the problems of using Bluetooth headphones in a recording studio. getting rid of the cord would be great but there are multiple issues with Bluetooth, which I won't go into here. But it got me curious to see what the current state of the art was. The last time I attempted to use Bluetooth for anything was about 6 years ago and it was an abysmal failure. Well 6 years is a long time in the fast moving tech world so I figured it was worth another attempt. Found these and the price was excellent. Wasn't expecting much but was happily blown away with the results ... mostly....

I tried to hook these up to a debian linux laptop, which proved impossible. fact is that linux is great for many things but it sucks at doing Bluetooth.

So then I tried an Android Tablet and connecting them was flawless and effortless. Android is actually built on top of a version of linux... so weirdly the tablet version works and the laptop version does not.

My new favorite thing to do is to put my tablet in a backpack and go for a walk. It is very enjoyable to be able to listen to music as I stroll. The thing is though that as I walk around I find that there are places where these simply cut out and stop working. I have not investigated this in depth but my impression is that this appears to be caused by radio interference (they never cut out when I am at home - unless I walk out of range). It's a minor nuisance and is fine for casual listening but it does show that Bluetooth is still not reliable enough for serious/professional use. Anyway if I just keep walking I am soon out of the dead-zone and the sound resumes.

Final thought: the black plastic of the control unit stuck in the middle of your forehead does detract a bit from the overall aesthetics. I wish that they had made it in a color that more closely matched the headband.

Bottom Line: I wholeheartedly recommend this.

Whoever designed these deserves some hearty kudos for a job well done.

title: Excellent headphones for the $$
text:
I have used several earbuds, headsets, and OTE headphones over the past decade…including a pair of $300+ Sony BT with N/C capabilities, Apple EarPods, and an Audio Technica wired studio monitor set.

Sound is a personal and subjective determination…but, I am very pleased with these SoundCore headphones. I have purchased many Anker Products, including cables and BT earbuds and always been pleased with their quality and value.

I use these SoundCores to watch movies at night when the house is quiet and others are sleeping. They have linked every time to my tv (Samsung w/Amazon Fire-Stick 4K) within seconds of powering them on…they have never dropped a connection. I have only used them for 3 hours at a time…so battery life has not been truly tested yet. I leave them plugged in to charge after each use. Noise cancellation is not an issue for my needs so I won’t speak to their N/C abilities.

Bottom line: excellent sound quality…excellent BT connectivity and they are consistent with the fit, finish, and value I have come to expect from the Anker company.

I highly recommend these units at this price point if you are in the market for a quality BT headset for 1/3 the price of Bose or Sony.

I have owned these for 2 weeks and will update my evaluation if something untoward happens in the next few months. Typically, the issue with BT headsets is their non replaceable/rechargeable batteries fail…taking your $300 Sony’s with it. :-/

Good luck!

title: Anker Q35 - Affordable Excellence
text:
I'd been looking for a solid set of wireless around-ear headphones that weren't $300-500 type expensive. I don't do a ton of critical listening. I just wanted some comfortable headphones to have for quiet listening during study/work and occasional air/train travel.

These fit that bill. They produce rich sound, excellent noise cancellation, are super comfortable, and have great build Quality. Are they the best in each of those areas? No. But they do all of those things well. If you're into cars, these are like the VW GTI of headphones. Jack of all trades, Master of None, but always better than only Master of One.

I've tried Apple's headphones, Bang & Olufsen units, Bose's flagship NC-units, crazy expensive Sennheisers, and even the Aussie Nura units which modulate Soundwaves for your psycho-acoustics.

I'd say these are just as comfortable as the Bose units, and the noise canceling is about 80-90% as effective as that of the Bose. The sound quality is similarly a decent 70-80% of the acoustically personalized Nura's.

Bottom line: with Amazon Day discounts, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better set of NC-headphones for about $100-120. I heartily recommend them if you're looking for the absolute best bang for your buck.

Audiophiles should look elsewhere; but these aren't designed for them either. They're just really excellent and comfortable for an affordable range of headphones.

title: Perfect for Use with an iPhone!
text:
When I talk to my friends for hours on end the last thing I want to do is hold my iPhone in my hand up to my ear or even be on speaker phone. My husband does not like hearing the speaker phone when he's trying to concentrate on his iPhone. It takes too much effort to talk on a speaker phone for hours. So as soon as I answer the phone I switch over to these headphones and talk through the microphone in the headphones. Perfect!

My friend who calls me once a week sounds like a radio DJ, in fact he used to be one but the headphones make him sound that way just naturally. It is really cute. He's always had a nice voice but this makes him come through like rich stereo sound. At first I thought I was talking to a stranger, but got used to his new voice sound.

You just have to hold the button down for a few seconds and an AI voice tells you what the headphones are doing. So if you are finished with the headset you just press the middle button and it tells you the headset is off. So that saves on battery power and makes it easy to know when the power is on or off. I find that I can make these the best volume easily and have it now where I don't need to change it at all.

My friend who calls me every week told me about these headphones and I bought them on his recommendation. I had these years before I got an iPhone because I prepare ahead of time!!!! Now that I have a new iPhone 14 I'm happy as can be with my headset. Since the microphone is built in this is perfect for phone calls but it also works like a regular headphone if you want to listen to audio on your phone. I haven't started listening to music on it yet but will report back when I do. The sound is just superior to any headphones besides my AKG K553s.

~The Rebecca Review

title: A must-have for anyone who loves listening to music or taking calls without the hassle of wires!
text:
The Pollini Bluetooth Headphones Wireless is a must-have for anyone who loves listening to music or taking calls without the hassle of wires. These headphones have been designed to deliver an exceptional audio experience with their deep bass and crystal-clear sound quality. I recently purchased these headphones, and they have quickly become my go-to option for listening to music or taking calls.

The first thing that caught my attention when I received these headphones was their stylish and sleek design. The black color is versatile and goes well with any outfit. The ear cups are cushioned with soft memory-protein earmuffs that provide ultimate comfort even after hours of use. The adjustable headband makes it easy to find the perfect fit for your head.

The headphones also have a foldable design, making them compact and easy to carry around. You can easily fold them and put them in your bag or backpack without worrying about them taking up too much space. This feature makes them perfect for travelers or anyone on the go.

The sound quality of these headphones is impressive. The deep bass and crystal-clear sound make listening to music a pure joy. The battery life on these headphones is also impressive. With up to 40 hours of playtime, you can enjoy your music or take calls without worrying about running out of battery. The headphones also have a fast charging feature, which means you can quickly charge them up and return to using them.

The Bluetooth connectivity on these headphones is smooth and effortless. Pairing them with my iPhone and Android devices was easy, and the connection remained solid and stable even at a distance. The headphones also have a built-in microphone that makes it easy to take calls without taking off the headphones. The microphone delivers clear audio, making it easy to communicate even in noisy environments.

Another impressive feature of these headphones is the controls. The controls are intuitive and easy to use, allowing you to adjust the volume, skip tracks, and answer calls without taking off the headphones. The rules are conveniently located on the right ear cup, making it easy to access.

In conclusion, the Pollini Bluetooth Headphones Wireless is an excellent option for anyone who loves listening to music or taking calls without the hassle of wires. The sleek and stylish design, deep bass, and crystal-clear sound quality make these headphones a must-have. The 40 hours of playtime, foldable design, and intuitive controls make them perfect for anyone on the go. I highly recommend these headphones to anyone looking for a high-quality audio experience.

text:
Overall great value. I don’t use them to drown out sound, but just enough to help me tune out other sounds around me.

As a sleep mask this item works rather well. There is some light leakage for me around the nose, but it cuts out the greater portion of light and doesn’t put pressure on the eyes. Sometimes the padding at the bottom needs adjustment so it’s not pinching my nose. As a side sleeper, I was surprised that the speakers weren’t more uncomfortable. It’s usually a few hours of sleeping on one side before they begin to bother my ears.

I typically only get about 5 to 6 hours of sleep a night and that means I often get two nights worth of play time at about 30% volume. I was actually surprised by the sound quality, I expected it to have a more canned type of sound, but the speakers have a decent range. The speakers do have to be lined up with your ears in order to hear much, but that hasn’t been much of an issue for me.

As to other reviews about things shifting around, I haven’t noticed that with the speakers. You can move the speakers a little bit to adjust them, but I haven’t noticed any big shifts without my input. The controller does move around enough that at times it can be difficult to see the led indicators, but I haven’t had it shift so much that the buttons didn’t work.

title: Comfy, good mids and highs
text:
I'm wearing these now and they're quite comfortable to wear for extended periods. Connection was easy. I wish they had more control buttons instead of just the one. The charging port is also in an odd place (presumably to keep people from charging while wearing) (it's on the left ear-pod).
Sound quality is a little funky and I guess to be expected on a cheap pair of headphones: the biggest thing is that they don't reproduce bass really at all, I can feel the bass hits when the pod hits my ear, but the bass isn't making it to my eardrum; at highest volume there's a bit of distortion but they don't really get /that/ loud; otherwise, at low-medium levels and for treble and mids, the sound reproduction is excellent. I suspect I'm going to like these more for podcasts and audiobooks than music.
If you're not into really bass-y music, and you don't need substantial volume, these will probably be perfect for you.

text: I really love these headphones. I don’t like to stick earbuds in my ears as I have my daiths pierced and it can be very uncomfortable to wear earbuds. Earbuds also tend to block out sound around me for the most part and I like to be aware of what’s happening around me. This is the first time I have tried bone conduction headphones, and I really like the experience. I do find that I have to turn the volume louder than if I had earphones in my ears, but I’m OK with that. I feel like the price is really reasonable considering the technology. I gifted a set of of these by a different brand name to my father for Christmas, and he absolutely loves them. They make a great gift!

text:
I found it very difficult to locate the correct spot for good listening. This is not necessarily a defect of the headphones but more likely my inexperience with this type of headphone. The front of my ear felt like it was vibrating with the music which was not an enjoyable feeling. Of course the sound quality varied as I tried to find a good location on my ear.
The instructions say nothing about the microphone. If someone received this headphone without seeing the product write up on the Amazon page, they would never know you can talk through the headphone.

title: Weird but effective, comfortable for long-term wear
text: I have what is apparently a larger-than-normal head (enough so that buying non-adjustable hats is a no-go), so I wasn't sure how bone conduction headphones would work for me- while I still don't know if all bone conduction headphones would work, this particular pair worked quite well  for me and also worked for multiple other folks. The piece that needs to be in contact with your bone is actually pretty independent of the flexible but not flimsy cable that runs behind the neck to connect the two earpieces, so head size is less of a concern than I thought.  While the audio is better on more focused headphones(over-ear or in-ear), the audio on this is more than sufficient to hear without drowning out the world around you.  My husband could hear a little of the music I was listening to, but not so much that it was disruptive.  Overall, these are a decently-priced foray into bone conduction headphones, and I'm glad to have had the opportunity to check them out.

title: Really shines while wearing hearing protectors
text:
This is my first set of bone-conduction headphones, so with that important disclaimer out there, up front and center...

I like this headphone set pretty well. I was a bit perplexed by them at first, as, similar to other reviewers, I was a bit puzzled about the seemingly relatively loose fit on my head, relatively low volume level, etc.

My "ah-ha" moment came when I lightly covered my ear canals with my fingers while wearing them and streaming music - the audio level was greatly boosted! I bounded off to the garage, grabbed a clean set of my favorite hearing protector plugs and put them into place, put on the headset, adjusted the volume, then turned on my big ol' air compressor - easily the noisiest thing I have in my house & shazam!, I could easily enjoy my music while in a high noise environment, even at relatively low music volume levels!

I have used connected hearing protectors before (such as ISOtunes AIR DEFENDER Bluetooth Earmuffs and 3M PELTOR E-A-R buds Noise Isolating Headphones EARbud2600N, both available on Amazon), and I like those options very well, but I think this particular solution is TRULY-SUPER-DUPER convenient: simply use any appropriate hearing protector plug for your environment and add these nifty headphones to stream your music.

If you use these in a work environment / employment situation, make certain your employer is OK with this. Many will not allow employees to wear earbuds because wearing regular old earbuds in a high noise environment can overexpose a worker to noise, leading to hearing loss. However, if one is wearing appropriate hearing protection to protect one's cochlea from excessive noise levels, then using these headphones will not pose the same risk to hearing as traditional non-protective wired (and not level-limited) earbuds.

I don't think I would enjoy using these during a workout or other open-ear uses because of the relatively low volume levels that I was able to obtain - although, in a quiet environment and at low volume settings, they are just fine for casual listening.

I did try wearing these under my motorcycle helmet, but that was a non-starter for me - the headset is too high-profile/large to stay in place while putting the helmet on.

Overall, I think these are very good and can recommend them. The audio seems somewhat heavy on the bass end of the sound spectrum, and the highs seem a bit trimmed or low, but in a high noise environment (such as mowing, snow blowing, weed-eating, etc.), with hearing protectors in place, the audio quality is as good as I've experienced with any other protective streaming option that I have tried.

title: Lightweight, fit well, good sound quality; 5-Star earbuds at this price point
text:
At this price point, these USB-C earbuds sound good for everyday use. The key is fit. Make sure you have a tight seal. This may even involve using a different size tip for each ear. Without a good fit, your music will sound flat and tinny and you'll think the earbuds are terrible.

If fit properly with a tight seal, these UNOLYO earbuds have decent sound quality. Don't expect thumping bass. If you are looking for strong low frequencies (bass), these are not the earbuds for you. 

For me, they fit well right out of the box (or should I say, out of the tin). I didn't need to change the tips. I easily got a good seal. Very lightweight.  They don't stick out of your ears too much so no Frankenstein effect. My Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra accepted them with no fuss, no battery usage warnings. All good. Magnets that hold earbuds together are strong enough. BONUS - they magnetically attach to the tin case and file cabinets too! Not sure what to do with this "feature."

There is a controller on the right earbud wire. It has three buttons. Obviously, two on the ends are dedicated to volume control. The center button allows you to play/pause and move forward/backward through the tracks. All worked as expected. The controller also manages phone calls.

When I put my phone in my pocket with these earbuds in and walked/ran around, they worked well. The cable length between the phone and your ears was more than adequate (I'm 6' tall). No tugging. These come with two extra sets of tips (small and large; medium is installed). They also toss in a USB-C to USB-A adapter which I assume is for plugging into a computer - Zoom, Meet, etc.

These are 5-star earbuds in this price point category. I plan to put them in my bag as a backup pair of USB-C earbuds. It's nice not to need a dongle.

ABOUT THE PHOTOS... As of now, there is one photo posted of a little bag. I assume the earbuds are in it. I didn't get a little bag. I got a tin as pictured.

Hope this helps!

The headphones themselves are situated in small pockets that allow for a very small amount of adjustment in their placement. However, when adjusted so that they're in the right spot to hear the sound, the front portion pulls down and puts pressure on my forehead and sinuses, and the massive padding that goes over the bridge of the nose pushes my nostrils closed. I was able to get them to a reasonably comfortable spot, only to wake up an hour later with a massive headache and them slipped up onto my forehead. This happened three times before I finally just gave up and took them off. I can't see me using these for anything other than light blocking in the future, so thankfully they were pretty cheap on sale.

As a side note, they have a VERY bright blue light that flashes every few seconds, right in the center of the forehead. text:
Trust me.. from one who’s tried them all- if you want headphone to fit a toddler or little one choose a style such as this!! A wider band over the head actually is whats needed to hold in place. the comfort helps kiddos not to fuss with or remove! Bands padded fit rests right atop the crown of head to hold steady.. and adjustable length lets you customize and even grow with child to use for years.. how great is that!!

Avoid my mistakes trying to save a few $. I tried old school Walkman skinny type headset- using everything but duct tape and bubble gum to MacGyver a secure fit.. it was a total bust!! (I tried sweatband, ball cap bandana rag.. even hair styles like a ponytail + clippies to hold but, nope!) Ha! and earbuds?! It sounded good at the time- only lets just say to spare a longer read.. I have just x1 bud left! Getting a realistic design compatible for kiddos wiggles is a must- just like this has. Offered at a respectable price.. is icing on the cake!

Ear cushions like tiny “donut pillows” plume outward the so no hard plastic presses against ear.. comfort’s what brings a toddler to forget device is even there! Ergonomic style cups also keep the sound from escaping.. ideal if you can’t tolerate another round of “baby shark or cocomelon” sing-along x1 more time!

Volume feature is brilliant with a safety level it place, it cant get dialed up to harm eardrums.. and yet still able to deliver respectable sound quality! Love old-school plug-in method… Kids can use themselves.. Bluetooth option usually requires adult help! Splitter is nice feature for sibling/buddy use- haven’t used but, glad it’s there.

Foldable design is perf. for use on the go.. slip in carryon for airplane, road trip in car.. or, store easy at home! Comes with carry bag- my only wish is this included a hard case to protection vs. nylon pullstring! Otherwise, it’s perf. Great gift or spoiler for little.. 4.5 star for sure.
