title: I'm very surprised.... some pros and cons listed below
text:
PROS:

*PRICE - at the time, the black ones were $25 with an $8 off coupon!

*SOUND QUALITY - The clarity , for being budget headphones , is actually REALLY good. NOT the best, but compared to other cheapy $20 to $50 head phones I've owned (about 10 over the past 10 years or so) , these have the best clarity, hands down! The bass is decent without being over powering , but its not weak either. I think its just right. However, the bass could use a TINY bit more "richness" . With discount headphones , even the ones that have heavier bass, the problem is that the bass thumps, but its like a muddled thump, not clear, rich and deep. Here, its fairly clear, not super rich, but not muddled either, perfectly serviceable! and you could crank a bit more, with your app.

*THE BUTTON LAYOUT - ok seriously, EVERY headphone should have this layout. First the buttons are on the outside of the ear part! there are 5 buttons and they are all very well separated from each other so you don't accidently press something you don't want. They are all on the left ear... this is important because the volume up/next button, faces forward, forward makes sense because the next track, the next video etc is you ... going forward and the button faces forward. Same for the volume down/previous button which is to the back of the ear piece. The center button is big and is the pause/play/phone button which makes sense, since it will be the most used.... perfect layout.

*TYPE-C usb connection - This is self explanatory. Lots of these cheaper headsets still use micro usb type connection and it's just annoying, when everything now is type-c.

*THE LOOKS/STYLE - These look pretty good! On the black and gold color ones, the gold looks more like rose gold. Maybe they don't look like $100+ headphones, but they certainly don't look like $20 ones. These could (for the most part) easily pass for $50-ish (maybe even a bit more) headphones.

*FUNCTIONALITY - everything functions the way it should. Battery life seems pretty good too. I've gotten 20hrs so far on a charge, haven't tried to see if it goes to the advertised 40, but for me, even if its just 20, that's more than enough.

---------- WHAT'S "SO - SO" ----------

Here are somethings I think are kinda "so so" :

*QUALITY OF MATERIALS - Some quality seems good, like the stitching on the pads and the pads feel good, but then when you fold the headphones, everything is plastic and sometimes when you try to fold them back open, it feels like something might break. Also when you press in the play/pause/phone button, it feels cheap and makes a very cheap clicky plastic sound, but not a big deal, it still works. There is no metal band, that goes from one ear piece, across the top and to the other ear piece on the other side, its all plastic.

-----------CONS---------------

*THE "FOLDING" - As mentioned above, I wouldn't feel confident using the folding feature regularly on these things. If you plan on using that a lot, you might want to reconsider. It just feels like their gonna break if you keep folding them. I always leave my folding headphones open anyway so no biggie for me, but this could be a deal breaker for someone else

*THE RE-PAIRING BUTTON - Ok this might be minor , but a little annoying for me. With pretty much every other headset, you hold down the power button when turning on, to go into pairing mode. With these you turn them on, after that, THEN you hold the Equalizer/M button for 3 seconds to go into pair mode. I know, first world problem, but why not do this with the power button?

*THE PLAY PAUSE PHONE BUTTON PAINT - So these headphones look really nice for the price, look more expensive, that's good! buuuuut then you have the play/pause/phone button with the big bright yellow play/pause/phone symbols on it, and it looks really cheap! There's no need to have those symbols painted on anyway, but why not choose a more subdued color... not neon yellow! lol

*THE PACKAGING - the box they come in, is pretty flimsy, and the headphones themselves are in a very ultra thin like bubble wrap pouch thing , that does nothing to pad them. And the box itself looks cheap, but none of that affects the head phones.

------ OVERALL----------

I think these could be one of the best bang for the buck headsets out there! The only one of my cons that really carries any weight, is the whole folding thing, which I don't use, aside from that, overall, I am so pleased , that I ordered another set for me, the first ones were for my wife. The pros (for a budget set of headphones) far out weigh the cons here, at least for me.

title: For the price these things are pretty great.
text:
Seriously? I thought these things were going to sound awful. Usually, when it comes to headphones, you get what you pay for and I’ve bought enough bargain headsets in the past to know that they all sound like crap. Or so I thought.

These are pretty freaking good! They may look a little plasticky and cheap but they feel about as sturdy as my Sony Pulse 3D’s and sound quite good - at least at the top end. They certainly sound better than any of my Airpods.

The ear cups are a little small and sit ON my ears, rather than around them (very old school) but the padding and material are very soft, so it doesn’t feel particularly uncomfortable.

Sound wise, the trebbles and mids are actually pretty great - I’m noticing bits of songs in the upper end of the mix that I’ve just never heard before - but the bass is where things get a bit muddy. It feels like they’re doing something in the processing/EQ to try and ramp up the low end but all it succeeds in doing is making it sound sludgy and ‘under water’.

The “6 EQ presets” don’t do anything to help there either. There is ONE *mostly* balanced setting that is pretty great, four that lean into the muddy bass and one that is nothing but treble.

Because of my experience with cheap headphones in the past I wouldn’t have paid money for them and am only reviewing them because I received a free pair to review. But now that I’ve used them I’ve come away pretty impressed.

At $50 these would be a 3-star but for $25-$30? 5-stars for sure.

As a primary headset, this is lacking in terms of comfort, volume, noise cancelling, and much more. It's more of a minimal viable product than daily tool. Since I use it mostly as a backup, it's a fair tradeoff. If I had to use this daily, I'd be looking for another headset.

title: Nice multi-connector headset works great for web meetings & for audio voice over without USB adapter
text:
We got this just before a trip and used it right away to replace a set of ear buds. Using the 3.5mm adapter, this works well and avoids the audio latency introduced by using the USB adapter. The headset is quite comfortable and includes a cushion between your head and the metal band that gives it a bit of tension to stay on your head.
The foam cups fit on your ear, not over your ears. I prefer this Nuroum design as the headset is smaller and lighter than my old ham radio headset, though I have to give the nod to my old ever the ear JBL headset for comfort over very long sessions. The Nuroum ear pieces fold and the headset tucks into a handy cloth drawbag. Definitely more portable for trips than our JBL over ear headsets.

The boom mic has good sensitivity and the position is easily adjusted. The audio signal wire comes off the left side, at least that's what my audio test told me. Though you can reposition the mic to work on the right side of your face, you may have to swap the L/R channels as they will be reversed with the wires coming off the right side.

Doing audio voice over, it was preferable to use the 3.5mm connector, if your PC or Mac has one, instead of the USB connector. There is a slightly noticeable delay in using the USB connector and USB drivers compared to the 3.5mm mic/headset connector on my Lenovo Yoga 6 with Windows 11. All in all a far superior headset than my old clunky ham radio over the ear rig. It is a bit pricier than basic headsets, but I think you will find this a high quality alternative for web meetings, voice over, or yes, games.

title: Anytime earbuds claim "deep bass" be skeptical - Not great fit, not PS5 compatible
text:
These earbuds have a lot of flash going on, but in terms of user experience that's where they stop impressing and start underwhelming.

First off, what's good:
1. Pairing.
Bluetooth pairing has come a long way in the last decade and now instead of crossing your fingers and hoping your device and your headphones/speakers will show up when you ask them to look for each other, it's much easier. Sure enough, when you take these out of their case and they launch into "discoverable" mode, it's a small matter of just selecting them from your device's bluetooth options, and you're good to go.

Quick note here: I'd picked these up in the off-hand chance that maybe, JUST MAYBE, they'd pair and work with the PS5 as a wireless headphone and mic combo. ***THEY DO NOT WORK w/ PS5***. I'm putting that in caps not because it's a serious flaw, I 90% expected they wouldn't, but a man can dream. I just want to get that out of the way in case anyone else was wondering/hoping also. I don't even consider that a strike against the product.

2. Battery life.

Look, anytime Bluetooth is involved, I know battery life is going to take a hit. Bluetooth is a battery vampire, but we put up with it because, hey, not having a headphone cord scraping across your collar and sending noise up to the earpieces is really, really nice. In my uses of these headphones, they've been lasting through the days when I use them as long as I make sure to put them back in the case between uses instead of just taking them out and putting them in my pocket forgetting they're still linked to my device. That's probably the worst mistake you can make if you want your headphones and your device to have power at the end pf the day.

3. Sound quality.

Okay, so I'm separating Sound Quality and Bass Quality, because while these things DO NOT deliver on bass like they claim to, as far as just providing good clean sound for music and making phone calls or watching a show or movie on your device, these are perfectly capable and stuff sounds pretty good with a nice field of depth for earbuds.

And now, what's not so good.

1. The attempt at tapping/hands-free controlling on the earbuds.

Yeah, good luck with that. Half the time I attempted to control my device's volume/mic control/next-prev track/etc. whatever else these things promise to do with taps and swipes, the tactile sensing of the earpieces is just so finnicky and hard to pindown that's it's not really worth it. If that's a factor that weighs heavily into what you want from bluetooth headphones, don't bother with these. For me, it was less of an issue because I still operate from a "prefer to be looking at my device when I'm using it" mindset, so it's usually open/unlocked in front of me anyways. For volume, I rely more on the side buttons of my phone than I do trying to tap my earbuds.

2. Bass Quality

I'm sorry, but these things do not have good bass and it's weird that tried to single that out as something they bring to the table over other headphones. And this isn't even a case of comparing apples to oranges, because yes, if you REALLY care about bass, you're going to invest in some studio headphones and go that route, but even with other earbuds I've had many do bass better than these. When these things encounter deep bass they do what many earbuds do and end up trying to digitally imitate it and you end up with distortion. This is a pretty common thing with earbuds, and frankly it's not surprising that these things suffer the same problem. What's surprising was that they tried to brand themselves as being GOOD at bass. They're earbuds, drawing attention to how they handle bass is not a good idea.

3. Ear fit and feel

This is always a very, very subjective game of comfort roulette anytime you have earbuds with completely solid earpieces made to go inside the ear. Every ear is not shaped the same, so for some, these will be a perfect fit and they'll be confident enough to even go jogging with them in. For me, that's not the case. For me these stay in well enough for casual listening and viewing, but anything too movement intensive and these things get jostled out. Honestly, if these would have had the kind of buds with silicone pieces that fit into the ear that would've helped immensely, but I get it, they wanted to go for the iPhone earbud style imitation. But for me, that style of earbud has always been a bit uncomfortable and problematic in terms of fit.

4. The charging light patterns/color scheme

This is a minor thing, and the instructions clear this up, but the choice to go with solid red as the "charging is done" indicator color is counterintuitive to me.

title: Glitchy Bluetooth Connection, Flat Audio Sound
text:
These earbuds are glitchy. After hooking up to Bluetooth they announce "connected" which is soon followed by "disconnected" and then by "connected" again minutes later. This happens on repeat for no reason. They also give off a buzzy-fax-machine-like faint white noise when no music is playing, even when they are disconnected from Bluetooth. I am not a fan of the unnecessary buzzing and clicking in my ears.
Unfortunately, for me, the sound quality isn't anything to praise either. The audio they give off is a bit flat and lacks depth and dimension.
I will continue to use these earphones when I'm in a pinch, but they are far from my preferred choice. And although the design is "cool looking" and they fit decently in the ear canal, I would still advise someone who is looking for a pair of earbuds to invest in a more quality pair for the reasons listed above.
I posted some photos to give you a closer look and hope that they, along with my experience with this product, help you out a bit with your choice. Bottom line? I can't recommend them. Thank you!

text:
With all the hype around Beats, Bose, AirPods etc. You may think a pair of $19 - $30 headphones wouldn’t compare in any meaningful way, but in my opinion you’d be wrong. Now, I’m not an audiophile, but I listen to audiobooks and podcasts constantly. For that reason, I have 2 different pairs of SoundPeats. I own the Q30’s and Q36’s and have been overwhelmingly satisfied in the following 3 ways. This does not mean that they don’t produce outstanding music quality, I just wouldn’t be the best person to give an opinion in that regard. If the following areas are important to you as they are me, you cannot go wrong with SoundPeats Products.

1. Durability - I’ve purchased other wireless earbuds at an equivalent price point and they last me, maybe 6mo before they fail. These headphones hold up to listening of 4-8hrs a day. (I’m fortunate to be able to listen while I work)

2. Battery Longevity - again, other equivalently priced headphones boast 8hr run times and last maybe 3 hrs. in real world use. These claim 8hrs and I get 6-8hrs out of them consistently even well into a year of usage.

3. Customer Service - other equivalently priced Headphones claim a lifetime warranty and if/when you end up needing it (you usually will), they are no longer in business. Not so with SoundPeats. I’ve used their customer service to replace a pair of headphones and they are excellent! I have a pair that gave a slight crackle when the wire would move. Nothing that couldn’t be dealt with and as much as I use them, it’s possible it was a result of something I had done. At any rate, they shipped me a replacement, no questions asked.

title: Great multitasking headphones with microphone!
text:
Wow! These are awesome. I work during the day, and was hoping to find a bluetooth headset with a mic that can sync with more than one device at a time. This is it! I love these.

Dual Synchronization:
Being able to switch between my laptop and my cell phone was important to me. I often have to switch between phone calls, zoom meetings, videos on my laptop, podcasts on my phone, etc. I've tried some others, but none worked at all. These work seamlessly. The only problems I had were NOT with the headphones, but with the settings on my laptop, which I eventually figured out.
They headphones switch easily from one source to the other and back again. When I'm listening to something on my laptop and answer a call on my phone, they easily pause what I'm listening to and switch to the phone, and then easily switch back again and resume playing, and vise versa.

Headphone Sound:
The sound on these is outstanding for voice calls, podcasts and other functions, which is primarily what I use them for. The sound for music is ok/pretty good. They're not fantastic for music, but the sound is clear and works well enough. If your primary concern is the sound of the music, you may want to look at some other pairs with bigger drivers or a full earcup.

Microphone sound:
A lot of the earbuds and headphones that I tried sounded horrible to the people that I was talking to. People often complained about the static, or said that it sounded like I was in a jar or underwater. One pair had a mic that was so sensitive that every normal breath that I took sounded like I was breathing hard from going on a run. Creepy!!
With these headphones, everyone said that the sound clarity was outstanding. Even when I was actually breathing hard during an uphill walk. I've used these headphones on podcasts and zoom meetings and everyone has verified that the voice sound is very good. There is also a mute button on the mic, which is pretty convenient.

Comfort:
These are very lightweight and comfortable. The rest easily and comfortably on my ears and have a low profile which looks far better than those dorky huge 70's looking headsets when you're on video, or in a car.
The headband is adjustable which makes it easy to custom fit to your needs, and also makes it more compact for storing away. The ear speakers also rotate making packing it away in my briefcase even easier.
Of course, if you wear them all day as I often do, they may become a little bit uncomfortable, and if you're sweaty, they aren't as comfortable against your ears.

Charging/Battery Life:
Because when I'm working I can't have the headset fail, I haven't yet run them dry. I usually charge them at the end of my work day.
I have worn them for two long 10 hour shifts two days in a row, and the battery was still going strong. I even forgot to turn them off overnight and had no problems.
They charge to full charge really quickly.

Buttons/Controls:
The large center On/Off/Pause button works really well. It also works seamlessly while switching between media sources. The Fwd/Bkwd buttons and the mute button all work well also. I have really big hands and fingers and tend to break everything, and so far it's been rugged enough to withstand the assault and overly hard button pushing of my banana fingers.
On & Off is accomplished with a push and hold for about 10 +/- seconds.

Bluetooth:
Easy to use & program. It links up quickly to your devices and hasn't failed me yet.

I love these and highly recommend them for anyone who needs to use and switch between two devices. They are compact and easy to travel with, and they work really well. Also, you cannot beat the price!

Thank you for providing these. I really appreciate this product!

title: Only cancels about 5% of noise
text:
I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.

I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.

Test:
In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair
While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better)
Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better)
In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)

They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.

The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset pretty much useless.

I would recommend not buying these headphones. I returned the set I bought, and got my money back. There are better headsets at this price.

title: I'm returning these.
text:
I've been looking for NC headphones, and I have an overseas trip coming up. So when I saw these I did a rare thing and bought them from a local retailer without any prior research. I like Sony products. I have a 55" TV, blu-ray player, surround sound, and 5 disc changer - all Sony. I like them all. These headphones are a joke. On a prior overseas trip I tried the expensive Bose model of NC headphones, and was very impressed. I thought if these were a fraction as good, they would be worth it. Nope.

Pros: Rather comfortable for the ten minutes I wore them. Low price (assuming NC works - which it doesn't). Music sounded great with the NC switch on or off. Blocked a fair amount of noise just physically.

Cons: Falsely advertised as NC. The only noticeable difference with the switch on was a slight hiss. No carrying case included. Wires on both ear cups.

Eager to try them - I went outside where my neighbor two doors down was mowing the lawn. I noticed a fair amount of noise BLOCKING when I put on the headphones. When I flipped the switch I could hear the slight hiss i expected - but the neighbor's mower was not attenuated whatsoever. If I could plainly hear a distant mower with these activated, how could I expect them to attenuate the sounds within a passenger jet? Granted the sound these produced was great for dub-step - my test of dynamic range. But good sound wasn't the point of these.

If you want noise cancelling, look elsewhere. If you just want good sounding headphones, you can probably do better for your money.

text:

The complaints about putting these in are founded, but honestly, if you spend a little time practising, it's not complicated and you can find easier ways. Sometimes I'll put the cord over the ear first, then fold the bud into the canal. Other time, the opposite. I tug on my lobe with the thumb and ring finger and use my index finger to apply pressure on the body of the plug to seat it in my canal.

I do run with these in. They block a lot of sound, but not everything. I' pretty hyper vigilant about my surrounding when I'm running, so I'm usually very aware anyway. I wear them to listen to music while working in the workshop and it turned the quite loud combination of my radial arm saw + shop vac into an EXTREMELY manageable background sound, and I could still hear my son yell at me to shut it off when he wanted to ride his bike in the garage - all without taking away too much from the music.

In less than perfect settings, like resting my head against a pillow (or car seat) they do start to hurt a bit after about an hour. General wear, however, hasn't really had that effect.

The cord doesn't tangle remotely as much as my previous pair, but I hope to keep up the habit of winding them and putting them in the pouch that comes with them.
I got the "black", but they are transparent black. I'd rather opaque, but really, it's not a big deal.
I do sometimes wish the distance between the "Y" where the L/R cords connect was a little longer, again, it's not bothered me enough to dock points, really.
I'd actually give a 4.5/5 but don't feel the need to take away an entire star.

(Update)
7 months it made it without a hitch. Then the right side started to flake on me. I have to contort the wire and get lucky to get sound, which usually stays fine until I remove them and have to do it again the nest time I use them. I'll be returning to Shure for a replacement, but I have to say that my previous Sony pair, with near daily use, lasted 6-7 YEARS without issue, so this bothers me. I'm certain Shure will replace at least the cable, otherwise I'd be dropping more than the one star I took off. I'll update if I have other issues with the replacement process or otherwise.

title: Beautifully designed product with good noise cancellation
text:
Unboxing: Wouldn't usually make a section of this, but every once in a while a product makes it a pleasure. Especially a weird one like this. It's like unboxing a little UFO. It starts out in something like a hat box with a couple sticky tabs of tape to remove. Wish they could have found a better closure method, but the box is nice. Inside that you're immediately presented with the odd looking earbuds and a starter guide (also round) that has you immediately trying them on and fitting the best sleeve size for in your ear. There are no extra sleeves obviously apparent, so time to dig deeper. Next up is the UFO. A large earbud like this needs a large charging case. This one is round and unzips like some of the nicer headphone cases, but it's also a hard case with lights and buttons. Nothing inside but a charging dock. Under it is a secret compartment (made less secret by the thumb holes for easy removal). At the bottom of the hat box we have our missing sleeves and a charging cord.

Even with a diagram, putting these on was confusing and took four tries. Once they're on though, they are quite comfortable, and I think I'll learn to put them on after a few more tries.

Back to the book, and ugh! now they're telling me to put them in the charging case to pair. But I just finally got them on! &*^@#!

Ok, after getting things paired and back on, I'm able to put them through some testing. I'm not really an audiophile, but I've tried a lot of earbuds. Comfort is good. They don't rely on being stuck in your ear to hold themselves up, so there isn't a high stress point that's going to get sore first. They sound good. Better than most, but not the best I've heard. The control button is on the back of your ear, and I find it awkward and unreliable. Noise cancellation is solid, but like every other one I've tried, it is hard to tell sometimes because it scales with volume. Turning them on in a noisy room doesn't result in a quiet room, but turning up what you are listening to will result in noise other than what you are listening to disappearing quite a lot. There is a passthrough mode if you need to hear what's going on around you, but it doesn't sound very nice.

I like that it's USB-C. No more having to turn the cord over three times to figure out which end is up, and much faster charging. The case has three lights to show you charge progress for the case Each one represents enough charge for one full use of the earbuds. There's also a light on the top to tell you whether the earbuds are charged yet.

It's a solid product. Not my top favorite, but definitely innovative and a competitive offering.

title: Good Experience...But Only After Upgrades
text:
This is my second pair of IEMs, and I bought them as more of a backup. I'd read about these having a high value-to-price ratio and being very comfortable, so I went in with extremely high expectations.

Unfortunately my first impressions of these were that they were awful. As compared with my other pair (an older model from Ultimate Ears) I found it to be incredibly difficult to get a proper seal. The sound felt tinny and washed out. And comfort? Quite the opposite: Pain.

I almost gave up, re-packed them, and send them back. But I decided to invest further. I bought a set of Comply tips and tried those instead of the stock tips. HUGE upgrade! I was able to get a great seal and the comfort level shot way up. But Comply tips aren't cheap; the set of 3 pairs costs more than 20% of what I paid for these IEMs, so I'm removing one star there.

Comfort was still not where I wanted it and eventually I realized that the problem was the absolute piece of garbage cable that these came with. It's stiff, plasticy feeling, doesn't fall naturally, and I was constantly fighting with the memory wire. I upgraded to a much better cable--another 30% cost boost (second star deduction)--and now I had one of the two things I'd originally come for: A very comfortable setup.

So, now that I have comfort and seal, how about the sound? Impressive, actually, even at the 50% price bump point to which I'd taken things. I listen to electronic music primarily, so I like plenty of bass. These certainly deliver there. Very decent clarity on the high end as well. Sound doesn't sparkle nearly as much as it can with a good multi-driver, but for listening to music during my commute to and from work these are way more than adequate.

With the upgrades, these are really great. But for the base price, I feel the value level isn't quite what I expected. I'm not sure everyone needs to change out the tips. Some people seem to love the ones from Shure. But I think the cable does need to be replaced if you want a decent experience with these. So all in all, I recommend these, but only if you're willing to spend an extra $30+ over whatever you pay for the actual earphones.

title: Great mixing headphones for the price
text:
These are the second pair of open back headphones I've used so far, for mixing music, and for the price I am very pleased. I had been using AKGs before, their entry level, and it was a little lacking in all frequencies. But theses headphones proved what I would describe as a better all-around sound. The bass is at a very neutral setting, allowing you to hear how the entire mix might sound after compression and mastering. The highs are not too shrill. When I listen to the same mix in my Nura phones and or car stereo, the mix sounds great, and allows me to be able to identify areas that need to be EQd etc..

As for the way they fit, I would say that they could improve just a touch on the ergonomics. While they do not cause ear fatigue (most important) they do tend to slip down, and I have a big head, so for smaller headed people it may be a bigger deal. That is really my only complaint.

Overall I give these 4/5 stars. For the price I am very pleased.

title: Great headphones - cord is terrible
text:
These headphones produce very good sound quality in my opinion - crisp treble and straightforward mids. Contrary to rumor, these headphones are not "bassless," unless of course you are comparing them to Beats or some other brand/model made to pander to the preferences of common bass-junky. That being said, the sound profile of these headphones is still quite bright compared to what you may be used to, which I don't have a problem with but some people may. These phones work great for gaming, especially if you're looking to more easily hear subtle movement sounds in an FPS setting.

The reason I didn't give five stars on this product has nothing to do with the headphones themselves, but rather the cord. The cord is a frustrating nuisance. Audio-Technica has inadvertently educed the shape-retaining qualities of wrapping ribbon with the cord on these headphones. Forever defying gravity and coiling into a rat's nest of a tangled mess, this cord will make you question how a company that produces such good quality headphones could screw up so badly with something so simple.

title: I was legitimately amazed!
text:
Let's start by saying that I wear headphones about 12-16 hours a day. I do all my work from home and all my gaming and other hobbies wearing and using headphones. I'm not rough on them, but they get a ton of nonstop use.

I'm an IT professional and an amateur sound engineer as a hobby for my own music. Over the last decade, I've probably without exaggeration, bought 30-50 pairs of headphones/headsets. They always let me down no matter if I spend a little or a lot. Finally, I decided to just use my streaming mic (Blue Yeti) for work calls, and to get a pair of wired audiophile headphones. Audio Technica is a brand I know and know that they're respectable.

Let me tell you about how happy I felt the first time I put these on (earlier today)! First of all, they weigh almost nothing. It really feels like you are wearing a cloud on your head, but not in a way that feels like they are going to fall off. Despite being so light, they are well constructed of quality materials.

Next I noticed that instead of having a band that rests on your head, they have 2 arms that press lightly on your head and that's it. It not only adds to the feeling of lightness, but it doesn't trap heat which has been a big problem for me especially in summer months!

The cans themselves are feather light, and large enough to sit over my ears. They put very little pressure on my ears, solving another problem I have with most other headphones, and because they're open-backed, airflow passes through them and my ears don't get hot, sweaty, or irritated from the cups!

As far as the sound goes, I haven't yet done any extremely sensitive audio with them yet, but for music, video, gaming, and calls, the audio is at the top tier of any other headphones I've had. I can't say with authority that they are the best you'll ever hear, but they are very good, a good frequency range with a very low noise floor.

Lastly, the cord and 3.5mm plug are very well made. Where the cable comes out of the headphones is reinforced, so it doesn't look like it will be easy to bend and cause to fray. I am VERY happy with the quality of materials, assembly, and construction of these headphones!

So, in short, if you are a constant wearer of headphones, someone who struggles with headphone heat or discomfort, and want high quality (in sound and construction) headphones, then I very much recommend these!

title: Three sets in a row, DOA. SKULLCANDY = CRAP
text:
Over the space of a month, I bought 3 pair of these. Every set, the left was DOA. Would not power up, turn on, charge, or respond in any fashion.
Yes, I removed the sticker over the charge port for the buds.
I troubleshoot the system as far as I could without opening the case. I am a Systems Engineer. I deal with electronics all the time.
I even verified voltage was present on the charge pins, and in the earbud themselves (1.5v, FYI). The left earbud simply would not work.
This is a common problem with this product.
I should not have to troubleshoot it, when I can buy a 20 dollar pair and they just work.
Support from sellers and the manufacturer is nonexistent.
Happily returned all three sets. I will go with the Anker brand, as I've invariably had excellent experience with their products.
Skullcandy is trash. It's a shame, as the software upgrade feature seemed promising.

title: The sound is on point.. The ease of use, is amazing!
text:
Before reading, small caveat- Im a 40+ yr. old mom that loves my 80’s tunes.. Freddie Mercury, Boy George, Go-Go’s.. Wham! Ho-Jo and Frankie goes to Hollywood!!! These bands transcend me to a younger/carefree time in life ..A time in life of quality music!!! Well, If you can believe it.. my astute taste in music is not shared amongst my teenage and college kids. So, when traveling as a family unit, I have been deemed the outcast… and my music is reserved for only finest tastes- translation: I must listen ALONE in my own device!!

I am not a music connoisseur or some techno guru therefore, when I plug in a headset- (notice I said plug in.. Bluetooth makes me crazy!! I like control over everything and not being tech savvy means, I would need the help to hook me up... NoT!)

when listening to music, I expect some standard of quality. No sound distortion- residual vibration from base- and results to produce crisp sounding vocals. When this happens I consider it a success…PALOVUE LIGHTENING HEADPHONES was the trifecta of all my requirements- I was pleasantly surprised a basic/minimal plug-in headphone set could bring a decent of quality sound at such a reasonable price. Again- not a connoisseur… don’t hold me to the verbiage that, i wouldn’t know if I tried to review on a more technical level..!!

I realize, I may be the only one that truly believes the greatest invention was the Sony Walkman..??! me/my cassettes back in the 80’s had a beautiful love affair!! (OMG-saving babysitting $ for batteries was my life..!!) Obviously, this headset surpasses that level in comparison.. Yet, I have the same feeling of being in a happy Bliss!!!

I will add, our house boasts 2 pairs of AirPods, a pair of beats, and one Skullcandy high quality lightening platinum headset... I’ve tried them all! I don’t have a complaint about them, other than… OMG- The dang price! Summer jobs, Santa Claus and the likes have been too good to allow my children these luxuries but, that is just what those are LUXURIES!! For my purpose of listening to music at the pool, taking a brisk walk or, traveling with the fam… these are perfect! Best of all- I won’t cry or, die.. IF, something happened and these stopped working or, heaven forbid became lost!

These are simple, straightforward, easy to use from the moment removed from package!! This set is free of needing help to pair with Bluetooth as, you just plug-in to device.. and go- BooM!! These have standard 3 size ear cushions, to help find a good fit. BUT, the added bonus I appreciated was the clip, its super handy... it allows headphones to be attached to ones shirt- alleviating any excess pull or tension on the slack of the wires. Basically, it helps so, weight of the product will not to pull down on itself- making headphones pop out of ears...
These would be a great product for someone younger/older that like things simple.. or, lack text savvy skills and must have simple hook up. I myself struggle with Bluetooth connections and my ego takes a hit asking over and over for help in this department.. so, I relate. (I’m thinking this would be a perfect gift for my grandma- she could connect to her cellphone device -as grandma takes a walk each morning at the ripe old age of 86! This would be a great gift in the future- just plug in connection, and have her Dolly Parton tunes as she heads out on her walk!) This pair of headphones could be compatible for a variety of people..

title: Terrific eReader
text:
I've had my Nook for about 2 weeks and love it. Before I purchased it, I spent weeks researching the differences between the Barnes and Noble Nook and the Kindle and other ereaders. I chose the Nook because I can read .epub format books on it; something you cannot do on the Kindle. The Kindle only supports .pdf files and ebooks in the proprietary Amazon.com format. That severely limits the number and type of ebooks you can read.

With the Nook, I have borrowed free ebooks from my local library and within minutes downloaded them to my computer and then transferred them to my Nook. AWESOME! In addition, unlike the Kindle, I can read free ebooks available from Google.

The only thing I don't like about the Nook and the Kindle is that neither one of them has a back-lit screen so, at night or in the dark, you have to have alternative ample light. So I either turn on a lamp or use the small, clip-on light I bought at the local RiteAid for about $10. It works just fine.

So far, I have had no problems navigating my ebooks; everything works smoothly and the pages turn quickly. I'm enjoying the convenience of being able to travel with 30 books and audio-books at a time. I also have some music loaded on my Nook so I can listed to it while I read. Lastly, I'm glad I bought a case for it because I pretty much take it every place I go so the hard case prevents the screen from getting scratched or broken.

I'm very happy with my purchase.

title: Reading = A+ / Reading a NOOK = A++!!!
text:
My wonderful husband treated me to a Nook (Wi-Fi version - not 3G) for my birthday just one month ago and I haven't put it down since. We spent plenty of time researching and reviewing other e-readers and decided this was our reader of choice - I'm truly happy about the decision. It was user friendly right out of the box, simple to connect wirelessly and quick to charge. There are so many options for loading books on the Nook and one of the selling features for me was that I can take it to any Barnes and Noble store for free in-store downloads and reads. I even love the fact that I'm able to download (check out) digital books from our local library online - what a bonus! I have NOT experienced any trouble with battery longevity or overall durability. I take my Nook everywhere and just toss it in my purse, complete with Nook cover of course. I take it to school (while waiting for the kids!), doctor's appointments and even to church (gotta look up those Bible verses!). My NIV Bible is loaded on the Nook which is wonderful - although it is a bit difficult to navigate through the books/verses in a pinch. So I'd have to say I like my faithful, printed Bible for quick reference, highlighting and notetaking. But, all other reading is done on my Nook. The screen is clear and crisp, bookmarks are easy to use, books and documents are easy to navigate - and many times I'm fighting for control of my Nook with my son (9) who always wants to read it! The only complaint is that the internet connection is a bit slow at times, but who really cares? I've got my laptop to do all that. And any questions I've had on the Nook - I just take it to the store for quick, reliable and friendly service.

Use Nook as your e-reader ... less paper / more knowledge!

"Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body." - Joseph Addison

title: What a disappointment
text:
I bought the simple one-touch Nook e-reader and, although I love e-readers, this has been an exercise in frustration.

While reading a book, the Nook will suddenly freeze up, you can't page forward or backwards AND if you want to try the old reliable 'turn it off then back on trick' you learn that you can turn it off only with much difficulty. Another annnoyance is sometimes when touching the screen to turn the page, a word will be highlighted and will continue to be highlighted until you turn the Nook on & off (if you succed in turning it off); this is NOT to be confused with the normal highlighting feature.

I went to the local B&N store several times and was unable to get help. Once I was told that if you didn't unplug the Nook from the charger immediately after reaching 100% charge, the above problems would occur. Another time, I was told that these complaints were frequent with the One Touch Nook but not the color Nook. I was also discouraged from returning it to B&N customer service...

So, I have chalked the $139 up to 'lessons learned' and have bought an IPad. I just tried to turn off my Nook and, of course, could not get it to power off.

Ann

title: Highly Functional Quality Product. Near perfect!
text:
This keyboard is great. It is comfortable and the keys have nice tactile feedback. Overall I would highly recommend this keyboard to anyone.

I will list a few pros and cons.
Pro:
Highly functional: There are 7 keys with icons for their default function (IE: webcam button, Calendar button) but these can be changed to whatever function you want. Additionally, there are 12 Function keys ( accessed with an Fn Key + F# key) These also can be reassigned to your desired function. This includes; open a web page, keystroke, open an app, open a file or a folder. ( 2 function keys are dedicated to the battery status and eject button and can not be overwritten)

Gamers: Keyboard software permits you to disable a few keys, including the Windows key! (Disable: Caps Lock, Windows Key, Scroll lock, Num lock and Insert)

Sleep Key. Need to step away from your work. There is a dedicated sleep key. One press. (does not wake it up)

It's ergonomic! It is very comfortable to type on this keyboard. It did not however improve my typing speed.

Plug and play. (Note: you must download Logitech's setpoint software for advanced settings) but if you like the keyboard's functions as they are there is no installation required.

1 USB port to rule them all! Logitech Unify USB software allows you to pair up to 6 wireless devices to the USB receiver. Meaning you only have to use 1 USB port if you have other Logitech devices such as a mouse. (Keyboard is also offered in a bundle)

Included wristguard! (non-removable)

Texture. The way things feel is very important to me. The wrist guard has a nice soft leather feel kin to a nice steering wheel cover. The keys have light texturing to them also. The various buttons are a smooth texture. The use of various textures on the keyboard really makes it look premium also.

Media Controls: Play/Pause/Stop/Volume

Cons:

Key sound: The keys have a very plastic clack to them with no clicky. This is obviously not a mechanical keyboard but there is a noticeably hollow, loose, plastic cheap-sounding noise to this keyboard. This is not a deal-breaker. It is quiet enough that it is not disruptive to the office or sleeping partner.

Size: This is not a compact keyboard by any means. The wristguard is not removable. (19x10 inches)

Not backlit: This keyboard obviously is not RGB or backlit but it is worth mentioning. If your intended use is in low light or no light this is not ideal.

Key spacing: As this is designed to be ergonomic and maximize comfort it is clearly designed with intent. However, transitioning from my work dell keyboard with very tight key spacing and the same with my laptop keyboard there is an adjustment required. Since it is designed so that each key is where your fingers naturally rest you will quickly adapt.

text:
Our late 2015 iMac arrived with a compact wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a wireless touch mouse. At times I've wished it had also included a numeric keypad, so was looking forward to adding this one.

This keypad is listed as matching the iMac keyboard, but that's no longer true. It DOES match my old wireless Mac keyboard that ran on AA batteries, but does NOT match the rechargeable keyboard shipped with our late 2015 iMac. It's about twice as high.

But that's minor. What is NOT minor is the almost complete lack of instructions. I was able to follow the one page quick install guide, though it took two tries of installing batteries using a quarter to open and close the battery cap before I was able to get the keypad to switch on (thankfully indicated with a tiny green LED at the top right.) It then showed up on the iMac Bluetooth preference screen. I paired it, and was then asked by my iMac to press the key to the right of the shift key on the keypad (Z). THERE IS NO SUCH KEY! After trying many of the keys that ARE on the keypad, the installer eventually gave up and let me manually specify that it is a US keyboard, though I was never offered an option for a numeric keypad.

Once paired, the keys generally work, though it missed the first keypress after a while of non-use. That could be a deal-killer in heavy data entry, where accuracy is crucial.

Most of the keys make sense, though there is no indication of the purpose of the F13, F14, F15 and F16 keys. Presumably they are programmable, and as delivered, F15 brightens the screen and F14 darkens it. But would it have killed the vendor to use the mostly-blank back of the one page of instructions to explain this?

Overall, I'm disappointed, but will Google for instructions on using and/or reprogramming the other two function keys, and continue trying to use this numeric keypad. As Amazon's star guide indicates, 3 stars means "It's OK".

title: great 1990's throwback keyboard for system builders
text:
It's 2016, you say. And here you are, on Amazon, looking at keyboards. Why in the world would I buy a PS/2 keyboard? PS/2 was introduced nearly 30 years ago (1987!), and the currently reality is that not a single laptop in the market supports this input, and even desktops are starting to phase them out. Well, as sexy and shiny USB is, the geek in all of us seem to still prefer PS/2 when it comes to debugging system builds.

Frantically hitting DEL, F8, F9, or whatever cryptic combination of keys to get into the BIOS is a well known thing. Turns out, when motherboards are on the fritz, the USB controllers sometimes stop responding, leaving PS/2 as the only way to get access to the BIOS. That alone makes this keyboard worth it's weight in gold, because as far as I can tell, it's the ONLY new PS/2 keyboard available on the market. I went to Fry's, and the kid working there replies, "wrong century dude." Thanks man, cause I didn't feel old enough already.

The keyboard is light, but well built, and feels very solid. The key actuations are a bit mushy, and feel very 90's. Which is not surprising, since this keyboard feels like it rolled right off a 1990's assembly line - all it's missing is the beige plastics to give it that authentic feel. The NUM lock and SCROLL lock LEDs are nice and bright, which means you can't miss them. Most importantly, the DEL, ENTER, and arrow keys work great - a must have for mucking with the BIOS.

TL;DR, a really great throwback keyboard for a ridiculously great price. More importantly, every system builder should have one of these in their closet, for the typical once a year usage. I'm sure if you trolled one of those surplus warehouses you could find a used PS/2 keyboards caked in who knows what, but why bother when you can get one brand new?

title: Product not as Shown
text:
This keyboard has two things working immediately against it. The first is that Amazon has the wrong image for this product. This keyboard is small and square, very ordinary without the extra buttons and ergo support shown in the image provided. The second is this line: Ideal for use with your PC or PS/2, which implies this keyboard, might offer USB support... which it does not. This keyboard only has a PS/2 connection available. This really isn't an issue for desktops, but notebook users will have to know this is PS/2 use only and be prepared with an adapter.

Like other reviewers, I was a little disappointed that the product I received was not the product shown and it was not USB. Now some people might think it's obvious this is a PS/2, but the problem is the line kind of implies it is a USB keyboard with a PS/2 adapter. USB to PS/2 adapters are cheap and easy to come by with pretty solid results. PS/2 to USB are not as cheap, can cost up to 30 dollars if you don't do your homework and search the web and the results may vary because of the processor required. I am using this keyboard with a Tripp-Lite 8015-000 that cost a heck of a lot less than 30 dollars, and it works well with this keyboard. The only thing I noticed as far as the adapter goes is the use of the keyboard does not keep me from going idle in some messenger programs, a minor issue I assure.

Now onto the keyboard, this keyboard is compact so it will take up very little space which is why it is so ideal to have alongside a notebook. Naturally my desktop use was no problem at all either, but I have fuller keyboards with more robust offerings for that. I found the length of the cord to be pretty good. The keys have a textured feel to them that some like, my Sidewinder board is smooth for example. The resistance of the keys is also pleasing, and feels a lot better than the flat keys of many notebooks or the cheap feel of some no-name brands I have used. It's very light making it mobile and has a couple of feet at the back to make it more dynamic. I would still use a wrist rest however. The backspace key is a little on the small side but it's not too bad or as small as some of those backspace keys that only show an arrow which I hate. They've shortened the spacebar a bit but it's barely noticeable.

Overall, I like the keyboard and would recommend to anyone who wants no frills, compact keyboard for their desktop without hesitation. I also wouldn't mind hauling this around with me should I want something mobile for the notebook (with adapter) or taking to other people's houses when I troubleshoot some of their PC issues. (I've encountered some unpleasant keyboards in the past).

title: The little keyboard that could!
text:
Pros:
-Blue-ish LED's with 6 built in modes
-Brown switches for a pleasently tactile typing experience
-Compact design that can fit literally anywhere.

Cons (more of preference)
- Wish it had a metal backplate but for $26, I mean this is really as good as it gets.
- Layout is pretty standard but it might take some getting used to.
- Wish the backlighting was a bit brighter.

This was arguably the best $26 I've ever spent on a peripheral. I was looking for a TKL keyboard as an alternative for my Corsair K70 since it was so huge and this pretty much had everything I wanted. Like another reviewer had mentioned the LED's on this board are more of a teal/turquoise over a bluish-white, which I was completely okay with since I have a blue themed build. Coming from my Cherry MX Reds, these Outemu browns definitely feel different, but not in a bad way. They're more silent than the red's and in my opinion feel a little more tactile without actually announcing it to the world through excessive click-clacking. The cons aren't so much cons, more of personal preference, I liked the size and look of this keyboard but it seemed pretty boring in terms of looks, which I fixed by changing out the keys to the red keys off my K70 (see pics). I was surprised to see that this little guy had a braided cable, it's not the most rugged thing out there but it's definitely nice to see on a budget board like this. All in all if you're looking for Brown switches, a 75% board with the look of a 60, and blue LED's without forking over an extra $15 for RGB's, then this is for you!

title: UPDATED: All-in-all, a great pseudo (non-Cherry) MX Brown mechanical non-numpad keyboard experience, all minor Cons considered
text:
UPDATE:
Addition of a personally subjective Con:
- The key surfaces are not quite gritty/grippy enough; a hair too much slip and slide for my taste, but not noticeable enough.

Removal of an originally posted Con:
" - Also I was a little bummed that while there are 6 low budget modes of backlighting, there does not seem to exist an "off" setting - the backlighting is always on in some manner until the keyboard loses power. I currently have it set to "breathing" because it's the least distracting of the modes and most frequently produces the closest "off" moments."

This removal is because that function does actually exhist, and it is by pressing Fn+Down Arrow until the backlight is off. I've found that the 3 brightness levels should be considered in a range of 0, 1, 2; where 0 is Off, 1 is Low, 2 is High. As already quoted, my original review gave a Con for a lack of such a backlight-off setting.

Due to these new considerations I have changed my rating score from 4 to 5, as I felt that the remaining Cons (including the new Con mentioned) weren't enough to keep from giving a 5. I also changed the title to read "great" instead of the original "very good" qualification.

- - - ORIGINAL - - -
Very good product for the price. I was looking for a good small mechanical keyboard for gaming that would allow me to regain real estate on my desk for more mouse movement versatility. While that end has successfully been achieved at an affordable price, there are a few Cons that kept this from a 5-star rating in my book.

Cons:
- A little more wobble in a few of the keys than I would prefer, but nothing too disappointing.
- I would have liked, at the very least, a no-frills height adjustment of some sort, even just a pair of small single-setting legs. Instead the keyboard base is just ever-so-slightly angled.

All-in-all, a very good pseudo (non-Cherry) MX Brown mechanical non-numpad keyboard experience.

title: Otemu Brown Switches For a Decent Price and Keys Can Be Swapped
text:
My overall score is between a 3 and a 4. If there was a 3.5 then that's what I would rate it. The first reason why it didn't earn a higher score is due to an issue with the first keyboard I received. I took it out of the box and realized it was a used / returned keyboard. Someone stuck wide Velcro strips to the bottom of the keyboard. The USB cable was also unwound. This is a result of poor quality control when receiving a returned item and just putting it back on the shelf. I hope no customer receives that keyboard labeled as "New".

These are Otemu brown MX switches and I chose these since I don't really like the clickity clack of keys. The prior keyboard I used were Cherry MX reds which felt real nice with every press. Very smooth. These browns are stiffer and require more pressure to push / press but they are quiet. I guess it will take some time to get used to them.

Size of the keyboard is very compact which is what I wanted after coming from a full size keyboard. This is a huge plus. Losing the number pad is a negative but it's balanced by having a very compact sized keyboard. There is no Prnt Scrn button. This may not be a huge deal for some but others will find it somewhat annoying (like myself). There are Fn keys at the top. The ones like for volume, keyboard brightness, Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, and Insert are okay to keep but the music set (there are four) could be removed. I don't know of anyone who uses the music function buttons on their keyboard to control their music player. One of these could have been swapped for the Prnt Scrn.

The cable has a great length to it and it's braided which is a plus.

The keyboard cannot be adjusted but I feel it's a decent height (at least for me). It's not completely flat and it's not too high. There are rubber pads at the bottom to help it grip to a surface.

Finally, a huge plus for this keyboard is having the ability to swap out keys to customize them to your liking. I was able to get a couple of different PBT key cap sets from eBay for less than $10 each. They're shipped from China but it only took 2-3 weeks for them to arrive. Worth it for the price. Swapping keys is a breeze. Funny thing is how the orange key caps make the LED lights look white.

I got this keyboard as part of the Lightning Deal which makes it worthy purchase but at its regular price I would consider maybe saving up a little bit more for something with a higher quality build.

title: Nailed it
text:
Zero actual complaints. Lighting options are great, brightness has 5 steps but you can adjust RGB color to make it darker, so full spectrum effectively. No light bleed from underneath keycaps if you're on lower brightness levels. Letters are perfect, easy to see. Feels solid, pretty heavy.

This is one of the only keyboard on Amazon with Brown switches, and I believe the only RGB one, at this price range. Blue is so common but the Browns are either non-existent or way more expensive (like 35 vs 55). At least when I was buying this. I just previously got a different one that I had enough of and I'm happy to say this is a step up (albeit I can't speak to their RGB so I'm not comparing apples to apples).

Oh and it has a braided cord and USB cap/cover - nice touch if you're carrying yours around. The spare switches are also considerate. Instructions are more of a cheat-sheet, and I don't see a reason for anything different, but I did have to deduce some things (the questions on this product page are helpful). I'm sure they will respond if you ask them.

To change solid color: you want [FN]+[Ins/M1] a few times to get solid. Then [Fn]+[=/RGB] to get the keayboard to light up rainbow. Now press the key that has the color you want. Or just install the software; it's a tiny footprint and you can pick from a color wheel.

OK now for the nitpicky stuff:
-The number row's letters are more faint than the rest of the keyboard. The symbols especially. I kind of like it because it makes the letters stand out more. I'd rather too dim than too bright. But at any rate it's not that bad.
-The spacebar. It clicks like a Blue. I checked and it's a Brown. But it clicks. I think it's from the support-"switches" on either end of the bar, jiggling. I'm gonna try a rubber O ring. The Right shift, and less so Enter, has the same issue - all of those keys have the supports. It's worst on the spacebar though.
-Slight cosmetic thing: Under those support-"switches" for the spacebar are 2 pieces of metal... wire? Like a thin metal coat hangar. They're supports for the plastic things that look like caps but aren't. So you've got this deep black keyboard with alien spaceship-like lighting, and then there are these 2 pieces of shiny bare metal that you can see. Kinda ruins the shot. To put this into perspective, though, you're seeing about 1/8" of each. This is the nitpicky section, after all.

OK that's it. Good product for an awesome price (~$40). I'll update regarding clicky spacebar and O-rings, if I remember.

title: Went from Drevo to this...
text:
Best thing I ever did tbh. I was using the compact Drevo keyboard which had a few issues of its own. The compact design was done in a way that didn't allow easy cleaning AND the software for easy RBG light management didn't work 100% as it should have. Not to mention it was more expensive and had less features... And due to the harder cleaning the keys needed to be smashed/wiggled a bit to be coerced into working.

So this one is 20 bucks cheaper, has a 100% working software program, and you can even change the polling rates. The keys are properly spaced for proper cleaning and it comes with back-up switches for when your most used keys (usually ASDW sfor gamers) start to wear as mechanical keys often do. It's small enough and has all the proper keys for media and gaming without smashing them all too close together. A very attractive and well-thought out keyboard. As for the switches, I got red. They work just as well as the Drevo brand and seem to be just a bit quieter (especially the space bar/bigger keys). As for the lights, they seem to be a bit brighter than Drevo's keyboard and have more options for the lights, but solid standard blue at 75% brightness is good enough for me.

If you're upgrading from a membrane keyboard (you want red switches btw) or looking for a moderately priced mechanical keyboard, then look no further. This thing has all you need... Except a wrist rest. But hey, you can't expect them to sell a 80to100-dollar-type of keyboard for half the price AND expect a wrist rest, now can you? lmao

title: Amazing gaming & multitasking keyboard – improved my gaming and my everyday typing.
text:
I purchased this keyboard to go with my first custom-built gaming rig that I built around 2 months ago. I had been getting so frustrated with my old standard Logitech keyboard and I wanted an upgrade. I am not new to gaming, but this was my first ‘serious’ build, so I went with the advice of many of my more experienced friends and purchased a mechanical keyboard.

I needed a keyboard that could multitask as well. I work as a web developer, and I am in grad school for marketing – I do a lot of typing. So I wanted something that was going to last and perform in all of these uses – and still improve my gaming experience. After doing a TINY bit of keyboard research, I chose the blue switches since I do a lot more “regular typing” than gaming.

I’ve had the keyboard for about 2 days, and in that time I’ve used it to play the DOOM Multiplayer Beta, and several hours of Fallout 4. So far this morning I’ve written 2 blog posts, one paper, and now this review :D.

My first impression of this product was it was HEAVY. Not in a bad way, just in a very sturdy was that was a sharp contrast to what I had had before in my standard keyboard. Since this is a desktop keyboard, there’s no need for this keyboard to be light. The other thing I noticed was the high quality braided USB cable. I must’ve missed that feature when I ordered because I was pleasantly surprised – the USB connector is also gold plated. I did not expect that for such a low price point of around $100. (Note: I did receive a discount on the product in exchange for my honest review.)

I also received this keyboard exceptionally fast. I ordered on a Thursday afternoon and got it Saturday morning – no Saturday delivery fee!

**Important** So the package comes with a guide that is very concise – pay attention! I got confused when I didn’t get a ‘new hardware found’ notification like the manual said. However, the rest of the instructions worked fine, so it must not have mattered. I’m on Windows 10.

I was surprised to find that the shortcut keys (like for volume and track control) worked without any software at all. To access the different light settings, you just press FN and select the pattern from the keyboard itself. I settled on FN+0 – It’s a responsive setting that lights up the keys you type and then lets them fade – very cool since I don’t want to have the keyboard lit all the time. I’ll admit though – this thing is pretty, when I leave my desk I’ve been quickly pressing FN+Ins to get it to do the wave effect if I’m gonna be away for a while.

So that’s just the extra stuff – let’s talk about the performance. I can without a doubt say this keyboard has made a difference in my playing. The game mode is essential – make sure you enable that when you launch a game. The DOOM multiplayer beta was probably a bad gauge since that game is ridiculously hard anyway – but I noticed a marked difference in my performance on Fallout 4. I’m not going to pretend to be a keyboard expert, all I can say is that the response time was way better.

And I am SO glad I went with blue switches. Writing papers, I feel like an old world typist – the mechanical and audible feedback I get from typing is so satisfying. I have noticed reduced typos from ‘accidental’ slips. The audible click sound doesn’t really sound like the bulky old keyboards, it’s more of a quick, clean clicking. It isn’t loud, but it’s NOT whisper quiet, which I prefer.

Pros:
- The rubber feet keep it in place on my desk (I am one of those crazy people who don’t use a slide-out keyboard tray).
- The keyboard is study, and well made. A great value for the money.
- No special software needed to change effects and settings, everything is controlled on the keyboard, and the instructions are only 1 page.
- The game features are useful! Locking the windows key, consecutive attack mode.
- Custom patterns – this is essential when gaming. I used it to highlight the keys used when playing.
- Excellent physical and audible feedback when typing – extremely satisfying.
- The confidence that comes with the 50 million actuation lifecycle (I type a LOT)

Cons:
- There weren’t any instructions on what to do if you never got the ‘new hardware found’ message when plugging in the keyboard. This confused me ' but I figured it out. If this happens to you – just proceed with the manual, as far as I can tell, it makes no difference.
- As far as I can tell, you can’t make ALL the keys light up one color. I might be overlooking something though. This might be a con for some.

I would say this keyboard is perfect for someone like me who wants a serious gaming keyboard, but is ultimately a multitasker. You will definitely notice a difference if switching from a non-mechanical keyboard.
The quality of this keyboard has me anxious to try other GAMDIAS products, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for an upgrade!

title: Customer Service
text:
Since it is so easy to buy almost anything on Amazon, I want to discuss customer service. Not Amazon customer service which I have always found to be excellent. No, I want to write about my experience with Macally. I bought this keyboard in November 2020. It worked fairly well well except for the Caps lock light which I didn't care about at the time.

In September of 2021 the keyboard got really finicky, dropping the first letter of a sentence when I was typing and it began to start getting really weird. Finally it literally stopped working -- I mean my Mac Pro wouldn't even recognize it in the system preferences.

I checked it out with another computer and realized that it must be broken. WHAT TO DO. At first I thought of calling Amazon but I realized they usually only allow returns for 30 days. I decided to look up Macally's customer service phone number because I noticed that the keyboard had a 1 year warranty.

I called them and actually got a real person who listened to my concerns and immediately transferred me to their returns dept. After leaving a message and not getting a return call, I called once again. this time I got the returns dept. and spoke to their customer service rep. She asked for my email address after I explained the situation and within moments I got a link to a short questionnaire. I filled out the info asking for the model number, serial number, where I purchased it, etc.

Within 2 days I got a package with a new model. It was quick and easy -- that's what customer service should be like. Quick and Easy. Bottom line, I will buy many of my Mac accessories from Macally from now on.

This review is not about Filco, it is about Cherry MX blue switches.

There is something wrong with the blue Cherry MX switches on these keyboards. The first one I bought, had "dead" sounding keys. In other words, you could press the "A" key - nice crisp click. "S" nice crisp click. "D" dull click barely even audible. "F" crisp click. "G" no click what so ever, and so on. I would say that on the first one I got about 10% of the keys were not clicking consistently.

So, I returned it, and got another. Same problem. Inconsistent clicking sounds from the keys that felt "mushy" to the touch. I have seen on MULTIPLE websites that this a major complaint with recent purchasers of keyboards that have Cherry MX blue switches. Keep in mind, I have an older Cooler Master with cherry blues on it, and every single switch clicks just like the next one. Not one problem with a single switch on the entire keyboard.

I love Filco keyboards. I have one with brown switches that are flawless. I also have one with red switches that types like a dream. Maybe it's just me, I am a bit of a mechanical keyboard freak. Some people collect baseball cards, I collect mechanical keyboards. Maybe this wouldn't even bother a "normal" person just buying a "nice" keyboard. But if these flaws would bother you as well, buy it, test each key, and if you have the same results I do, just return it and go for a brown, or red switch.

title: Beware of the Shape of the RETURN Key -- ISO vs ANSI
text:
I really like this keyboard, generally. Easy to see, quiet, nice touch, nice throw length for each keypress.

But, specifically, I simply cannot use it because of the shape of the return key.

For years I have typed using a horizontally-shaped return key the ANSI standard.

This keyboard is an ISO standard, and has a vertical return key, with the backslash key next to it, right where my pinky has been hitting the return key for...well, forever.

I literally popped the backslash key off the keyboard because I was hitting it so often. I may glue a plastic extension onto the return key to make it wider and just lose the backslash key. Or buy an ANSI keyboard.

Bottom line: when choosing a keyboard, be aware of the Return key's shape. Turns out I want an ANSI, not an ISO.

title: Great keyboard!!! 4+ years now
text:
I just thought I'd chime in and let you all get a review from me. I did not order from Amazon but from MechanicalKeyboards(dot)com. I believe I've had my Ducky keyboard now around 4 or 5 years. In the past I have used full-sized keyboards from Corsair and Logitech. The other day I pulled those full-sized keyboards out and they feel like tanks on my desk now.

The Ducky has been very reliable and is a joy to type on. The smaller size is something I enjoy as well. The silent cherry red keys I got are not completely quiet but I've never used them and been annoyed at all. My Corsair Strafe has Cherry Browns which are much more "clanky" than the Ducky is.

One of the adjustment things you'll have to deal with are the loss of the numpad, function keys, arrow keys, etc... but fear not you actually still have them but you need to hold the "Fn" key before pressing for example the number 1 for F1 (Fn+1)... or Fn+J for left arrow. In 99% of cases I never need to use Arrow keys. If you're a gamer you're using WSAD anyways. I can't remember the game but once it had unmappable arrow key controls I actually just used my Xbox controller instead of dealing with that.

You'll learn to memorize these Fn combos. The most often used one I use is Fn+] which is the PrintSc key. I used this when taking screenshots using SnagIt.

Overall this is a great minimalist keyboard with great RGB lighting.

title: Great extras but not a good typing experience
text:
I'm yet another Natural Elite fan saddened by the fact that Microsoft no longer makes it. If they started making it again and added some of the features this one has, I'd buy a lifetime supply.

I had this for about a week and really, really wanted to keep it. Having a dedicated calculator key was great, but even more useful were the page back and forward buttons and the toggle switch to change magnification. That toggle made my life much easier at work; I wish every keyboard had it.

I didn't use the riser for the front of the keyboard, though I would have used it more had I kept it just to see if it made typing more comfortable. The padded wrist rest was nice, and the keyboard itself was easy to clean. And although I don't care much about aesthetics, my colleagues all commented positively on the keyboard's appearance.

Unfortunately, the negatives outweighed all of that. The biggest problem was that the typing experience just wasn't that good. I've been using a split keyboard for years -- a Natural Elite, as it happens -- but having the center keys be larger than regular keys threw me off. Maybe it shouldn't matter, but it slowed me down and was very frustrating. Also, as noted by others, it is loud. My office has rather close quarters and everyone hears some noise from others, but my keyboard was far louder than other keyboards. Nobody complained, but I was bothered by the idea that I might be bothering others.

Then there were the customizable hotkeys that never worked. I would seem to have them set one day, but they wouldn't work the next, and searching for help online didn't yield any useful advice.

And then there was the fact that it came without instructions, not even so much as a slip of paper directing users to a web page for more info. That's absurd. Even the cheapest electronic items I've purchased have had a manual of sorts, either printed or online. It makes me wonder whether I got a legitimate product, a knockoff, or a refurbished model.

After returning this one, I got a Perixx Periboard-512. It's not a sexy looking and it doesn't come with the awesome extras that the 4000 has, but it's a smooth typing experience and I can type a report without everyone on my floor hearing me bang each letter. Ideally, Microsoft will someday resurrect the Natural Elite and add those oh-so-useful extras, but this is okay for now.

title: AWESOME
text:
I've always heard that an ergonomic keyboard was much better for you, so finlly I decided to bite the bullet and buy it. At first I hated it. I went from typing 60 words per minute down to 40, no joke. But, as time marchs on I love this thing. It is now easier for me to use the ergonomic keyboard rather than the old kind. I've also noticed that my shoulders don't hurt at the end of a long typing day either.
Please remember this, if you decide to buy it, give yourself about 1-2 weeks to adjust.

title: Good keyboard but it takes time to adjust.
text:
I had a prior version of this keyboard (the Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 3000) for my office PC. It did admirably, but after a year or so, my wrists were starting to hurt IN SPITE OF the ergonomics helping. This one is better rated. So far, it has helped, but it took at least a week of use just for my hands to BEGIN to get used to the differences. I'd do a pro/con list, but I'm not sure there are any "cons" as compared to "issues to expect" if you buy this keyboard.

1. Expect a steep learning curve to get used to the layout. The "bend" in this keyboard is significant, and it will take time for your fingers to get used to hitting the right keys on a consistent basis. Give it one or two weeks of regular use before deciding if you like it or not. You can't know in a couple of days if it's helping you because you do need to re-learn your hand placement and fingering to some degree.

2. There is a physical break in the left and right hand keys. This "no man's land" means you need to unlearn using the wrong hand for the wrong keys because you will either miskey or just hit nothing when you go to use your right hand to it the G key (or a similar situation). Likewise, some of the keys have an odd shape that takes getting used to. I had considerable issue getting used to hitting V and B correctly. Again, this is all about relearning how to keyboard properly. My best tip is to avoid looking at the keyboard while typing. For me, looking at the keyboard made it harder compared to just backspacing and repeating until I got it right. Passwords are about the only thing where I still watch what keys I strike.

3. This keyboard is wider and "taller" than most. If you use a keyboard tray, clearing it might pose and issue (see next point below). You will likely have less room for your mouse as well, but I found it something I could live with.

4. The keyboard has three (maybe four) resting positions. There's a removable front skirt that elevates the front. There are the standard rear folding supports to elevate the rear. So, that's resting flat (none), rear elevated, front elevated, and both elevated. Lying flat, the keyboard works fine with my keyboard tray. Set the way I find it's most comfortable for me, I can only push the tray in halfway before the keyboard hits the desk. This isn't a deal breaker for me, so I'll live with it. You keyboard tray may need to allow at least 3 inches of vertical clearance to not have an issue with this keyboard.

I was divided on four or five stars, but since I need this more extreme curve to deal with wrist pain, it's not the product's fault, so I won't hold the awkwardness of it against the designers. It does what it's designed to do for a good reason. That comes with a trade off.

title: The case of the disappearing letters...
text: I really like this keyboard due to its comfort.  However, I am very disappointed that the key paint disappears too quickly.  I've got no "A", "S", "D", or "C" and only a partial "E", "R", and "V".  The keys still work.  The letters have gone incognito.  Even after buying a new keyboard (I bought the same one again as I like the comfort and feel) the letters started disappearing within a couple of months.  I'd sure like to see some proactive action on behalf of Microsoft to reach out and replace the keys with new ones that are painted to last a few years as opposed to a few weeks.
